subtitle.text: It was Ben's first day of school at Monster Academy.
He floated into the auditorium for the first-day assembly.
Inside, he saw some other ghosts, along with a crowd of goblins, zombies, and other monsters.
Everyone was talking loudly.
"Ben, over here!"
Ben easily spotted the giant who was waving to him. Ben shot over to her.
"I'm glad you're here, Gaby," said Ben as he sat down next to her.
"You're the only one I know in—"
Crash!
Ben stopped talking. So did all the other monsters around him.
A two-headed monster looked up at the ceiling.
"What made that sound?" asked one of her heads.
"I don't know," answered her other head.
"It sounded like a giant landed on the roof of the school," said a goblin.
"Maybe it's my mom," Gaby whispered to Ben with a giggle.
Ben grinned. Gaby's mom was a giant, just like Gaby.
But Ben was pretty sure she wasn't on the roof of the school.
Mr. Freaky, the school principal, rushed onto the stage.
He was tall and thin, and he had three noses.
"Monsters, please be seated! Everything is totally under control!"
"Mr. Freaky loves to say that everything is under control," Gaby whispered.
"But what he really means is that everything is totally out of control!"
Ben laughed. It was lucky that his family had moved next door to Gaby over the summer.
Gaby had told Ben nearly everything he needed to know about Monster Academy.
"All the students and teachers are monsters, just like us," she had explained.
"The principal is pretty nice—as long as you don't get in trouble.
The office ogre is friendly too, unless she gets really busy.
After all, she only has four arms!"
Ben looked around the crowded auditorium again.
Most of the students were still talking.
A few ghosts in the last row were batting around a ball of paper.
Mr. Freaky clapped his hands for silence.
"Please don't worry about the loud crash. I'm sure it was just another broom."
A murmur went through the crowd.
"What is Mr. Freaky talking about?" asked a troll.
"We've had a few . . . incidents involving flying brooms this morning," Mr. Freaky went on.
"But let's forget about that for now.
Your eighth-grade class president, Waldo Wizz, would like to say a few words."
Monsters whistled and shouted as a young wizard approached the microphone.
Gaby's eyes lit up. "Waldo's amazing," she gushed.
"He's so cute. Plus, he's super smart, and he can do all kinds of magic."
Waldo waved to the crowd.
"This is going to be a fabulous school year," he began.
"We have two new after-school clubs—marching band and spell casting—and the first dance is coming up soon.
The Monster Mash dance will be held in a few weeks. So don't forget to show your best school spirit and participate in all our great activities!"
The crowd cheered again.
Waldo handed the microphone to Mr. Freaky.
"Settle down, students," said Mr. Freaky.
"Before you go to class, I have some news about People Place.
There's a new mayor."
"People Place is creepy," murmured a skeleton.
In the next row, a four-eyed monster leaned toward a three-eyed monster.
"I heard the new mayor is really scary looking. He only has two eyes!"
"Eww, gross!" replied the three-eyed monster.
Ben knew that Monsterville was next to a town inhabited by people.
A huge wooden fence separated the two towns.
His parents had warned him and his brother, Sid, to stay away from that fence.
But he didn't know anything about the mayor.
Mr. Freaky was still talking.
"I've been told that Mayor Hubbletree doesn't like monsters. So we must be extra careful not to upset him.
Remember—Monster Academy was built on land owned by People Place.
If we scare the people, they could force us to leave our school."
The two-headed monster raised her hand.
"I was near People Place last week," said one head.
"A human kid saw me and screamed!"
"I wasn't even doing anything!" said the other head.
Mr. Freaky nodded. "Unfortunately, some people get scared just looking at monsters.
Now, please exit quietly, monsters, and enjoy your first day of school.
It's going to be a wonderful school year!"
Ben and Gaby exchanged looks.
"And everything is totally under total control!" they said at the same time, laughing.
They headed out of the auditorium.
Ben thought it was fun to kid around with Gaby, and so far Monster Academy seemed really cool.
But he had to admit that a few things were worrying him.
The principal seemed nervous, and empty brooms were crashing around the school.
Plus, People Place had a new mayor—one who didn't like monsters!
Ben paused in the hallway to check his class schedule.
His first class was Cooking in room 103.
"Cooking class?" thought Ben. "I don't want to learn to cook!"
Around him lockers slammed and feet thudded as other monsters hurried to their classes.
"How does my eye makeup look?" Ben heard a purple monster ask a goblin.
"My mom says I put way too much on."
"It looks great," answered the goblin.
"But you missed your fourth eye completely."
Ben sighed and floated down the hall and into room 103.
He saw a zombie sitting alone at a table.
"Hi," said Ben. "Can I sit here?"
The zombie stared silently at Ben.
Ben felt uncomfortable. "Maybe he doesn't like me," he thought.
There hadn't been any zombies at his old school—mostly just other ghosts.
A witch sat down at the table. Ben recognized her from his homeroom.
She had flowing black hair and was dressed all in black.
Even her fingernails were painted black.
The witch smiled at Ben.
"Zombies just like to stare. It doesn't mean he doesn't like you."
"What?" Ben thought, startled. "How did she know what I was thinking?"
The witch laughed.
"I can't always tell what others are thinking, but sometimes I can. Have a seat."
"Uh-oh," Ben thought, sitting down.
He was going to have to watch his thoughts when this witch was around.
Ben sneaked another look at the witch.
Her eyes were green and flecked with gold.
She was the most beautiful witch he'd ever seen.
Just then a huge monster with two sharp horns stalked over to the table.
"Move over!" he growled at Ben. "I sit next to Winnie!"
"Chill out, Mog," said the witch, spreading her fingers to admire her nail polish.
Mog ignored her. He moved his face so close to Ben's that their noses nearly touched.
"Did you hear me?" said Mog. "I said, move over!"
The room was suddenly quiet. All the other monsters were looking at Ben.
Ben puffed out his chest, trying not to look scared.
"I heard you," he said. "But I'm not moving."
He glanced at Winnie, who was watching him with a surprised look.
Mog glared at Ben for a few moments.
Finally the big monster grunted and sat down on the other side of Winnie, at the end of the table.
To Ben's surprise, a ghoul sitting at the next table gave Ben the "claws-up" sign.
A moment later an old witch hobbled into the room.
She wore a crooked purple hat and orange sunglasses.
On her chin was a huge mole.
"She used to be the broom-flying teacher," Winnie whispered.
"My sister had her last year. She was terrible at flying brooms, though.
So now a new teacher, Miss Bungle, teaches it."
"Good morning, monsters," said the teacher.
"My name is Mrs. Hag, and I will be your cooking teacher."
Mog groaned.
"Excuse me!" said Mrs. Hag, fixing her eyes on Mog.
"Did you have something to say?"
"Yeah," said Mog. "I hate cooking."
"We actually have something in common," thought Ben.
Mrs. Hag grinned, revealing a row of brown, rotted teeth.
"Well then, Mog, perhaps you'll prefer cleaning.
That will be your job at the end of class."
Mog scowled, and Ben tried not to laugh.
After Mrs. Hag took attendance, she opened an enormous cookbook.
"For our first cooking lesson, we will make Slimy Toad Stew."
"Yum!" said the ghoul, smacking his lips.
"First we need to gather the ingredients." Mrs. Hag read from the cookbook.
"Let's see . . . Six rotten eggs, four dried worms, one ounce of bat claws.
Oh, I just bought some bat claws yesterday."
She felt in her pocket. "I thought I had them with me."
Mrs. Hag searched her other pockets, but she couldn't find the bat claws anywhere.
"Oh, well. I must have dropped them somewhere," she muttered to herself.
Mrs. Hag opened a cabinet and peeked inside. "What else can we use?
Aha! These thorns will probably work just as well as bat claws."
The teacher pulled a small bag from the cabinet.
"It says here that these are very special thorns," said Mrs. Hag as she examined the bag.
"They're from a bush that was grown by the light of the full moon."
"I'm not sure she knows what she's doing," Winnie murmured.
By now some of the monsters in class were starting to doze off.
Ben thought he heard the zombie snoring, but the zombie's eyes were still open. Ben looked at Winnie.
Winnie shrugged. "I don't know either.
He might be sleeping, or he might be awake. It's hard to tell with zombies."
Ben was about to respond when suddenly his stool flew out from under him and across the room!
Ben looked at his stool in surprise. It was halfway across the room.
Ben, however, was floating exactly where he'd been.
Mog lay sprawled on the floor. "He tried to knock me over!" Ben realized.
"Mog!" cried Mrs. Hag. "What are you doing?"
The monster got up off the floor. "I was, um, trying to get my stool back."
He pointed to the stool he had knocked across the room.
"That's not your stool," said Mrs. Hag.
"That's Ben's stool. Now sit down and behave yourself!"
Mog sat down as Ben got the stool.
When Ben came back, Mog leaned over the table, scowling at him.
"Listen, you pathetic excuse for a monster," Mog whispered.
"Stay away from Winnie, or you'll end up all alone, haunting a ghost town!"
"Oh, Mog," said Winnie. "He wouldn't be alone in a ghost town.
Those places are filled with ghosts." She flashed a smile at Ben.
"Grr," snarled Mog, still glaring at Ben.
"He's a really nice guy," Winnie whispered to Ben.
"He's just not showing it today."
Mrs. Hag clapped her hands. "Let's start cooking!
Mog, get out the soap and scrub brush so you're ready to clean up when we're done."
Ben watched Mog get up. Ben had stood up to Mog earlier.
But he was new at school, and he couldn't afford to make enemies.
He'd better stay out of Mog's way for now.
Then he stole another quick look at Winnie, hoping she hadn't read his thoughts again.
Maybe he'd better stay out of her way too.
At lunch Gaby told Ben more about the dance that Waldo had mentioned.
And over the next few days, that's all anyone was talking about at Monster Academy.
Who was going with whom to the Monster Mash dance?
Which girl monsters had asked boy monsters?
Why did the girl mummies always spend the evening giggling and running to the restroom to rewrap their bandages?
Ben wanted to go to the dance.
He had already met a bunch of girl monsters at Monster Academy.
But there was only one he really liked—and she was taken.
A few days later during homeroom, Mr. Freaky made an announcement.
"Attention, monsters!" His voice crackled over the loudspeaker.
"As you know, we've been having some strange problems with our brooms since school started.
We've found brooms everywhere—the restrooms, the gym, the soccer field.
Just yesterday one crashed through my office window!"
"We're not sure who's causing the empty brooms to fly around, but we will find the monster responsible.
In the meantime, because of the danger, we're canceling all extracurricular activities.
That includes the Monster Mash dance."
"What?"
"That's not fair!"
Everyone in Ben's homeroom started complaining.
"Furthermore," continued Mr. Freaky, "all broom-flying classes will be suspended until the broom incidents stop."
"No broom-flying class?" shrieked a witch sitting next to Winnie. "That stinks!"
"You're not kidding." Winnie looked like she might cry.
"My parents promised to get me my own broom as soon as I got my broom-flying license." She sighed.
"I'll be an ugly old witch before I can fly a broom by myself."
"You could never be an ugly old witch," thought Ben as he gazed over at Winnie.
Winnie suddenly looked up, and her green eyes stared right into his.
Ben looked away quickly.
The bell rang, and all the students headed off to class.
As Ben drifted down the hallway, he thought about the sad look on Winnie's face again.
Poor Winnie. She'd looked so disappointed.
Suddenly Ben got a brilliant idea.
"I'll figure out who's crashing the brooms!" he thought.
"Then Winnie can go back to broom-flying class and get her own broom."
He was new at Monster Academy, but he could find the mysterious broom-flyer and help Winnie.
He knew he could.
Later Ben heard a voice behind him in the cafeteria.
It was Gaby. He turned to look up at her.
"Guess what?" she cried, jumping up and down. The entire cafeteria shook.
"Hey, quit jumping!" complained a goblin at the next table.
"You spilled my toad juice!"
"What is it? Tell me!" said Ben.
Gaby stopped jumping. "Waldo Wizz asked me to go see a movie on Friday night!" she said.
"That's fantastic!" said Ben.
"Waldo is so nice," Gaby gushed.
"He's cute too. Have I told you about how great he is at magic?"
"Yes." Ben rolled his eyes.
Gaby had told him about Waldo Wizz's magic skills—along with his bright blue eyes—many, many times.
Ben was about to remind Gaby of this when another idea came to him.
Waldo was supposed to be some kind of genius at magic.
Maybe he could help find the monster who was crashing all the brooms.
Ben finally spotted Waldo in the hallway after English.
"Waldo!" called Ben, hurrying up to him.
Waldo spun around, sending his glasses flying off his nose.
He picked them up and peered at Ben.
"Hey, you're the new ghost . . . Ben, right?
How do you like Monster Academy so far?"
"It's great," said Ben. "Except for the crazy brooms crashing everywhere.
I was looking forward to the Monster Mash dance.
I hear it's always really fun."
"It is," Waldo agreed. "Too bad Mr. Freaky had to cancel it for now.
But don't worry," he went on. "I'm a pretty amazing wizard.
I can figure out who's flying the brooms in no time at all."
"Wow, that's great!" Ben said. "What are you going to do?"
"I'll formulate a truth potion," Waldo answered.
"I'll give it to every single student at Monster Academy and then question them, one by one."
"Oh . . . um . . ." Ben hesitated.
"There are hundreds of students at Monster Academy.
Won't it take a really long time to question everyone?"
"Hmm . . . I guess you're right . . . Hey!" Waldo suddenly had a big smile.
"You're a ghost! You could investigate without anyone seeing you!"
"I can move quietly," said Ben. "But I'm not invisible."
"Oh, right," said Waldo, rubbing his chin. "I know! I'll cast a sleep spell!"
"Okay," said Ben. This idea sounded a little better to him.
"When can we start?"
Waldo glanced around. "I can do the spell now if we hurry," he whispered. "Follow me!"
Ben followed Waldo into the empty library.
Waldo took an enormous book out of his backpack and flipped through the pages.
"Here it is," he said. "The sleep spell."
"Are you sure it will work?" asked Ben.
"I've never actually tried it," said Waldo.
"But don't worry—I'm very skilled at magic."
"That's what I've heard," Ben murmured.
Waldo quietly recited the spell.
When he was finished, he looked at Ben.
"The spell is done," said Waldo.
"Go look for clues. But be quick—the spell lasts for only one hour!"
Ben decided to search the broom-flying classroom first.
The room's closet was filled with witches' brooms.
Each one was marked "MA," for Monster Academy.
"I don't see any clues in here," he murmured.
"Just a bunch of—what's that?"
Ben reached down and picked up a small object.
"I wonder what this is," he thought, slipping it into his pocket.
"It looks a little like a tooth."
Suddenly a voice said, "What are you doing here?"
Ben spun around and saw Winnie. Her eyes were wide open.
"Oh," said Ben. "I . . . uh . . ."
Why was Winnie awake?
And what was she doing in the broom-flying classroom?
Winnie started talking really fast.
"I was in math class, but suddenly I just couldn't sit still.
No one could. I mean, who wants to do math when you feel like running or going flying or something? Right?
Even Mr. Slime didn't want to be there.
'Class dismissed!' he said, and then he ran out of the room so he could go jogging around the track."
Winnie ran over to the brooms. "Oh, how I wish I could fly them!"
"See you, Winnie," Ben called. She was acting really weird.
He had to find Waldo right away to see what was going on.
Earlier the halls had been empty.
Now teachers and students were rushing around.
In the middle of the chaos, Waldo made his way toward Ben.
"Something happened with the sleep spell!" whispered Waldo in a panic.
"Instead of putting everyone to sleep, it made them wide-awake!"
"You're not kidding!" said Ben. "What happened?"
Waldo looked sheepish. "I guess even a great wizard like me can make a mistake sometimes."
"I guess," Ben muttered.
Waldo held up his hands.
"Don't worry. I have another spell I can use. Follow me."
Ben followed Waldo to the library once again.
The wizard opened his big book of spells and recited some new words.
"This spell will make everyone forget everything that happens during the next hour," said Waldo.
"Even if other monsters see you snooping around, they won't remember."
"Awesome," said Ben. "Let's go search for clues!"
Ben and Waldo hurried back into the hallway.
Instantly all the monsters—students and teachers—fell silent.
They all stared at Waldo.
A purple monster ran up to Waldo.
"Oh, Waldo, what a wonderful wizard you are!"
A witch pushed the purple monster aside. "Waldo! You are so cute!"
"Will you marry me, Waldo?" shouted a mummy.
"Will you go to the Monster Mash with me?" cried a goblin.
"What is going on?" cried Ben.
"Why is everyone in love with you all of sudden?"
Waldo put his palm to his forehead.
"Ugh! I didn't cast a forgetting spell. I cast a love spell!"
To Ben's relief, Waldo's love spell didn't last long.
Soon everyone stopped fighting and arguing over Waldo.
"Students!" Mr. Freaky hurried down the hallway.
"Why are you all hanging around the hallway? Get to class!"
As the monsters started making their way back to their classrooms, Ben glanced at Waldo.
The wizard was scratching his head.
"I wonder why the love spell wore off so quickly. Maybe I did it wrong."
"Who cares why?" asked Ben. "Just be happy that it did.
Otherwise, you'd be married to everyone at Monster Academy by now!"
"Let's go back to the library," said Waldo.
"I'm sure I can come up with another spell."
"Um . . . No thanks." So far Waldo's magic wasn't much help.
"Maybe later," Ben added quickly. "Right now I'd better get to class."
He floated off, absentmindedly fingering the tiny toothlike thing in his pocket.
"Now what?" Ben thought. Maybe he needed to make a list of suspects.
He didn't really know many kids at Monster Academy, but already one of them was high on his list—Mog.
Winnie had said Mog was nice, but he seemed like a troublemaker to Ben.
So maybe Mog was the one causing all the trouble with the brooms.
The next day at lunch, Mr. Freaky came into the cafeteria, looking even more nervous than usual.
His three noses were wiggling wildly.
"Everything is totally out of control!" he cried.
"Today two brooms are missing from the broom-flying classroom.
And we can't find them anywhere!"
Ben shot a look at Mog, who was sitting with Winnie.
But the monster wasn't looking his way.
The broom-flying teacher, Miss Bungle, was on lunch duty.
"Try not to get your noses in an uproar, Mr. Freaky," said Miss Bungle.
"You know what happens then—they all get stuffed up."
"How can I help it when someone keeps flying the brooms and crashing them all over school?" cried Mr. Freaky.
"It's a very dangerous situation!" He stopped to blow his noses.
"Until this problem is solved, I don't want to see anyone near the broom-flying classroom."
Ben glanced at Mog again.
Winnie was laughing at something the big monster was saying.
Suddenly Ben remembered that she'd come into the broom-flying classroom the day before. What was she—?
Abruptly, Winnie looked up and stared straight back at him.
Ben quickly looked back down at his lunch tray.
He hoped she hadn't been reading his mind again.
Then she'd know all about his suspicions!
That night Ben lay in bed, still thinking about Winnie and everything going on at Monster Academy.
The more he thought about the crashing brooms, the more suspicious he was of Mog.
"It can't be Winnie," he told himself.
She was too nice. And besides, there was no reason for her to cause trouble.
But Mog, meanwhile, was mean and—
"Whoo!" moaned Sid.
"Sid!" Ben snapped. He looked over at his younger brother.
They had to keep the bedroom totally dark or Sid got scared.
Ben didn't mind the dark.
But tonight Sid was practicing his moaning, which made it hard for Ben to think.
"Whoo!" moaned Sid again. He was even louder this time.
"Sid, be quiet!" said Ben. "I'm trying to concentrate."
"Well, I'm trying to moan," said Sid.
"I want to be really good at it. Whoo!"
Ben put his pillow over his head to muffle the sound.
Eventually, Sid stopped moaning and fell asleep.
Ben's parents had gone to bed too, so at last the house was quiet.
"Proof," thought Ben. "I need to find some proof."
Before long Ben had formed a plan.
He floated over to the window and quietly slid it open.
Careful not to wake Sid, he sailed out into the moonlit night.
Ben soared high above the streets of Monsterville.
Bats flew silently by, and the moon cast an eerie glow on the rooftops.
Ben looked nervously around. He hoped he didn't get caught.
Soon he was flying over Monster Academy.
The building was dark and empty. Ben knew he wouldn't be able to go inside.
He flew around the soccer field, looking for signs of the two missing magic brooms.
He checked the trash area and the bike rack, where Mog seemed to hang out a lot.
But there were no clues anywhere, as far as Ben could tell.
After that, Ben flew all around Monsterville, peering into alleyways, parks, and backyards as he looked for the missing brooms.
He saw a few brooms, but none of them was from Monster Academy.
He headed toward Mog's neighborhood, which was close to the fence that separated Monsterville from People Place.
Suddenly a loud, angry voice thundered below him.
"What do you think you're doing here?"
Ben recognized the voice right away.
It was Mog! There was a two-headed dog by his side.
"What are you doing here?" Mog demanded.
"I couldn't sleep," Ben said quickly. He landed in front of Mog.
"I was just flying around Monsterville."
"Just flying around?" Mog echoed.
He narrowed his eyes and moved closer to Ben. "Winnie loves to fly.
I bet you're looking for those two missing brooms to impress her!"
Ben was surprised that Mog had guessed the truth so quickly.
He backed away from the big monster.
"No, I'm just flying around," he repeated.
Suddenly Mog smiled. "I'm just kidding," he said.
"I'll tell you a secret, but you have to promise not to tell anyone, not one single monster!"
"Why is Mog being so friendly all of a sudden?" Ben thought.
He was suspicious, but aloud he said, "I won't tell."
"Come closer," said Mog. "I have to whisper so no one will hear."
"But there's no one here but us," said Ben.
"You never know," said Mog, glancing around.
"There could be spies on either side of the fence."
Ben hovered so he was at eye level with Mog.
"Closer!" hissed Mog.
Ben moved closer.
"I've been looking for the missing brooms too," Mog whispered.
"I think people are stealing them."
"What?" Ben felt his eyes widen. "Why do you think that?"
"I was sneaking around in People Place the other day," said Mog.
"I saw two brooms on the roof of a house.
I couldn't climb up to get them, but I could clearly see 'MA' on the handles."
Ben peered at Mog in the moonlight. Was he telling the truth?
"Why would people steal the brooms?" asked Ben.
"And how could they make them fly?"
"I don't know." Mog shrugged. "Maybe it's because the brooms are magic.
The people are probably jealous and want to learn how to fly them.
And that's why the brooms are crashing all over the place.
The people don't know what they're doing."
Ben still didn't trust Mog.
"If people did steal the brooms, why did they put them on a roof?
That doesn't make sense."
Mog shrugged again. "They probably just thought it was a good hiding spot.
After all, who would think to look up on a roof?"
"That makes sense," said Ben.
"So did you tell Mr. Freaky you saw the brooms?"
"No," said Mog. "I didn't want to get in trouble for sneaking around People Place."
He paused and seemed to think for a moment. "You're a ghost, though.
You could easily fly into People Place and get the brooms back."
Ben looked suspiciously at Mog. Could he really trust this monster?
"Listen," said Mog. "If we get those brooms back, we can put them in the broom closet.
Then, as long as they don't disappear again, Mr. Freaky will probably change his mind about the Monster Mash dance.
And you know Winnie will be happy."
Ben thought about this. Mog might be telling the truth.
Then again, Mog was probably lying. Maybe he wanted to get Ben in trouble.
Mog certainly wouldn't want Winnie to feel grateful to Ben.
Still, it couldn't hurt to fly over People Place just to see the brooms, could it?
Finally Ben nodded. "Okay, I'll do it. Where's the house?"
"Awesome," said Mog with a grin.
"It's a big house on Main Street. It's only a few blocks from the fence.
The house is yellow, and it has a tower. You can't miss it."
Ben took a deep breath. "I'll be back soon."
"I'll be waiting right here," whispered Mog as Ben flew off.
Ben couldn't believe he was actually flying over the fence and into People Place.
On the other side, he looked around.
Without any people, the town looked a lot like Monsterville, with schools and stores and parks.
Still, Ben knew he couldn't spend too much time looking around.
If he got caught, he'd be in serious trouble.
Ben flew a bit farther and found Main Street.
It was lined with houses, and cars were parked along the street.
He quickly spotted the yellow house with the tower.
He flew over it, but he didn't see any brooms on the roof.
"Mog definitely lied to me," thought Ben.
There were no brooms from Monster Academy here.
Ben was hovering outside a window when he noticed a young boy inside.
The boy was fast asleep in bed, hugging a giant stuffed teddy bear almost as big as Ben.
Suddenly there was a loud crashing sound from back by the fence.
A couple of lights in nearby houses blinked on.
The boy sat bolt upright in bed.
He stared directly at Ben and shrieked, "Mommy! Daddy! A ghost!"
A light in the yellow house blinked on, and Ben heard the sound of footsteps racing up the stairs.
A deep voice boomed, "What's wrong, son? Don't worry! Daddy's coming!"
Ben gulped. "I'm going to be in big trouble!"
Too scared to find out what would happen next, Ben shot back toward Monsterville as fast as he could.
Several garbage cans near the fence had been knocked over.
Ben flew over the fence and then stopped to catch his breath.
"That was scary," thought Ben. "That little kid was so scared of me!
I could have gotten in a lot of trouble!"
Looking around, he realized Mog was nowhere in sight.
"Mog!" called Ben. "Mog, where are you?"
There was no answer.
"Where did he go?" Ben murmured.
Then he remembered the loud crashing sound and the garbage cans that had been knocked over.
Could Mog have done that? Ben wondered about it as he flew home.
A short while later, Ben slipped back into his bedroom.
Sid was still snoring quietly in his bed.
Ben climbed into his own bed, his heart still racing as he thought about his adventure in People Place.
What if he'd been caught? He wasn't sure what would have happened.
Maybe the people would have captured him.
First thing in the morning, they probably would have marched him over to Monster Academy and into Mr. Freaky's office. Yikes!
Ben shuddered and tried to go to sleep, but it wasn't easy.
He tossed and turned all night.
He couldn't stop thinking about the little kid he'd scared.
And he couldn't stop thinking about Mog.
"I knew I never should have trusted him," thought Ben.
The next morning at school, Ben spotted Mog in the crowded hallway before homeroom.
He stormed toward him. "Where did you go last night?" he called.
To Ben's surprise, Mog shot a quick glance at Ben and then hurried off in the other direction.
Ben narrowed his eyes at the monster.
"Mog definitely knocked over those garbage cans.
I'm sure he was just trying to get me in trouble!
Well, he can't hide from me forever.
He'll have to talk to me in cooking class."
Ben went to homeroom and sat down, still fuming.
"Attention, all monsters!" Mr. Freaky's voice crackled over the loudspeaker.
"A very grave situation has come to my attention!"
"Uh-oh!" Ben bolted upright, worried.
But a ghost sitting next to Ben was laughing.
"A 'grave' situation? Ha-ha!
Maybe we're going to take a field trip to a graveyard!"
"Oh, I love graveyards!" said a skeleton girl dreamily.
Mr. Freaky was still talking. "First period is canceled this morning.
Instead I want all students to report to the auditorium."
Ben's thoughts were racing.
Did Mr. Freaky know about his adventure in People Place the night before?
Ben remembered that little kid and how scared he'd looked at the sight of a ghost.
Why in the world had Ben listened to Mog?
The bell rang just then, and monsters began to stream out of homerooms to make their way to the auditorium.
Ben followed them and slunk into a seat next to Gaby. "Hey," he murmured.
"I wonder what Mr. Freaky is going to talk about," said Gaby.
Ben was too worried to respond.
The principal walked up to the microphone, looking very serious.
"I received a phone call this morning," said Mr. Freaky.
"Apparently a ghost flew into People Place last night and scared a little child."
A shocked rumble went through the auditorium.
"A ghost?" said a fish monster.
"In People Place?" said an octopus monster.
"Scared a kid?" said a purple monster.
"That's terrible!" said Gaby.
Ben slid down in his chair, holding his breath.
"Quiet!" shouted Mr. Freaky.
Right away the entire auditorium fell silent.
"Unfortunately the child who saw the ghost isn't just any child," said Mr. Freaky.
"He's Mayor Hubbletree's son!"
Ben almost slid off his chair. The mayor's son?
Had Mog known that when he sent Ben to that house to look for the brooms?
Ben saw Mog sitting in the next row, but the monster was looking the other way.
"As many of you know," said Mr. Freaky, "Monster Academy was built on land owned by People Place."
The principal looked at the floor and took a deep breath.
"There's no easy way to say this, but . . .
Mayor Hubbletree has decided to evict us."
A huge gasp filled the auditorium.
"That means we must leave," said Mr. Freaky.
"Monster Academy is going to be destroyed!"
At first Ben had been afraid of getting in trouble for scaring the little boy.
Now something much worse was happening.
Mayor Hubbletree was planning to destroy Monster Academy.
And it was all Ben's fault!
"Maybe I should confess," thought Ben in a panic.
Maybe if he told Mr. Freaky the truth, the principal could find a way to get Mayor Hubbletree to change his mind about the school.
But Ben wasn't sure.
He was new at Monster Academy and still learning how things worked there.
Maybe he'd just better stay quiet for now.
At lunch that day, Ben wanted to be alone to think.
He found a table with two zombies and sat down.
While the zombies stared and drooled silently on their food, Ben thought about his situation.
Nearby he heard Winnie talking.
"I can't believe Mayor Hubbletree is going to destroy Monster Academy," she said.
"What's going to happen to us? Where will we go to school?"
"Believe it!" a mummy replied.
"And just wait until he finds the ghost who scared his son.
That ghost is going to be in big trouble!"
Ben looked over at Winnie. To his surprise, she smiled at him!
Ordinarily Ben would have been thrilled, but today he had too much on his mind.
"I have to find Mog," he thought.
Once he talked to Mog, Ben could make a plan, figure out what to do.
But Ben didn't have a chance to talk with Mog until the next morning in cooking class.
Mrs. Hag assigned the two of them to make a rotten-egg omelet together.
"Mog!" Ben growled as soon as they were alone at their cooking station.
"You got me into trouble!"
"It wasn't my fault," said Mog. He cracked a rotten egg into a bowl.
"What do you mean, it wasn't your fault?" Ben glared at the big monster.
"I know you knocked over those garbage cans.
You made a big loud sound just to get me in trouble.
And you're probably the one who's flying the brooms!"
"Monsters, quiet!" snapped Mrs. Hag.
"You're supposed to be cooking, not talking."
Ben lowered his voice.
"You knew the big house with the tower was the mayor's mansion.
I'll bet you never saw any witches' brooms on the roof.
You just wanted to get me into trouble because Winnie is nice to me!"
Mog's shoulders slumped. "Okay," he said. "You're right.
I made the whole thing up to get you in trouble.
The brooms were never on the roof. I knocked over the garbage cans.
But I just wanted you to get in a little bit of trouble.
I didn't know the whole thing would turn into such a big deal."
Ben noticed Winnie glancing over at Mog as the monster spoke.
"Well, it is a big deal!" Ben whispered furiously.
"What's going to happen once they find out it was me who entered People Place?
That was your plan.
So you'd better help me find a way to fix the problem it caused!"
Mog nodded slowly. "You're right, Ben," he said.
"I'm really sorry. But I'm not the one who's taking the brooms, I swear."
Ben nodded. For the first time, Mog actually seemed sincere.
He was pretty sure Mog was telling the truth.
"Meet me outside after school, by the flagpole," Mog said.
"We'll come up with a plan together."
After school Ben hurried outside. He was shocked by what he saw.
Several large construction vehicles sat in front of the school.
A big bulldozer rumbled loudly, puffing smoke.
In front of the vehicles stood a man dressed in a dark suit.
A few other people stood behind him.
"That must be Mayor Hubbletree," thought Ben.
Mr. Freaky ran out of the school, waving his arms frantically.
"Mayor Hubbletree!" cried the principal. "What are you doing?"
"I told you yesterday, Freaky," said the mayor.
"I'm knocking this place to the ground!"
"I didn't know you meant so soon!" said Mr. Freaky.
"We need time to move our things out!"
"The ghost who scared my little boy should have thought of that!"
Mayor Hubbletree shot back.
"Mayor, please," said Mr. Freaky.
"Over two hundred monsters attend Monster Academy.
Where will they go to school? Can't you at least wait until next week?"
Mr. Freaky's lip began to tremble.
Ben thought the principal was about to cry.
The mayor sighed. "Oh, all right.
I'll give you one more day. But that's all!"
Ben found Mog and rushed over to him. "Did you hear that?" asked Ben.
"We only have one day. You need to think of an idea—fast!"
Mog shook his head. "I can't think fast."
Ben was about to say something, but Mog put up a claw.
"I can think slowly though," he said. "And I have an idea."
"What is it?" asked Ben.
"We should sneak back into People Place," said Mog.
"What!" cried Ben. "Sneak back into People Place? That's your big idea?"
Ben stared at Mog in disbelief. Mog wanted to sneak back into People Place?
"Let me finish," said Mog.
"I think we should sneak into People Place, go to Mayor Hubbletree's house, and apologize."
"What?" Ben's jaw dropped.
He had imagined telling Mr. Freaky what had happened.
But he'd never imagined speaking directly to the mayor!
"It's the right thing to do," Mog went on.
"I'll tell him the truth. And I'll explain that I tricked you."
Just then Winnie stepped out from the crowd, her eyes flashing with anger.
"I heard that, Mog! It's your fault Monster Academy is going to be destroyed!"
Mog gulped. "I—I didn't mean to—"
"We're through!" said Winnie.
"Even if the school was still having the dance, I wouldn't go with you.
Not if you were the last monster in Monsterville!"
She spun around and walked away.
Mog stared after her and sighed.
"We'd better do something fast," he murmured.
That evening Ben and Mog met by the fence between Monsterville and People Place.
Mog couldn't fly, so Ben waited while he climbed the fence.
Halfway over, Mog let out a yelp.
"Uh-oh," said Mog. "I'm stuck!"
"How are you stuck?" said Ben.
"My pants are caught on a nail," said Mog. "Hold on a second."
The monster tried to lift himself to free his pants, but he slipped.
Rip!
Ben tried not to laugh as Mog hung from the nail by his ripped pants.
"Ugh!" cried Mog. "This is—"
Rip! Mog's pants ripped some more, and then he fell to the ground.
"Ouch!"
"Are you okay?" asked Ben.
Mog rubbed his head. "Yeah, I'm okay."
He stood up, and his pants fell down. "Aw, man! My pants are ruined!"
"Never mind that now," said Ben. "Let's just get this over with."
Ben and Mog hurried toward the mayor's house.
Mog had to hold up his pants as he ran.
The sun was setting, and the streetlights were beginning to flicker on.
Soon Ben and Mog were standing in front of the mayor's house.
"What do we do now?" asked Ben.
"We go up to the door and knock," said Mog.
Ben gulped. "You first," he said.
They went to the door, and Mog knocked with one hand.
The other hand was still holding up his pants.
Ben's heart beat faster as he heard heavy footsteps getting closer.
The door finally opened, and Mayor Hubbletree was standing there.
"Monsters!" cried the mayor. "What are you doing here?"
"Hello, s-sir," Ben stammered. "We, uh—"
"Monsters?" cried a little boy's voice.
Ben gulped as the mayor's son ran to the doorway.
"Oh no!" thought Ben. "He'll see us and get scared all over again!"
It was too late.
The boy stood in the doorway and stared, wide-eyed, at Mog and Ben.
He looked like he was going to scream.
Mog held up his hands and said, "Don't be scared!"
Instantly his pants fell down.
"Ha-ha!" The boy laughed hysterically.
Mog's face turned red as he quickly pulled his pants back up.
"Sorry about that, I—"
"That's funny!" said the boy. "Ha-ha!"
Mayor Hubbletree had been frowning.
But as he watched his son laugh, his frown faded.
Soon he was smiling. Then he was laughing.
Ben looked from the boy to the mayor to Mog.
Despite being embarrassed, Mog grinned. "Ha-ha!"
Then Ben laughed too.
The next day at school, Ben heard lots of kids talking about him and Mog.
"I heard Mog and Ben went to Mayor Hubbletree's house last night," said a ghoul.
"Yeah," said a troll. "I heard Mog's pants fell down."
"It's a good thing they did," said a purple monster.
"The mayor's son thought it was funny.
The mayor isn't angry at monsters anymore."
A mummy nodded. "Yep. And now he's no longer planning on destroying Monster Academy."
Ben also overheard that Mayor Hubbletree wasn't just going to leave Monster Academy alone.
"I'd like to see monsters and people get along," the mayor had told Mr. Freaky.
"Maybe our students could take a field trip to Monster Academy."
"That would be wonderful," said Mr. Freaky.
"And I'm sure our monsters would love to see People Place."
Ben was floating along the school hallway as monsters gathered around to congratulate him.
"Way to go, Ben " shouted a ghoul.
"Thanks," said Ben. "It was really Mog's—"
Suddenly—crash! A broomstick smashed through a wall!
Mr. Freaky rushed into the hallway.
He moaned when he saw the broomstick in the wall.
"Who is doing this? It has to stop!"
Ben cringed. He knew now it wasn't Mog stealing the brooms.
So there was only one other suspect—Winnie.
The next day in cooking class, Mrs. Hag was explaining the importance of using the best ingredients.
Ben tried to listen, but he was distracted by his worries about Winnie.
And his worries that Winnie would know what he was thinking.
"Everything should be moldy or rotten," Mrs. Hag told the students.
"Some cooks like to use fresh earwax and pocket lint."
Ben didn't have any earwax, so he reached into his pocket to see about lint.
He felt the tooth he'd found in the broom flying classroom and took it out of his pocket.
Mrs. Hag spotted it as she walked past Ben's worktable.
"Oh, you've got a bat claw.
I bought some the other day, but I can't find them.
I guess I lost them somewhere."
Ben was stunned. The object in his palm wasn't a tooth; it was a bat claw!
Had Mrs. Hag accidentally dropped one in the broom-flying classroom? Could she be . . . ?
Did that mean Winnie . . . ?
"Oh, wow," Ben murmured.
He had to tell Mr. Freaky! But Ben knew he needed proof before he accused a teacher of anything.
He glanced at Mog. Maybe Mog would help him.
They weren't exactly friends now, but they weren't enemies anymore either.
At the end of the day, Ben found Mog in the hallway.
"Mog! I need to talk to you."
"Sure," said Mog. "What's up?"
"I think Mrs. Hag is the one flying the brooms," whispered Ben.
"Really?" said Mog. He looked shocked.
Ben filled him in.
"It makes sense," said Mog.
"Winnie told me Mrs. Hag was really upset when Mr. Freaky made her stop teaching broom flying.
And everyone says she's terrible at flying.
That could explain the crashing brooms."
Ben nodded. He was getting more and more excited about his theory.
"Now we just need to prove it."
"Let's look for clues in the broom-flying classroom," said Mog.
The two monsters hurried upstairs and into the classroom.
"Hey!" cried a voice from the closet. "Get me out of here!"
"That's Winnie!" cried Ben. He quickly unlocked the closet door.
Winnie leaped out of the closet. "Thanks! It was hot in there!"
"What were you doing in the broom closet?" asked Mog.
"I came up here to look at the brooms," said Winnie. "I miss them.
But Mrs. Hag was here. She pushed me into the closet and locked me—"
Crash! A window smashed as Mrs. Hag rocketed into the room, flying two brooms.
"Look out!" she cried.
The brooms shot around the room, zipped upside down, and then flew out the door.
Ben, Mog, and Winnie rushed into the hallway.
One broom flew out from under Mrs. Hag and crashed into a trophy case.
The teacher lost her grip on the other one, which shot up through the ceiling.
Mrs. Hag tumbled downward. Bam! She crashed into Mr. Freaky.
The next day Mrs. Hag announced her retirement.
It turned out that she'd been making trouble at school to get back at Mr. Freaky.
Ben didn't think anyone at Monster Academy was sorry to see Mrs. Hag go.
Mr. Freaky had already hired a new cooking teacher, and Miss Bungle was going to start teaching broom flying again.
Later Gaby rushed up to Ben in the hallway.
"Did you hear the news? Mr. Freaky rescheduled the Monster Mash dance.
It's tomorrow night. Now Waldo and I can go together.
It's going to be so awesome!"
Ben floated down the hallway toward his locker.
He was glad for Gaby, but he couldn't help feeling a little sorry for himself.
Winnie wasn't mad at Mog anymore.
So now she would go with Mog to the dance, of course.
"It's just as well," thought Ben. Mog was his friend now too.
Maybe Ben could—
"Hey, Ben!" shouted Mog just then. The monster came running toward him.
"Hey, Mog," Ben replied.
"Do you know Lilly?" asked Mog. "She's got three eyes and a big blue horn."
"No," said Ben. "Why?"
"I just asked her to the Monster Mash dance," said Mog with a big smile. "And she said yes!"
"That's great!" said Ben. "But what about Winnie? Aren't you two—"
"Nah," said Mog. "We broke up."
When Mog left, Ben felt a smile spread across his face.
Winnie and Mog had broken up! Now he could ask Winnie to the dance!
But as he floated toward the exit, Ben felt himself getting nervous.
"Maybe she won't say yes," he thought.
"Maybe she's already going with someone else."
Outside, he could see Winnie soaring over the soccer field on one of the school brooms.
She was leaning over it with a happy look on her face, probably thrilled to be flying again.
"Here goes." Ben took a deep breath and then headed toward her.
Ben floated out to the soccer field where Winnie was flying her broom.
She looked so happy soaring over the field.
"I'm coming in for a landing!" he heard her say.
"Me too!" cried another witch, tilting her broom down toward the field.
Ben watched Winnie cruise to a soft landing.
Then he floated over to her, his heart beating fast.
He had come outside to ask her to the Monster Mash dance on Friday night.
"What if she says no?" Ben thought, suddenly panicked.
That would be terrible.
He'd feel so stupid, and then things would get awkward between them. Maybe he shouldn't—
Just then Winnie smiled at him. Her green eyes sparkled in the sunlight.
Ben smiled back nervously. Winnie could sometimes read people's thoughts.
Did she know what he was thinking now?
"Great flying, Winnie," said Ben quickly.
"Thanks," she answered. "I'm practicing for my broom-flying test.
If I pass, I'll finally have my broom-flying license.
Then maybe I can join the Witches' Formation team.
They get to fly over the school during important events."
"I'm sure you'll pass," said Ben.
He knew he had to ask her now, before he lost all his courage.
He took a deep breath—such a deep breath, he suddenly felt dizzy.
Winnie stared at him. "Ben, are you okay? You look pale, even for a ghost."
"I'm fine," Ben lied.
His heart pounded faster. "Winnie, will you . . . um . . . ?"
Smiling, Winnie tilted her head. "Will I . . . ?"
"Will you go to the Monster Mash with me?"
For a moment Winnie didn't say anything.
"Oh no!" Ben thought, panicking again. "I never should have—"
"I'd love to," she said.
"You would? I mean, wow! That's great!"
Suddenly Ben didn't know what to say. "Dancing is fun, right?"
"I love dancing," Winnie agreed.
"I love it almost as much as I love broom flying."
"Me too," said Ben. "I mean, not broom flying but just regular flying.
Not that there's anything wrong with broom flying. It's just that I'm a ghost and . . ."
"What a dumb thing to say," Ben thought as Winnie giggled.
He was babbling like an idiot.
"I'll pick you up at seven," Ben told her. "Okay?"
"Actually," Winnie said, "I'm on the decorating committee.
So I have to get to the gym early to help decorate.
Maybe we can just meet at the dance?"
"Sure," said Ben. "That sounds great. I'll see you at school tomorrow."
"Okay," said Winnie, grinning at him.
Ben floated away as fast as he could. He could not believe his good luck.
Ever since he'd first seen Winnie, he'd thought she was the most beautiful witch in the world.
And now she was going to the dance with him!
The next morning during homeroom, Mr. Freaky's voice crackled over the loudspeaker.
"Good morning, students.
I wanted to let everyone know that Miss Bungle is out sick with the flu today.
So all of her broom-flying classes and activities are canceled until she returns. Thank you."
Ben shot Winnie a sympathetic look.
She looked pretty disappointed at the news.
"Maybe Miss Bungle will be back soon," he whispered.
"Yeah, I hope she's okay." Winnie smiled and tried to shrug it off.
But Ben could tell that she was upset.
"At least I have the dance to look forward to tonight, right?"
"Right," he answered with a grin.
After homeroom they walked together to Cooking.
Today Ben was actually looking forward to cooking something.
Mr. Freaky had hired a new teacher to replace Mrs. Hag.
This one was supposed to be a much better cook than Mrs. Hag.
"Good morning, monsters," said the new teacher, who was wearing goggles and an apron.
"My name is Mr. Icky." His four tentacles waved to the students.
"Today we're going to make slug cupcakes with rotten-egg frosting.
They're for the dance tonight."
"Woo-hoo!" called Mog.
He was sitting with his new girlfriend, Lilly, and a few other monsters.
"Slug cupcakes are awesome!"
Soon the students started cooking.
As Ben plopped slugs into his cupcake batter, he overheard Winnie talking to some other girl monsters about the dance.
"I got my dress at Frightful Fashion," said a witch.
"My mom bought me some new shoes too."
"My dress is from the Suction Shop," said an octopus monster.
"It's bright pink, and guess what—"
She waved a bunch of her arms. "It's sleeveless!"
"Cool. You're going to look great," said Winnie.
She glanced over at Ben with a shy smile.
"My dress is from the Witch's Closet.
It's really pretty—black, of course, with lots of lace."
Ben smiled back at Winnie, and he was still smiling a minute later as he started stirring the cupcake batter.
He couldn't wait to see Winnie tonight.
Their first Monster Mash dance together was going to be perfect.
That night the moon shone bright and full.
Ben headed over to Monster Academy early.
"What a fantastic night," he said to himself.
"There will be great music, great food, and a whole night with Winnie!"
At school Ben peeked into the gym to see if Winnie and the others were still working on the decorations.
"Wow!" he burst out.
Silky spider webs shimmered from the ceiling, and eerie lights cast spooky shadows around the room.
Onstage the Boneyard Brass Band was setting up their equipment.
One skeleton tuned a trumpet, while another tapped a tune on his own rib cage.
"Winnie?" Ben called. The skeletons looked up, but there was no sign of Winnie or anyone else from the dance committee.
Ben stepped out into the hallway.
"Hey, Ben!" Waldo Wizz called. "You're here early."
"Yeah." Ben shrugged. "Winnie's here already, decorating the gym.
I thought I'd come early to help her."
"I think she finished decorating," Waldo reported.
"A bunch of girls just went upstairs to change into their dresses.
I've got nothing to do now, so I was going to check on my latest magic experiment. Want to see it?"
"Sure," said Ben.
"It's in the science lab, and it's top secret."
Waldo led the way to the lab.
"You can't tell anyone about it."
Ben held up a hand. "I promise, Waldo."
As they turned a corner, Waldo bumped into a large purple blob.
His glasses flew off his face.
"Oh!" Waldo fumbled for them on the floor and then put them back on. "Hi, Jen."
"Sorry about that, Waldo," said the blob.
"You haven't seen a, um, human around here, have you?"
"A human?" echoed Waldo.
"He's my date," said Jen awkwardly.
Ben wasn't sure, but the purple blob appeared to be blushing.
"I left him alone while I got ready upstairs with the witches.
Now I can't find him."
"We haven't seen him," Waldo said to Jen.
"If we do, though, we'll let him know you're looking for him."
"He's a little freaked out by Monster Academy," said the blob, jiggling as she talked.
"I don't understand humans sometimes."
"Yeah, humans are weird," agreed Waldo. "We'll keep an eye out for him."
"Thanks, Waldo." Jen moved past Waldo and Ben, and glided down the hallway, leaving behind a shiny trail of slime.
"I didn't know there'd be a human at the Monster Mash," said Waldo.
"Me neither," said Ben. He shivered. "Creepy!"
Ben and Waldo entered the science lab.
Inside, Waldo gasped. A strange purple fog filled the room.
Through the fog Ben could see test tubes and rubber hoses on a counter in the back.
Near them a small appliance that looked like a pressure cooker beeped noisily.
Waldo rushed to the back of the lab.
He quickly flipped a switch on the appliance, and the beeping stopped.
Ben floated over and saw that the hoses were all connected to the small appliance.
"I'm trying to make a talk potion," Waldo explained.
"Whoever drinks the potion will talk and talk and talk."
"Why would anyone want to drink a talk potion?" asked Ben.
"It's mostly for shy people," Waldo explained.
"But . . ." His cheeks were bright pink.
"But it looks like somebody pulled all the hoses off the test tubes!
Who would do that?"
"Shy people?" said Ben.
Waldo gave Ben a funny look.
"Why would shy people try to ruin my potion?"
"No, I mean . . ." Ben tried to explain.
"You said this talk potion is for shy people.
So I was asking why shy people would need it."
"Oh, right," said Waldo.
He began putting the hoses back on the test tubes.
"Well, usually shy people don't know what to talk about.
But if they drink my potion, they'll have plenty to talk about.
Police could also use it on suspects who are refusing to talk."
"Oh, I see," said Ben.
Though, knowing Waldo, Ben had a feeling that the potion might not work exactly as Waldo had described. "Is everything okay?"
"I think so . . ."
By now the purple fog in the room was beginning to clear.
Ben could see it disappearing into an air vent in the ceiling.
Boom! A sound came from the front of the room.
"What was that?" Ben asked.
Waldo was still busy fixing his equipment.
"There!" he said triumphantly as the appliance began to hum.
Ben saw that the door to the lab was now shut.
He hurried over and tried the handle. "Uh, Waldo . . ." he said nervously.
"I think we're locked in here."
"Huh?" Waldo finally looked up. "What?"
Ben tried the handle again, but the door still wouldn't budge.
"I mean that someone locked us in the science lab. We can't get out!"
Ben pulled on the door handle again and again.
No matter how hard he pulled, the lab door still wouldn't open.
"Pull harder!" said Waldo.
"I am!" Ben grunted. "Why don't you try?"
Waldo yanked on the door handle, but he couldn't open the door either.
"It must be locked from the outside."
Ben slumped against the door.
"We'll never get out of here," he moaned. He thought about Winnie.
Then he thought about Winnie in her beautiful new black dress.
By now she was probably back in the gym, looking for him.
"Let me think," said Waldo, pacing back and forth.
"There must be something we can do."
"You're a wizard," said Ben.
"Don't you know any spells that could open the door?"
Waldo shook his head. "I left my spell book at home."
Suddenly he laughed. "Wait a minute! Why are we worrying about this?
You're a ghost, Ben. Just float through a wall and unlock the door!"
Ben sighed. "I can't."
Waldo's jaw dropped. "Are you kidding me?
I thought all ghosts could float through walls.
I mean, what's the point of being a ghost if you can't do stuff like that?"
Ben was annoyed. "I never learned how, all right?
And you're not helping us either.
What's the point of being a wizard if you can't even use magic to open a door?"
"Good point." Waldo hung his head. "I'm sorry. I was just annoyed.
I don't want to miss the Monster Mash."
"Me neither," said Ben. "I've really been looking forward to it."
Waldo slid down next to Ben, and the two sat in silence for a moment.
"I'll be able to float through walls eventually," Ben mumbled.
"I practice every night, and my mom says that some ghosts just take longer than others to learn this stuff.
Don't tell anyone, okay?"
"I won't," Waldo promised.
"I'm the only wizard I know who still needs to carry around a spell book.
Really good wizards can do magic without spells."
"Oh," Ben replied. The two of them were quiet again.
Then Ben heard something.
"Footsteps!" he cried. "Waldo! Someone's coming!"
They leaped to their feet as the footsteps came closer.
"Everything is totally under control," said a voice.
"It's Mr. Freaky," said Ben. "He can get us out of here!"
"I'm really sorry, sir," another voice was saying.
"Jen was getting ready for the dance, so I decided to wander around and explore Monster Academy.
I didn't think I'd get lost."
Waldo looked at Ben. "That must be Jen's date," he said. "The human."
Ben nodded.
"It's fine," Mr. Freaky said to the boy. "I'm just glad I found you.
It's not a good idea to have a human wandering around alone.
You might scare one of the monsters."
"Mr. Freaky, help!" Ben shouted, "We're trapped in the science lab!"
"Let us out!" Waldo pounded on the door. "We're locked in!"
Mr. Freaky didn't seem to hear them.
"This will be a wonderful dance, young man," the principal was saying.
"I think you're going to enjoy dancing with our monster students.
And there's even another human here tonight—Mrs. Hubbletree, the mayor's wife!"
A moment later the principal's voice faded down the hallway.
"Help! We're trapped!" yelled Ben again. But Mr. Freaky was gone.
Ben turned to Waldo in disbelief. "Why didn't he hear us?
He went right past the door!"
Waldo slapped his forehead. "I forgot," he said.
"We could yell all night long, as loud as we can, and nobody would hear us."
"Huh?" said Ben. "What are you talking about?"
"Mr. Creepy, the science teacher, made the lab soundproof," Waldo explained.
"He used a magic spell that keeps sound in.
We can hear what's going on outside, but nobody outside can hear what's going on in here."
"Why not?" asked Ben.
Waldo looked sheepish. "Last year I was doing an experiment, and I caused a big explosion.
Nobody got hurt, but the explosion disturbed students who were taking the GMAT.
You know, the General Monster Assessment Test that we have to take every spring.
Mr. Freaky was really upset, so he asked Mr. Creepy to make the science lab soundproof."
Ben blinked in disbelief. "That means we're stuck in here forever?"
Waldo shrugged. "Or at least until someone comes to look for us."
He patted Ben on the arm.
"Don't worry. Our parents will probably start worrying about us by midnight.
And we'll definitely be out of here by Monday morning.
That's when Mr. Creepy comes back to work."
"Monday morning?" Ben echoed. He couldn't believe this was happening.
It had taken all of his courage to ask Winnie to the dance.
Now he was stuck in a science lab with Waldo, and he was going to miss the whole thing!
In the gym at Monster Academy, the skeleton Boneyard Brass Band played on and on.
The sounds drifted faintly toward the science lab.
"I bet Winnie is dancing right now," Ben muttered to Waldo.
"I bet she stopped looking for me, and now she's having fun with some other monster."
He sighed. "I just hope it's not one of the football players.
Or that troll who wears ties to school all the time."
"I'll tell you what I want to know."
Waldo stood up and went to look at his experiment again.
"I want to know who tried to ruin my talk potion."
"It was probably the same monster who locked us in here," Ben replied.
"That same idiot who—"
Just then the door flew open.
"Mr. Creepy!" Waldo burst out.
"It's Friday night! What are you doing here?"
The teacher stared at the two boys in surprise.
"I'm a chaperone at the dance. What are you two doing here?"
"Somebody locked us in," Waldo explained quickly.
"Oh, and by the way, someone also tried to ruin my talk potion."
"What?" said Mr. Creepy. He strode to the back of the lab.
"Who would do that?"
Ben didn't wait to hear Waldo's answer.
"Thanks, Mr. Creepy!" he shouted. "See you later!"
He raced down the hall toward the gym.
Inside the big room, the lights were dim. Ben peered around for Winnie.
"I hope she didn't leave," he thought.
"Waldo!" cried Gaby as Waldo rushed into the gym behind Ben.
"Where were you two? I was so worried."
"Sorry," said Waldo. "Somebody trapped us inside the lab."
"That's awful!" said Gaby. "I wonder who . . ."
Just then the band started playing a new song, and her eyes lit up.
"Come on!" she said, grabbing Waldo's hand. "You're here now. Let's dance."
Gaby and Waldo hurried off.
Ben scanned the dance floor for Winnie, but he still didn't see her anywhere.
"Whoa!" cried a voice.
Ben spun around just in time to see a human kid slip and fall.
Jen, the blob, helped him up.
"Sorry, Dave," said Jen. "My slime trail can be pretty slippery."
"That's okay, Jen," said Dave with a grin.
"I'll just watch where I step!"
As Jen and Dave danced, Ben looked around for Winnie again.
He saw Mr. Freaky dancing with a large, red-haired woman.
"I'm glad you're enjoying yourself, Mrs. Hubbletree."
Mr. Freaky sounded slightly out of breath.
"I'm having a great time!" replied Mrs. Hubbletree.
"Thanks again for inviting Mr. Hubbletree and me.
Unfortunately, my husband doesn't like dancing."
Ben floated past the principal and Mrs. Hubbletree.
And then, at last, he found Winnie.
Her dark hair was long and loose, and she was wearing a beautiful black dress.
"She's dancing with Zork!" Ben realized with a pang.
His heart sank as the scaly green monster whispered something in Winnie's ear, and she burst out laughing.
When the song ended, Winnie said something to Zork, who then hurried off.
Ben shot over to her. "Winnie! You'll never believe . . ."
His words trailed off when he saw the look on her face.
"Where were you?" she asked in a low tone. "I looked everywhere."
"I'm so sorry." Ben tried to explain again.
"I got here early, while you were getting changed for the dance.
And then Waldo wanted to show me his new experiment."
His chuckle sounded too loud, even to his own ears.
"This is unbelievable, but we got locked inside the science lab."
"What?"
He grinned at her. "Crazy, right?"
Winnie stared at him without smiling back. "You're a ghost, Ben.
If you were locked inside the lab, why didn't you just float out through the walls?"
Ben winced. "I . . . um . . ."
"I thought you wanted to go to the dance with me," Winnie said. She wasn't looking at Ben.
"I thought you actually liked me."
"I did," said Ben. "I mean, I do!
But then we got trapped in the lab, and . . ." Ben suddenly had an idea.
"Read my thoughts, Winnie. You'll see that I'm telling the truth!"
She shook her head. "I told you before, Ben.
I can read minds only sometimes.
Other times, especially when I'm upset, I can't read them at all.
So I have no idea what you're thinking right now."
Ben sighed. "I'm really sorry. I wish you'd believe me.
Can I get you anything?"
"Thank you," she replied. "But Zork is bringing me some iced sludge."
Ben looked at her pleadingly.
"I'm supposed to be your date tonight, Winnie.
Can't we just, I don't know, start over or something?"
Just then Zork appeared with two cups of iced sludge.
"Hey, Ben," said Zork.
"Great dance, huh?" He handed one of the cups to Winnie.
"Oh yeah," said Ben, forcing a laugh. "I'm having a blast."
The Boneyard Brass Band was playing "The Creature Conga," but Ben didn't feel like joining in.
He floated to a corner and watched the line of monsters go by.
He was miserable, while everyone else seemed to be having a great time.
Gaby and Waldo danced past and waved happily at Ben.
The next time they passed Ben, Waldo broke out of the line.
"Where's Winnie?" he asked.
Ben sighed. "She's mad at me.
I tried to explain everything to her, but she thought I was lying."
"Oh, man," said Waldo. "It's my fault for asking you to come to the lab.
Do you want me to cast a love spell on Winnie?
I could run home and get my spell book."
Ben shook his head. "No, thanks."
He remembered what had happened the last time Waldo cast a love spell.
Plus it seemed wrong to do that to Winnie.
"Okay," said Waldo. "Let me know if you change your mind.
I'm really sorry." The wizard headed back to the dance floor while Ben grabbed a slug cupcake.
Then he found a different corner to sit in.
As the skeleton band started playing a new song, Ben noticed something strange—purple fog spreading through the gym.
A few monsters had stopped dancing to stare at it.
"Cool!" said Mog.
"That fog is pretty!" said a girl skeleton.
"Just like you," replied the ghoul she was dancing with.
"That's odd," Ben thought as more fog seeped into the gymnasium.
"It looks like the purple fog from the science lab."
Soon monsters started to cough, and the band stopped playing.
"Everything is totally under control!" shouted Mr. Freaky.
The principal ran around the gymnasium, opening windows.
"I'm not sure what this fog is—probably just part of the decorations.
We'll get it cleared out in a moment! Oh, I hope Miss Bungle gets better soon.
I can barely run this school without her!"
After a few minutes, the fog cleared.
Bones rattled as the skeleton band started playing again.
Across the room Ben saw Winnie start dancing with Zork again.
"I'm out of here," he decided, heading for the exit.
"What a miserable night," he thought.
He could forget about ever dancing with Winnie—she was barely speaking to him now.
During homeroom on Monday, Winnie didn't look at Ben.
He thought about trying to explain things again, but suddenly Mr. Freaky's voice blared over the loudspeaker.
"Attention, students. We will have a short assembly this morning."
"Uh-oh," a few kids murmured.
Ben wondered what the assembly was about.
Maybe something about the dance . . . the purple fog?
It could even be about what happened in the science lab with Waldo's experiment.
Students filed into the auditorium, and Mr. Freaky stepped up to the microphone.
"Good morning, everyone. The Monster Mash dance was a terrific success."
Around Ben, students clapped and cheered.
"As you know," Mr. Freaky continued, "the mayor's wife, Mrs. Hubbletree, was at the dance.
She had a wonderful time!
In fact, she thinks the students of People Place should take a field trip to visit us.
That way, more humans can get to know monsters.
Maybe they won't be so scared of us anymore."
A goblin looked worried.
"You mean, a whole bunch of humans will come to Monster Academy at once?"
"Yes," replied Mr. Freaky.
A troll shivered. "Scary!"
"Dave is a human," Jen reminded everyone. "He's not scary at all."
"Now, students." Mr. Freaky held up his hands. "This will be fun!
And if everything goes well, Mayor Hubbletree will consider taking down the fence that separates Monsterville and People Place.
Wouldn't that be wonderful?"
The students clapped politely, but Ben could tell that a few were nervous.
"We do need to prepare for our guests," Mr. Freaky added.
The principal spent the next few minutes explaining that the school had to be cleaned from top to bottom.
"No more slime trails or drool puddles," said Mr. Freaky.
"And I've heard that humans like something called pizza.
We'll see if we can order some of that.
"Finally," Mr. Freaky said, "we'll all need to act a bit more . . . humanlike."
Mog raised his hand. "What does that mean?"
"It means we should not do some of the things that we normally do," said Mr. Freaky.
"The zombies should try not to drool too much.
Witches and wizards—limit your mind reading and scary magic spells.
And to all you ghosts, please remember to avoid floating through walls in front of the humans.
It tends to scare them."
Ben felt hot all over.
"I couldn't do that even if I wanted to," he thought, shooting a glance at Winnie.
Over the next few days, everyone at Monster Academy was busy preparing for the visit by the humans.
Mr. Bog, the custodian, mopped up slime trails and drool puddles.
The student council made a large Welcome, People banner to hang in the lobby.
In the computer lab, Ben's class researched humans and tried to learn as much as they could.
"It says here that humans don't howl at the moon," said a werewolf.
He scratched his head. "That's weird."
"Yeah, well, check this out," replied a two-headed girl at another computer.
"Humans have only one brain."
Ben was very curious about the humans too, and looking forward to their visit.
But his mind was also on Winnie.
Ever since the dance, she'd been avoiding him.
In Cooking one morning, he looked over and saw her watching him.
She gave him a funny look and then turned away.
"She's still really mad at me," realized Ben.
He wondered how often she could read his thoughts.
Did she know how bad he felt?
Or how embarrassed he was that he couldn't float through walls like a real ghost?
On the morning of the humans' visit, everyone gathered in the school's lobby.
"The humans will be here any minute," said Mr. Freaky nervously.
"It looks like everything here is totally under—"
The principal gasped as he caught sight of Mog.
"What's wrong?" asked Mog.
Mr. Freaky started trembling. "You're covered in . . . purple spots!"
Mog looked down at himself.
"Oh no! You're right—I am covered in purple spots. What are they?"
Mr. Freaky shook his head gravely.
"I don't know. You must have some kind of monster flu."
Now Mog looked scared. "Do you really think it's a flu?"
"I'm afraid so," said Mr. Freaky.
"You should go to the nurse's office right away.
Please, Mog, the humans will be here soon, and I don't want them to see your spots."
"Mr. Freaky!" cried a witch. "Winnie's covered in purple spots too!"
Winnie shrieked and pointed at the other witch. "So are you!"
The other witch screamed as she looked down at herself.
Ben's eyes went wide as he looked around.
Purple spots were appearing on all the students—even on himself.
"Things are totally out of control!" cried Mr. Freaky.
He took out a handkerchief and blew his noses.
"I wish Miss Bungle were here. We have a full-blown epidemic in our school!"
"What's an epidemic?" asked Mog.
Waldo leaned toward him.
"It's when a disease spreads all over a place, like a school."
Mog looked at the purple spots on his hands and gulped.
"Is this disease . . . serious?"
Waldo shook his head. "I hope not."
"Everybody, go to the nurse's office!" said Mr. Freaky.
"We can't have human visitors while we have a monster flu epidemic.
When their bus arrives, I'll tell them we need to reschedule."
The principal started pacing. "This is terrible.
First Miss Bungle fell ill, and now all the students are sick too!"
Students started heading toward the nurse's office.
Ben was about to follow when he saw the bus from People Place pull up.
Curious about the humans, he ducked behind a tall plant to watch for a few minutes.
Mr. Freaky straightened his tie, took a deep breath, and headed outside.
Ben slipped out after him.
Mayor Hubbletree stepped off the bus with a grin. "Mr. Freaky!"
"Good morning, Mayor," said Mr. Freaky.
"I'm afraid I have some bad news."
Mayor Hubbletree had suddenly frozen.
He was staring curiously at Mr. Freaky. "What are all those purple spots?"
"Purple spots?" said Mr. Freaky, alarmed.
He looked down at his hands. "Oh dear. The epidemic is getting worse!"
Mayor Hubbletree took a step back.
"Epidemic? What's going on here, Freaky?"
"Nothing!" cried Mr. Freaky. "It's just a . . . minor illness, we think.
Everything is totally under control."
"It doesn't sound like it's under control. You just called it an epidemic."
Mayor Hubbletree glanced at the school building.
"I can't bring students into Monster Academy if you're all sick with some weird monster disease!"
"You're right," said Mr. Freaky.
"Maybe we should reschedule the field trip for next week."
"Are you kidding?" cried Mayor Hubbletree.
"I'm not rescheduling the field trip.
Whatever crazy monster illness you have in there, I want no part of it!
In fact, I'm sending over a health inspector to look into this epidemic.
My wife and Dave have been inside that building!"
Mr. Freaky wrung his hands, muttering to himself.
"This is terrible—I was really hoping the fence between Monsterville and People Place would be taken down."
Ben drew in a breath as the mayor folded his arms and scowled.
"Oh, that fence is coming down, all right," Mayor Hubbletree snapped.
"I'm going to replace it with an enormous concrete wall!"
Ben sat with his friends in the crowded hallway outside the nurse's office.
Everyone was talking about the epidemic.
"I wonder if we'll get to go home," a ghoul murmured.
"I hope we don't need shots," said a three-eyed monster.
Suddenly Mog shouted, "My purple spots are getting bigger!"
His girlfriend, Lilly, looked nervous.
"If those spots keep growing, your whole body will be purple."
"My spots are growing too," said a goblin. He looked around.
"Everyone's spots are growing!"
"This is awful!" cried Jen, jiggling nervously.
"What's happening to us?"
"What are you worried about?" asked the goblin.
"You were purple already!"
Ben looked at his own hands.
His spots were getting bigger and bigger too.
He looked at Waldo and Gaby. They were completely purple by now.
Mr. Freaky hurried down the hallway, his noses wiggling wildly.
"We have a serious problem," the principal announced.
His spots were growing as he spoke.
"Mayor Hubbletree is sending over a health inspector to look into this epidemic. He's very upset.
He plans to build a concrete wall between Monsterville and People Place.
I don't think he'll ever let his students visit us."
Ben and his friends exchanged looks.
He'd already told them about the concrete wall.
Mrs. Germ, the school nurse, came out of her office.
Usually she was large and blue. But by now she was large and purple.
"I can't find any information about this epidemic, Mr. Freaky," said the nurse.
"Monster flu usually causes green spots, not purple."
Mr. Freaky scratched his head. "What does that mean then?"
"It means that we don't know what this disease is," said the nurse.
"It must be more serious than we thought."
Everyone gasped. Mr. Freaky's noses wiggled more than ever.
"I'm placing Monster Academy under lockdown," continued Mrs. Germ.
"Until everyone is well, we have to be quarantined."
"What does quarantined mean?" Mog asked Waldo.
"It means we can't leave," said Waldo.
"That way we won't spread the disease."
Ben heard Winnie gasp nearby.
"Lockdown?" she echoed.
"I was going to practice broom flying after school today!
I have my flying test soon."
"Yeah! I have a violin lesson today," complained another monster.
"I wanted to go home and watch TV!"
Mr. Freaky held up a hand to silence everyone.
"This is nothing to worry about, students.
We'll try to turn this into something . . . fun."
"Fun?" repeated a skeleton. "Since when is living at school fun?"
The new cooking teacher strode over.
"The cafeteria trolls and I can cook a lovely dinner for everyone.
How does frog brain stew sound?"
Murmurs of excitement ran through hallway.
"After school I'll set up some games in the gym," said Mr. Gwarg, the PE teacher.
"Can we fly brooms in the gym too?" asked Winnie hopefully.
"No," said Mr. Freaky. "Unfortunately, Miss Bungle is still out sick."
"Oh," said Winnie in a small voice.
Then she murmured something else that Ben couldn't hear.
He stole a glance at her. "Poor Winnie," he thought.
She loved broom flying, and she couldn't wait to pass her flying test.
Once she got her license, she could fly all over Monsterville on her own.
He felt sorry for her, but he was glad to see that she was sitting with her friends and not with Zork.
"It seems that everyone feels well despite the spots," Mr. Freaky was saying.
"So I think you can all go to class."
The students groaned.
"When the school day is over, we'll have fun," Mr. Freaky promised.
"Now I must get back to my office to alert your parents about the quarantine."
"Attention, students." At the end of the day, Mr. Freaky's voice came over the loudspeaker again.
"We have set up activities throughout the school.
Please try to have some fun.
Even if we are all suffering from a terrible epidemic, things are still totally under control!"
The bell clanged, and students dashed into the hallways.
"I'm playing volleyball!" called out a fish monster, racing toward the gym.
A group of trolls, goblins, and skeletons raced after him.
Ben floated at the top of a stairwell.
"Maybe I should look for Winnie," he thought.
Maybe if he tried again to explain about the locked door, she would understand.
Maybe he could even tell her about how he couldn't float through walls like a—
"Oh! Ben! There you are." Suddenly Waldo was standing in front of him.
"We must solve this mystery," the wizard declared.
"What mystery?" asked Ben.
Waldo adjusted his glasses.
"The mystery of who tried to ruin my talk potion."
Ben nodded slowly. "There are definitely some weird things happening at this school."
"It can't be just a coincidence," said Waldo.
"First purple fog filled the gym during the Monster Mash dance.
And now we've all turned purple!"
"I don't know, Waldo," Ben said. "The whole school is under quarantine.
Plus, we're just kids. So how can we solve the mystery at Monster Academy?"
"I don't know yet," Waldo admitted.
"But what if it was my potion that caused the fog during the dance?"
His glasses slipped down his nose, and he pushed them back up.
"Maybe the fog from the lab traveled through the air vents to the gymnasium."
"Could be," Ben murmured, remembering the fog inside the lab.
"So you realize what this means, right?" said Waldo.
"The epidemic is all my fault!"
"It's not your fault, Waldo," Ben replied.
"If the flu was caused by the fog from the lab, then it's someone else's fault—the monster who ruined your experiment."
Waldo nodded, looking a little relieved. "Maybe you're right.
But sometime soon Mr. Freaky or the nurse will trace the flu back to the lab.
And then I'm in big trouble."
"Well, maybe we can try to find out who tampered with your experiment," said Ben.
"We could find the guilty monster and make him or her confess."
"That's what I was thinking too," said Waldo.
"First we have to figure out what we know—all the facts.
Then we can use those facts to figure out who our culprit is.
We know that there was fog in the lab."
"Another fact is that someone removed the hoses from your test tubes," Ben added.
"And we also know that purple fog filled the gym during the dance."
"Good," said Waldo.
"Here are some more things we know: both my potion and the fog were purple.
And now everybody in Monster Academy is purple."
"And nobody was sick before the dance," added Ben.
Suddenly Waldo's eyes lit up. "Actually, that's not true!
Miss Bungle has been sick since before the dance—before my potion caused that fog."
"You're right," said Ben thoughtfully. "I forgot about that.
Hey! Maybe your potion didn't cause this epidemic at all!"
Just then they heard voices.
They looked over the railing and saw Mr. Freaky at the bottom of the stairs.
The principal was with a tall human in a white coverall.
The man was wearing a mask and carrying a clipboard.
"That man must be the health inspector from People Place," Ben whispered.
"So you have no idea how this epidemic started?" the health inspector said to Mr. Freaky.
"No," said Mr. Freaky, wringing his hands.
"But trust me—I will find out what caused it.
Mayor Hubbletree has nothing to worry about.
Everything in Monster Academy is totally under control."
The health inspector sounded doubtful.
"It doesn't appear that things are totally under control here.
Everybody is purple. Nobody in People Place is purple.
Now, that's a place where things are totally under control."
Mr. Freaky took out his handkerchief and blew his noses.
"When did the epidemic start?" asked the health inspector.
"Who was the first person, er, monster to get sick?"
Mr. Freaky put away the handkerchief. "The first monster? Hmm, let's see . . .
That would be Miss Bungle, our broom-flying instructor."
Ben and Waldo looked at each other and smiled proudly.
The two of them had just remembered this fact.
"And where is she?" asked the health inspector.
"She's at home," said Mr. Freaky.
The health inspector made a note on his clipboard.
"Show me the cafeteria.
A lot of health problems occur where food is prepared.
I want to see what you monsters are cooking."
"Of course," said Mr. Freaky. "Follow me."
Waldo looked at Ben and grinned. "Whew!"
"I don't think you have anything to worry about, Waldo," said Ben.
"The health inspector will figure out what caused the epidemic, and then someone will find a cure." Ben sighed.
"I still have a problem though. Winnie's still mad at me."
"I'll help you explain things to her," Waldo offered.
"Come on, let's go find her right now."
Ben and Waldo went downstairs to look for Winnie.
As they passed through the lobby, a door opened, and in walked Miss Bungle!
The ogre who worked in the main office rushed into the lobby.
"Miss Bungle! You can't enter the building!
Monster Academy is under quarantine!"
The broom-flying teacher halted.
She looked quizzically at the office ogre, and then at Ben and Waldo.
"Why are you all . . . purple?"
"There's an epidemic. And a quarantine!" the ogre repeated.
"You have to leave at once!"
Waldo stared at Miss Bungle. "Wait a second," he murmured.
"Why are you surprised that we're all purple?
You've been sick with the flu all week. Didn't you turn purple too?"
Miss Bungle shook her head.
"No, I just had a minor case of monster flu—you know, sore throat, achy joints, and small green spots."
"You had green spots?" Waldo echoed, and Ben gulped.
If Miss Bungle hadn't turned purple, then her sickness was different.
That meant Waldo's talk potion could have caused the epidemic after all.
