Mr. Freaky hurried into the lobby with the health inspector.
The principal beamed when he saw Miss Bungle. "I thought you were still ill!"
"I'm feeling better now," said Miss Bungle.
"I just stopped by to check on a few things. What is this purple epidemic?"
Mr. Freaky shook his head. "We don't know. I assumed you had it too."
She shook her head. "No."
"Miss Bungle!" the office ogre commanded. "You must leave at once!"
The health inspector narrowed his eyes.
"This is the teacher who's been out sick?"
"Yes." Mr. Freaky introduced her.
"You're not purple," the inspector said to Miss Bungle in a suspicious tone.
While the man scribbled on his clipboard, Ben turned toward Waldo.
"Come on!" he whispered.
They found a quiet spot in the hallway.
"Now we know my talk potion caused the epidemic," Waldo moaned.
"We have to find out who tried to ruin my experiment!
And we need a cure for this disease before it spreads to People Place."
Waldo glanced at the health inspector.
"The people are obviously worried about it.
Oh!" Waldo's glasses flew off his face. "I just thought of something!"
Ben was startled. "What?"
Waldo picked up his glasses and put them back on.
"There were two humans at the dance, remember?
And neither turned purple. So maybe . . ."
Just then the health inspector's phone rang.
"Hello? Oh no! That's terrible news.
Yes, sir. I'll get out of here right away. I'll meet you at the hospital."
The health inspector put the phone back in his pocket and rushed for the doorway.
"I can't stay here any longer," he called over his shoulder.
"Two people have turned purple!"
Ben sighed. "Now Mrs. Hubbletree and Dave, Jen's date, are purple too.
Sorry, Waldo, but your talk potion definitely caused this epidemic."
Waldo slumped. "You're right, Ben."
Mr. Icky's voice came over the loudspeaker.
"Time for dinner! Everyone, please report to the cafeteria.
We have frog brain stew, fried caterpillars, and pond scum soup."
Ben and Waldo walked down the crowded hallway.
"This is fun!" said a ghoul. "I love lockdowns!"
"Me too!" said a troll. "I can't wait to eat!"
Ben and Waldo arrived in the cafeteria and waited in line for their food.
"It smells good in here," said Ben.
Waldo sniffed. "Yeah, it does." He looked around.
A lot of monsters were already eating.
"You know what, Ben? It feels good in here too."
"What do you mean?" asked Ben.
"Look around," said Waldo. "Do you notice anything?"
Ben gazed at the tables.
"Watch this!" called a werewolf.
He held one of his nostrils shut and shot a fried caterpillar out of the other one.
His friends laughed hysterically.
Ben looked back at Waldo. "I don't notice anything unusual."
"Exactly!" said Waldo. "Everyone is acting as they normally do.
I don't think this is an epidemic at all.
We're not sick. We're just . . . purple."
Ben nodded. "I do feel fine." He thought for a moment.
"Okay, so we don't have to worry about a cure.
We just need to figure out who ruined your experiment."
"The school was pretty empty when we went to the lab," Waldo thought aloud.
"The witches on the dance committee were in the restroom upstairs getting ready.
The only monster we saw in the hallway was Jen."
Waldo gasped. "It could have been her, or . . . Maybe it was her date, Dave!"
"Maybe," said Ben. "He did get lost in the building."
Ben remembered how Mr. Creepy had suddenly appeared.
"What about the science teacher?"
Waldo shook his head. "No way Mr. Creepy would be involved."
He looked around the cafeteria. "It's too bad Monster Academy is in lockdown.
I wish we could sneak out to People Place and question Dave."
Ben smiled. "Actually, I might be able to go and question him.
Watch this." Concentrating, Ben moved his hand toward the wall.
Just as his hand reached the wall, light sparkled, and Ben's hand passed right through the wall!
Waldo's eyes went wide. "Wow!"
"I finally figured out how to do it," said Ben proudly.
"I'll sneak out, go to the hospital in People Place, and see what I can find out."
"What about the flu?" said Waldo. "You could spread it."
Ben shrugged. "I think it's a risk I have to take."
He floated toward the school's lobby.
First he tried opening the doors, but the office ogre had locked them tightly.
Ben glanced around. And then, sure that nobody was watching, he turned back to the doors and floated right through them.
After a few tries, Ben managed to slip through the walls of People Place Hospital.
Down a corridor he spotted the mayor talking with news reporters.
They all stood outside two hospital rooms that were sealed shut.
Danger signs hung on the doors.
"Mayor Hubbletree," said a reporter.
"Is it true that this disease started with the monsters?"
"Yes," said the mayor.
"But don't worry. I'm building a large wall between People Place and Monsterville."
"How is Mrs. Hubbletree?" asked another reporter.
"Dave and my wife are both in very serious condition," said the mayor gravely. "This is a very—"
Just then the door of one room flew open.
Mrs. Hubbletree stood there in a hospital gown.
She glowered at her husband. "I'm not sick!"
She held out her purple arms. "In fact, I like being purple!
It reminds me of the wonderful time I had at the Monster Mash dance."
Dave appeared in the second doorway.
"I feel fine too! I don't know why I'm in this dumb hospital."
The reporters' cameras flashed, and they all began shouting questions.
The mayor waved his arms in a panic.
"Get back in that room at once! You're—"
"They probably do feel fine!" Ben blurted out.
Everyone turned and gasped.
"A ghost!" cried a reporter.
"Nobody's sick," said Ben.
"The epidemic was caused by a talk potion my friend was making.
Somebody tampered with it and—"
"It was me!" shouted Dave.
"What?" Mayor Hubbletree spun around.
"I didn't mean to!" Dave's words rushed out.
"I was curious about monsters, so I wandered around Monster Academy.
I saw the experiment and started playing around with the test tubes.
I didn't want to get in trouble.
So I locked that ghost and a wizard in the lab and then ran back toward the gym.
But I got lost and . . ."
As Dave continued to talk, Mrs. Hubbletree started talking too.
"Monster Academy is absolutely lovely," she said.
"Everyone there is so interesting!"
Both patients chattered on. Suddenly Ben felt a strong urge to talk.
"I'm so glad you guys liked Monster Academy," he said.
"I love it there!" Ben rambled on and on.
"Huh?" Mayor Hubbletree scratched his head.
A little while later, Ben got out of a long car in front of Monster Academy.
He was still chattering away about Monster Academy.
Ben was followed by Dave, who was talking about Jen.
Mayor and Mrs. Hubbletree climbed out next.
Mrs. Hubbletree was telling the mayor about her favorite dance moves.
When they opened the school doors, they heard a roar of voices.
Everybody inside was talking too!
"The first monsters arrived in 1493," said Mr. Freaky.
"My family took a broom-flying trip across France last summer," said a witch to nobody in particular.
"Ahem!" Mayor Hubbletree cleared his throat loudly.
Mr. Freaky looked stunned for a second, and then he beamed.
"Mayor Hubbletree! I'm so glad you're here.
Do you know anything about monster history?"
Mr. Freaky and other monsters started talking again.
"Not now, Freaky," said the mayor, looking uncomfortable.
"I . . . I owe you an apology.
I learned that Dave accidentally caused the epidemic."
"And that's not all," said Mrs. Hubbletree, giving her husband a stern look.
The mayor grinned sheepishly.
"No one is really sick at all. My wife says she feels fine. So does Dave."
"We all feel fine too," said Mr. Freaky. "We're talkative but fine."
"I'm not going to put up that concrete wall," said the mayor.
"Wonderful!" said Mr. Freaky. "Now I really must tell you about . . ."
Dave ran over to Jen. "Look! I'm purple!"
Jen laughed. "We match!"
Ben found Waldo in the crowd. "Guess what, buddy—your talk potion works!"
"Better late than never," said Waldo with a grin.
Then he started talking about his next experiment.
"Ben! I'm sorry I didn't believe you."
Winnie was hurrying toward him, talking fast.
"I was just disappointed about the dance."
She lowered her voice and flashed him a sympathetic smile.
"And I read your mind about the walls.
I didn't know you couldn't float through them."
"Well, now I can do it!" boasted Ben.
"At least some of the time.
I kept trying to talk to you after the dance, Winnie, but I was too embarrassed, I guess.
Now I can talk—and talk and talk! Do you have plans for Saturday night?"
"Yes, I do," said Winnie.
"Oh," said Ben, disappointed.
Winnie laughed. "I have plans with you. Let's see a movie."
Ben beamed. "That sounds great!"
A few minutes later, Waldo's potion began to wear off. The talking stopped.
Mrs. Hubbletree, Dave, and all the monsters returned to their normal colors.
Everyone was happy.
Well, almost everyone.
Mrs. Hubbletree frowned. "I liked being purple!"
Ben floated through the crowded auditorium at Monster Academy.
He was looking for Winnie so they could sit together at the morning assembly.
Boomph! He tried to float through a row of chairs, but instead he slammed into something hard.
"Hey! Watch it!" a werewolf growled.
"Sorry," said Ben. "I'm still working on my floating technique."
He headed toward the front of the room.
"Ben!" a voice called. Gaby waved him over. "Over here! Sit with me!"
Ben dropped into the seat next to the giant.
"Hey, Gaby," he said. "How's it going? Have you seen Winnie anywhere?"
"No, but maybe—" Before Gaby could finish, Mr. Freaky hurried onto the stage.
His noses were wiggling wildly.
"Good morning, everyone!" said the Monster Academy principal.
"Today is a very exciting day.
The humans from People Place will be arriving very soon."
"We're already here!" shouted someone from the crowd.
Ben turned around and saw three humans in the back row.
They were wearing matching black jackets.
Suddenly one of the humans turned into a large, furry monster.
Most of the students laughed, but Ben was confused.
"What's going on?" he asked Gaby.
"They're the Doppel Gang," she explained.
"Moe, Larry, and Carly. They're doppelgangers."
"Huh?" Ben knew that doppelgangers usually looked like humans.
He'd also heard that they could make themselves look like anyone—or anything—they wanted.
Plus, they had some magical abilities.
"The gang loves to play pranks," said Gaby. "They're really funny."
"Moe!" Mr. Freaky snapped. "Stop that at once!"
Moe quickly returned to his human form. "Sorry, Mr. Freaky."
"I need everyone to behave today," said Mr. Freaky.
"We must not scare the humans."
He looked at Miss Bungle, who was sitting in the front row with some other teachers.
"Is the broom flying squad ready for the flyover?"
"Oh yes." The broom flying teacher beamed.
"All of my best students are in the squad.
We're going to fly over the school to welcome our visitors.
It's going to be spectacular!"
"Of course," thought Ben.
"That's where Winnie is. She's getting ready for the flyover."
Miss Bungle was still talking. "The broom flyers are very excited to—"
A roar of laughter filled the auditorium.
The doppelgangers were making their eyes bulge out of their faces.
It looked as if invisible hands were squeezing their heads.
Mr. Freaky looked up to see what everyone was laughing at.
The doppelgangers immediately returned to their normal appearances.
Ben heard a couple of monsters still giggling quietly.
He was laughing too—he couldn't help himself.
Gaby was right—the Doppel Gang was pretty funny.
Mr. Freaky turned his attention back to Miss Bungle.
This time the Doppel Gang made themselves look like Mr. Freaky.
Ben and the other students laughed hysterically as the three Mr. Freakys wiggled their noses and danced.
Mr. Freaky looked annoyed. "What is so funny?" he demanded.
Nobody answered.
"This visit must go well, students!" Mr. Freaky warned them.
"If it doesn't, Mayor Hubbletree will be very angry.
He almost bulldozed our school a couple of weeks ago.
Who knows what he'll do if there are any problems today!"
Mr. Freaky glanced at Mr. Gwarg.
"What time is it?" the principal asked the gym teacher.
As Mr. Gwarg looked at his watch, the Doppel Gang turned into three enormous noses.
The auditorium seemed to shake with laughter.
Mr. Freaky looked up, and everyone stopped laughing.
The Doppel Gang looked like their usual selves again.
"Why does everybody keep laughing?" asked the principal.
Mr. Gwarg stood up and turned around to glare at the students, his hands on his hips.
"I don't know, Mr. Freaky. But I don't like it."
He glared at the students for another moment and then looked at his watch. "It's 9:40, sir."
"Good," said Mr. Freaky.
"Now, students, the humans should be here in about 30 minutes.
We have a lot of fun events planned for our guests.
Waldo Wizz will present a wonderful new experiment in the science lab.
We'll eat a delicious lunch together.
And our two schools will play each other in soccer.
So please behave today, and remember: don't scare the humans!"
The principal dismissed the students, and everyone headed for the school lobby to wait for the humans to arrive.
Ben floated through the crowded hallway.
"I wonder where the broom flyers are," he thought.
"I want to wish Winnie good luck.
She'll probably get to do some cool tricks."
He spotted Miss Bungle talking to a group of flying students.
"Oh, good. It's the broom flying squad," thought Ben.
He shot toward the group. But then he stopped.
Holding their brooms were four witches and two goblins.
But there was no Winnie.
Ben scratched his head. "Where is she?" he wondered.
Ben stared at the broom flying squad in confusion.
"Winnie is one of the best flyers at Monster Academy," he thought.
"So why isn't she with the other flyers?"
Ben hoped she wasn't at home, sick today.
It would be a shame for her to miss such a big day—the humans' first visit to Monster Academy.
Ben and Winnie had been dating for a few weeks.
Their first date was to a horror movie about ghosts who lived in a house haunted by people.
After the movie they got some moldy ice cream and went for a walk in the park.
It had been a lot of fun, and Ben really liked Winnie.
Ben drifted through the lobby until he found Gaby again.
"I'd thought Winnie would be with the broom flying squad," he said.
"But she's not with them. I'm not sure where . . ."
He let his words trail off as he realized that Gaby's eyes were darting all over the hallway.
She wasn't really listening to him.
"Hmm. . . ? What did you say?" Gaby murmured.
"You didn't find Winnie?" Gaby was still searching the hallway.
"I'm sure she'll show up soon, Ben.
I'm looking for someone too. Have you seen Deb anywhere?"
"Who's Deb?" Ben asked.
"A ghoul," said Gaby.
"She just started at Monster Academy last week, and I've heard she's super smart."
"Why are you looking for her?" asked Ben.
Gaby frowned. "Someone told me that she offered to help Waldo with his experiment demonstration today.
If you ask me, that's a ridiculous idea.
I mean, Waldo is the smartest kid in school. He doesn't need any—
Oh! There she is. Whew!" Gaby let out a big breath of relief.
Ben looked down the hallway.
At the other end, a pretty ghoul girl was getting something out of her locker.
"I guess that was just a rumor about Deb," Gaby said.
"Would it matter if Deb were helping Waldo?" Ben asked.
Gaby was acting pretty weird.
"Um, no. Of course not!" Gaby said quickly.
"But, like I said, Waldo's the smartest student at Monster Academy.
He doesn't need help from some new ghoul girl."
As Gaby went on about how smart Waldo was, Ben turned to hide his smile.
He knew now why Gaby was acting so weird. She was jealous—jealous of Deb!
Ben started floating through the halls again. Soon he spotted Mog.
"Hey, Mog!" Ben called to his friend. "Have you seen Winnie?"
Mog shook his head. "No. Have you seen Deb?"
"Deb?" Ben asked. Why was everybody suddenly looking for Deb?
"Yeah," said Mog. "She's this awesome new ghoul."
"I know who she is," said Ben. "She was at her locker a minute ago."
He glanced back at the row of lockers. "She's gone now, though."
Mog sighed dreamily. "She's like something out of my nightmares.
And I love nightmares."
Ben was surprised. "I thought you were dating Lilly."
"Nah," said Mog. "That was last week. This week I'm going out with Deb."
Ben shrugged. "I guess she could be in the science lab," he said.
"Gaby told me that Deb might help Waldo with his experiment today."
Mog raised his eyebrows.
"What do you mean, she 'might help Waldo with his experiment'?
You don't think Waldo likes her, do you?
They're just working together because they have to, right?"
"Whoa." Ben held up a hand to slow Mog down.
"Don't panic or anything. I'm not even sure they are working together.
It's just a rumor."
Mog still looked worried. "I'd better talk to Gaby myself.
I want to find out what's going on."
The monster stomped down the hallway toward Gaby.
Ben rolled his eyes. He couldn't believe everyone was so jealous about Deb.
"Hey, Jen!" Ben called to a purple blob.
"Hi, Ben!" said Jen, her body jiggling. "Isn't it wonderful?"
"The people's visit?" Ben asked. "Is that what you mean?"
"Yes," said Jen. "I can't wait to see Dave again.
I haven't seen him for three whole days! Do I look all right?"
Ben watched as Jen slowly spun around.
A pool of slime spread out on the floor around her.
"You look great," he said.
"Thanks!" said Jen.
"You haven't seen Winnie, have you?" asked Ben.
"She's probably with the broom flying squad," said Jen.
"They're planning a big flyover for when the people get here, aren't they?"
Ben sighed. "Yeah, I thought she would be with them too.
But I saw the squad a minute ago, and she wasn't with them."
Jen shrugged. "Maybe she was in the bathroom or tuning up her broom.
She might even be—"
"Hey, everybody!" An excited voice cut her off.
"The people are here!" shouted a goblin.
Ben rushed outside with the others to meet the humans.
The school bus from People Place was parked in front of the school.
"This is going to be so scary!" said a werewolf.
"I know!" said a fish monster. "I love being scared!"
Mr. Freaky was standing on the sidewalk near the school bus.
He turned around to warn the Monster Academy students again.
"Remember, monsters!" said the principal.
"I want you all to behave. No growling, fire breathing, or drooling!"
A zombie slowly reached up and wiped the drool from his mouth.
Ben hoped everyone would listen to Mr. Freaky for once, and the humans' visit would go smoothly.
He didn't want Mayor Hubbletree to be angry with monsters.
What if the mayor really did bulldoze Monster Academy?
Where would Ben go to school? He might never see Winnie again!
The door to the school bus opened, and Mayor Hubbletree stepped out.
Luckily the mayor appeared to be in a good mood.
"Good morning!" Mayor Hubbletree greeted the monsters.
"It's a beautiful day for a field trip."
He pumped Mr. Freaky's hand up and down.
"Don't you think so, Mr. Freaky?"
"Of course!" said Mr. Freaky. "Thanks for coming, Mayor Hubbletree.
We have a wonderful day planned—all kinds of fun and exciting events."
A thin woman holding a clipboard stepped off the bus.
"Excuse me," she murmured as she tried to slip by a large blob to greet Mr. Freaky.
Mayor Hubbletree introduced them.
"Mr. Freaky, this is Ms. Prim, the principal of People Place Middle School."
"Oh, hello!" said Mr. Freaky. He shook the woman's hand.
"I'm . . . um . . ." Ms. Prim cleared her throat.
"I'm very pleased to meet you."
A human boy peeked out the door of the bus next. He looked nervous too.
After a moment he stepped out, and then more students followed.
The students' eyes all went wide at the sight of the monsters.
Near Ben, a few monsters started whispering.
"People are so creepy," said a goblin.
"Yeah," agreed a purple monster. "They look so weird!"
For a few moments, nobody said anything.
Mayor Hubbletree looked at his watch. Mr. Freaky coughed nervously.
Then Jen called out, "Hi, Dave!"
Dave stepped out from the crowd of people and grinned. "Hi, Jen!"
All at once the Monster Academy cheerleaders began to cheer.
Welcome, welcome to our school! We know you'll find it really cool!
We hope before the day is done, You'll be friends with everyone!
Yay!
The cheerleaders shook their pom-poms.
Several of them formed a pyramid, while others did flips in the air.
The spectacle ended with an octopus monster doing an eight-armed split.
Everyone—monsters and humans—whistled and cheered. Mr. Freaky was beaming.
Mayor Hubbletree clapped him on the back.
"This is very impressive stuff, Freaky!"
Suddenly—zoom!
"Whoa!" Ben glanced eagerly toward the sky.
It was time for Winnie's performance in the flyover.
The broom flying squad shot through the air, dropping black and orange confetti.
They did a wide loop, and then swooped back down, zigzagging.
"Whoa!" cried the students, human and monster. "Awesome!"
The broom flyers were now weaving in and out of one another.
"How do they do that?" asked a human boy.
"They're going to crash!" cried a human girl.
But the flyers didn't crash.
Instead they sailed high above the school, flying up and down, faster and faster, doing loops and figure eights.
"These flyers are amazing, Freaky," said Mayor Hubbletree.
"Are you sure this is safe?" asked Ms. Prim.
"Oh yes," said the principal. "You can relax, Ms. Prim.
Monster Academy has the best broom-flying teacher around.
And the students in that squad are the best flyers at our school."
While the rest of the crowd cheered and clapped, Ben watched silently.
The flyers were amazing, but something was wrong.
Winnie wasn't with them.
"This doesn't make sense," thought Ben.
"Why isn't Winnie flying with the squad?"
"This is quite a welcome, Freaky!" Mayor Hubbletree declared.
Mr. Freaky flushed with delight.
"Thank you, Mayor. We wanted to make sure you humans felt at home."
The cheerleaders formed another pyramid.
An octopus monster leaped to the top of the pyramid and then held out her arms.
Poof! A large banner appeared in front of the octopus monster.
Light sparkled across the surface of the banner, and then letters began magically spelling out something.
"Oh yes, Freaky," Ben heard Mayor Hubbletree say.
"We certainly feel welcome at Monster Academy.
I have to admit, I was mistaken about monsters. I never should have—"
Suddenly a gasp rose from the students.
Written across the banner were the words: "We Eat People!"
"'We . . . eat . . .'" Mayor Hubbletree was reading the cheerleaders' banner out loud.
Suddenly his face clouded, and he spun around to face Mr. Freaky.
"People? You eat people?"
"Eek!" cried a human girl. "The monsters are going to eat us!"
"Run for your lives!" cried a human boy.
The human kids started pushing and shoving to get back to their bus.
Then—whoosh! The banner burst into flames.
People and monsters screamed.
"Everyone, settle down!" cried Mr. Freaky.
He pulled out a handkerchief and blew his noses.
"Everything is totally under control!"
Mayor Hubbletree glared at him. "Is this your idea of a joke, Freaky?"
The head cheerleader rushed over. "We're so sorry, Mr. Freaky.
The banner wasn't supposed to say, 'We Eat People!'
It was supposed to say, 'Welcome, People!'"
Loud laughter rang out. Ben turned and saw it was coming from the Doppel Gang.
All three of the doppelgangers were bent over, laughing hysterically.
Mr. Freaky stalked over to them. "It was you three, wasn't it?
You changed the message on the banner and then made it burst into flames!"
The Doppel Gang stopped laughing.
"No way!" cried Moe. "We didn't cause the fire!"
"Yeah, that wasn't us!" added Carly.
"I don't believe you," said Mr. Freaky.
"Mr. Gwarg, please escort the Doppel Gang to my office.
Ask the office ogre to call their parents."
Mr. Gwarg led the doppelgangers back into the school building.
Mr. Freaky looked at the mayor and Ms. Prim, and grinned sheepishly.
"Sorry about that. Unfortunately, we have some students here at Monster Academy who like to play pranks.
I can assure you, Mayor Hubbletree, nobody is going to get eaten."
Mayor Hubbletree made some grumbling noises.
Ms. Prim spoke up. "Well then!" she said brightly.
"Let's not let a couple of bad apples spoil our day.
I think this field trip is going to be lovely."
Mr. Freaky suddenly clapped his hands in delight.
"Oh, I love bad apples! Especially when they get brown and mushy.
And I love to see a small wormhole.
That's how I know there's a tasty treat inside!"
Ms. Prim wrinkled her nose.
"What's next, Freaky?" asked Mayor Hubbletree.
"Let's get this field trip started."
Just then Ben noticed something out of the corner of his eye.
A human girl darted into the school.
She was wearing a hoodie with a green skull on the back.
A witch had spotted her too. She went over to tap Mr. Freaky on the arm.
"Excuse me? Mr. Freaky? I think a human girl just ran into the school."
"Are you sure?" asked Mr. Freaky.
"Ms. Prim!" Mayor Hubbletree ordered.
"Find out who it was! This is a dangerous situation."
Ms. Prim started calling out students' names.
"Don't worry, Mayor," said Mr. Freaky.
"Monster Academy is perfectly safe."
"Hmph!" said Mayor Hubbletree.
Ms. Prim came back, looking at her clipboard and muttering to herself.
"Well?" said the mayor. "Who's missing? Who ran into the school?"
Ms. Prim looked at him. "Not one of our students. They're all right here."
"That witch must be imagining things, Freaky," said Mayor Hubbletree.
"Now, what are we doing first?"
"Our eighth-grade president, Waldo Wizz, has a magnificent science experiment planned," said Mr. Freaky.
"Everybody, follow me to the science lab!"
As everyone headed into the school, Ben wondered again about the mystery girl.
He didn't want to get anyone in trouble, but he'd seen her too.
Who was she, and why did she run into the school?
The human kids were whispering to each other.
"I hope the monsters don't turn us into frogs or something."
"Hey!" said a frog monster. "What's wrong with frogs?"
"Oh!" The boy laughed nervously. "Um, nothing."
The frog monster laughed. "I'm just kidding!"
"Actually, we do need to be careful here," said Dave.
He was walking next to Jen.
"Last time I was in the science lab, I turned purple."
"And whose fault was that?" asked Jen, giggling.
Dave grinned. "Mine!"
When the group got upstairs, Mr. Creepy, the science teacher, hurried ahead to open the lab.
Ben saw him jiggle the door handle a few times.
"That's strange," said Mr. Creepy. "The door is locked."
He reached into his pocket. "Oops. I don't have my key with me."
He knocked on the door. "Waldo, are you in there? Open up!"
There was no answer.
"I hope nothing's wrong," Gaby murmured.
Ben made his way to the door. "Don't worry, everyone.
I'll float through the door and unlock it from inside."
Concentrating, Ben slowly pushed his head through the door.
He was about to pull the rest of his body through when something made him freeze.
Broken glass and burned hoses covered the floor.
Green liquid formed a large puddle.
And lying unconscious in the middle of it was Waldo!
"Oh no!" cried Ben. "Something happened to Waldo!"
He tried to continue floating through the door of the science lab, but he was stuck.
Ben cringed from embarrassment.
Here he was—stuck halfway through a door—with everybody looking at him!
"What happened to Waldo?" called Mr. Freaky.
Ben tried to answer, but the science lab was soundproof.
So no one could hear Ben yelling back to Mr. Freaky.
Then suddenly—crash! The door was ripped off its hinges, and Gaby stormed into the lab.
Ben landed hard on the floor.
"Waldo!" Gaby cried. "What happened to you? Waldo, please wake up!"
Mr. Freaky and the human adults rushed into the room.
"Someone get the school nurse!" Mr. Freaky shouted.
Mog and some other students stood in the doorway.
Minutes later the nurse slipped through the crowd.
"Excuse me, dear," she said to Gaby.
Gaby backed away as Mrs. Germ checked Waldo's pulse.
The nurse opened one of Waldo's eyes and shined a light in it.
"He'll be fine," she declared.
Ben was relieved that Waldo was okay.
He was also relieved that nobody was talking about how he'd gotten stuck in the door.
Waldo opened his eyes and moaned. "Oh . . . What's going on? Where am I?"
"You're in the science lab," said Mr. Freaky.
"Can you tell us what happened to you?"
Waldo sat up and rubbed his head.
"The last thing I remember, I was standing in here, waiting for Deb."
"Deb?" cried Mog and Gaby at the same time.
"Um, yeah," said Waldo. "She offered to help me with the experiment."
He glanced at the mess on the floor and sighed.
"I guess my experiment is ruined."
"Oh, Waldo," Gaby gushed. "You don't need her help!
You're so much smarter than she is."
Mog looked insulted. "What are you talking about? Deb is super smart!"
He paused. "But I agree that she doesn't need to help Waldo.
She should just hang out with me today."
Mog scratched his head. "Where is Deb anyway?"
"And where is Winnie?" a witch asked. "I haven't seen her all day."
"Winnie is working on a . . . special assignment for me," said Miss Bungle.
Ben perked up. Winnie was working on a special assignment?
"Deb never showed up," said Waldo.
Mr. Freaky wrung his hands. "We need to find out where Deb is.
Miss Bungle, can you please ask the office ogre to look for Deb?"
"Of course," said the broom flying teacher, who then hurried out of the room.
Mr. Freaky glanced around the lab. "Waldo, do you remember anything else?"
Waldo nodded. "Yes, a human girl ran into the lab."
Mayor Hubbletree looked startled. "What?"
"It must be the same girl who ran into the school," Ben put in.
"I saw her too."
"You did?" said Mr. Freaky.
Ben nodded. "About Winnie, though, do you know where—?"
"I don't believe it!" Mayor Hubbletree interrupted.
"You heard Ms. Prim, Freaky. None of our students is missing."
"A human was in here," Waldo insisted.
"She seemed really scared and confused."
The mayor folded his arms.
"Can you blame her? This place gives me the creeps."
Waldo continued. "I asked her who she was and what she was doing here, but she wouldn't tell me.
She said something like, 'I don't understand what's going on.'
Then she saw her reflection and shrieked.
I don't remember anything after that."
Gaby's face grew red with anger.
"Whoever that girl is, she must have knocked you out!
If I ever get my hands on her, I'll—"
"This is outrageous!" boomed Mayor Hubbletree.
"The idea that a human would come in here and attack a monster is absurd!"
"Do you think that crazy human hurt Deb too?" Mog asked Waldo.
"Of course not!" shouted Mayor Hubbletree.
"Everyone knows that it's monsters who attack humans!
Not the other way around!"
Mr. Freaky pulled out a handkerchief and blew his noses.
"Maybe it was a human, but she didn't mean to hurt Waldo," said Dave.
"After all, I caused the purple spot epidemic by accident.
Or maybe something went wrong with the experiment."
The mayor nodded. "Yes, it was probably something to do with the experiment."
Now Waldo looked annoyed. "My experiment was going fine."
"Was the human wearing a hoodie with a green skull on the back?" Ben blurted out.
Waldo looked surprised. "Actually, yes, she was."
Just then Ms. Prim came back into the lab with her clipboard.
"I've done another head count, Mayor.
All of our students are here. No one is missing."
"There you go, Freaky," said Mayor Hubbletree, looking around at the monsters.
"It wasn't a human who caused this mess. That means—"
"It was a monster!" Mr. Freaky put his head in his hands.
"Everything is totally out of control!"
Ben and Mog helped Mr. Creepy clean up the lab.
When everything was back in order, Waldo volunteered to demonstrate some simple science experiments.
"Yeah!" yelled a tall boy. "We want to see the wizard do some magic!"
Mr. Freaky nodded at Waldo.
"If you're feeling well enough, Waldo, please go ahead.
I'm going to see if the office ogre has found Deb yet.
I hope this mystery girl—whoever she is—hasn't harmed Deb too."
Waldo did some simple experiments, which calmed everyone down.
But Ben was too busy thinking to pay attention.
What if the mystery girl attacked Winnie?
Where was Winnie anyway? And what was the special assignment?
"I'll ask Miss Bungle," thought Ben as Mr. Freaky came back into the lab.
"Your wizard here is pretty talented, Freaky," said Mayor Hubbletree. "How did he—?"
The loudspeaker's shriek cut him off.
The mayor clapped his hands over his ears. "What is that horrible sound?"
"The lunch bell, of course," said Mr. Freaky.
"Then let's eat lunch," Ms. Prim put in.
Mayor Hubbletree scowled. "What is for lunch, Freaky?
Some kind of disgusting monster food?"
"Actually," Mr. Freaky replied, "the cafeteria trolls are serving something that you humans love—pizza."
"Oh." The mayor looked surprised. "That sounds pretty good."
Everyone headed downstairs to the cafeteria.
As Ben searched the hallway for Miss Bungle, he spotted Winnie.
The witch was walking away from her locker, holding a broom and a lunch bag.
"Winnie!" Ben shot after her, zigzagging between monsters and people.
The office ogre abruptly stepped into his path. "Has anyone seen Deb?"
Shloomp! Ben flew right through the ogre.
"Ouch!" cried the office ogre.
"Sorry!" Ben called over his shoulder.
A second later Ben caught up to Winnie. He tapped her on the shoulder.
Startled, Winnie spun to face him. "Oh. Hi, Ben."
"Where have you been all morning?" asked Ben.
"Miss Bungle said you're working on a special assignment." He paused.
"And you weren't in the flyover."
"Don't remind me," Winnie muttered.
"What do you mean?" asked Ben.
Winnie huffed. "Don't remind me that I wasn't selected for the broom flying squad."
Ben was shocked. "Why weren't you selected?"
Winnie flushed. "I failed my broom flying exam.
So now I'm just some loser who can't fly a broom by herself."
Ben blinked in surprise. "But you're so good at flying. What happened?"
"I got really nervous," Winnie explained.
"The test was hard, and I felt so much pressure.
I just started making stupid mistakes with my broom."
She sighed. "What good is a witch who can't even fly her own broom?"
"What good is a ghost who can't float through doors?" Ben said, trying to make her laugh.
"I got stuck in one today."
Winnie giggled. "You did?"
"Yeah, right in front of the whole school," said Ben.
"Including all the humans from People Place!"
Winnie laughed. "Sorry, I shouldn't laugh, but that is funny!"
"Can you retake the test?" asked Ben.
Winnie nodded. "Miss Bungle told me I can retake it tomorrow.
She's letting me spend today practicing and studying.
That's my special assignment."
"Awesome," said Ben. "And just think—even if you fail again, it's not a big deal.
You'll just be one of those thirty-year-old witches whose parents still fly them around."
"Not funny!" Winnie laughed as she playfully punched Ben on the shoulder.
"I'm just kidding," said Ben.
"I know," said Winnie. "I should get back to work.
I'm going to eat my lunch in the library while I read about broom flying techniques."
"Okay," said Ben. "Good luck!"
Ben watched as Winnie headed around the corner, toward the library.
He was sure that she would pass the test the next time.
Feeling much better, Ben floated down to the cafeteria.
But when he got there, he saw that something was wrong.
Mayor Hubbletree was yelling at Mr. Freaky again.
Ms. Prim was standing near them, looking ill.
"This is disgusting!" the mayor shouted. "Is this another prank, Freaky?"
Ben looked around. On each table was a large round pie.
"That must be the pizza," thought Ben.
Ben thought the pizza smelled and looked delicious.
The human kids, however, didn't seem to think so.
They all stared at their food, looking scared.
Mr. Freaky looked shocked. "What are you talking about, Mayor?
I thought humans loved pizza!"
The mayor's face was bright red.
"Not when it's covered in . . . in . . .
What on earth is it covered in?"
"That's just pond scum and worm guts," said Mr. Freaky.
The color instantly drained from Mayor Hubbletree's face.
"It's worse than I thought! We can't eat this!"
The mayor reached into his pocket and pulled out a cell phone.
"I'm ordering pizza from Enzo's, in People Place.
And you're going to pay for it, Freaky!"
"Hello, Enzo?" The mayor spoke loudly into his cell phone.
"Mayor Hubbletree here. I need you to send twenty pizzas over to Monster Academy as fast as you can.
What? Yes, of course it's safe to come over here."
The mayor listened for a moment.
"No, Enzo, none of the monsters will try to eat you.
Just bring those pizzas!"
The mayor put his cell phone away.
All the monster students started eating their pizza while the humans waited for theirs to arrive.
Ben looked around the cafeteria and was surprised to see Deb standing with her back to the wall.
"I guess the office ogre found her," he thought.
"Over here, Ben!" called Waldo from a nearby table.
Gaby, Dave, and Jen were with him.
Ben floated over to his friends.
"This pizza looks great," he said.
Then he glanced at Dave, who looked ill. "Sorry you don't like it."
"I-it's okay," said Dave. "The regular pizza will be here soon."
Jen grabbed a slice and took a bite. "Mmm! The worm guts are so slippery!
Are you sure you don't want to try it, Dave?"
Dave held up a hand. "No, thanks. I'm fine."
"I love pond scum," said Gaby. "I put it on everything!"
Mr. Freaky was apologizing again. "I'm really sorry about lunch, Mayor.
I hope you're enjoying some parts of the field trip."
"Are you kidding?" said Mayor Hubbletree.
"This field trip is a complete disaster!"
Mr. Freaky took out his handkerchief and blew his noses.
Thirty minutes later the other pizzas arrived.
The human kids cheered as the deliveryman entered the cafeteria.
The deliveryman looked nervously around the cafeteria.
"I h-have t-twenty pizzas here for—"
Boom! The pizzas exploded, sending cheese and tomato sauce all over the cafeteria.
At the same moment, Ben spied someone running out the door.
It was a squid monster. Ben didn't recognize the monster.
But he did recognize what she was wearing.
"A hoodie with a green skull on the back!" thought Ben.
Why were the mystery girl and the squid monster wearing the same thing?
Were they part of a gang?
Mayor Hubbletree stared at the pizza explosion.
"What is wrong with this school?" he said.
Mr. Freaky had his face buried in his hands. He was moaning loudly.
A cafeteria troll came out of the kitchen with a mop and a bucket, and began to clean up the mess.
Mayor Hubbletree went over to the deliveryman.
The deliveryman was shaking. "I-I'm sorry, sir," he said.
"I don't know what happened."
"It's not your fault," said the mayor. He glanced around at the monsters.
"It's this place—strange things happen here.
Go back to the restaurant and get another twenty pizzas.
And don't worry—the principal here will be paying for everything."
The deliveryman left the cafeteria.
Waldo shook his head. "Wow, what a strange day.
What made those pizzas explode?"
"I'm not sure," said Ben. "But I think it was a squid monster.
And I think she and the girl who attacked you are in a gang together."
"What?" Waldo raised an eyebrow. "What do you mean?"
Ben explained all the odd things he'd seen that day.
"You should tell Mr. Freaky about the squid monster," said Waldo.
"Maybe he can stop the gang from ruining the field trip.
Otherwise Mayor Hubbletree might decide to bulldoze the school for real this time."
Ben nodded and got up from the table.
He floated over to the principal, who was standing with Mayor Hubbletree and Ms. Prim.
"Mr. Freaky," said Ben. "I think I know who made the pizzas explode."
The principal's eyes went wide. "Who?" he demanded. "Tell me at once!"
"It was a squid monster," said Ben. "I think the monster is part of a gang."
"Aha!" declared Mayor Hubbletree.
"You monsters are finally admitting that a monster is the culprit!
I knew a human student wasn't causing problems."
He stared at Mr. Freaky. "Well, Freaky? What are you going to do about this?"
The principal started wringing his hands. "Oh, where is Miss Bungle?"
"I'm right here!" called the broom flying teacher, hurrying over.
Mr. Freaky told Miss Bungle about the squid monster.
Miss Bungle hurried out of the cafeteria to search for the monster.
After several minutes she returned.
"I used every kind of seeking spell I know," she said.
"There are no squid monsters anywhere in the building."
She looked out over the students.
"Except Beth and Henry, who are sitting over there."
Ben knew those two squid monsters.
Neither was the one he'd seen run out of the cafeteria.
Mr. Freaky took out a handkerchief and blew his noses.
"This is terrible! First we had a mystery human running loose in the school.
Now we have a mystery squid monster!"
After the humans finally had lunch, everyone headed outside to the soccer field.
"We have a friendly game of soccer planned," explained Mr. Freaky.
Ben saw Mayor Hubbletree's face brighten.
"I didn't know monsters like soccer.
I played soccer in college—I was actually rather good at the game."
Mr. Freaky beamed. "Wonderful! It's going to be very exciting!"
Ben sat near his friends in the bleachers.
He watched the Monster Academy soccer team walk onto the grass.
The human team followed them.
Mr. Gwarg was already there. A large bag sat beside him.
"Listen up, monsters," said the gym teacher.
"You're playing against humans today, so there are a few rule changes."
A tiny goblin raised his hand.
"We can still throw fireballs at each other, right?"
A human player gulped.
"Absolutely not," said Mr. Gwarg.
"The humans can't do that, so it wouldn't be fair.
You also can't use claws, fangs, or any kind of magic."
Zork huffed, "This game is going to be so boring."
"It'll be just like regular soccer," said Mr. Gwarg.
"But safer for the humans. Oh, and there's no flying."
"What!" cried a monster with wings. "How can we play without flying?"
Mr. Gwarg folded his arms.
"If the humans can play without flying, then so can you, Leo."
"That's not a problem for me," said a worm monster. "I can't fly anyway."
"You can't pop up from underground either, Francis," Mr. Gwarg said.
"Boo," said the worm.
Soon the players took their positions on the field.
The monsters' goalie was an enormous green blob.
"Hey, no fair!" shouted a human boy. "Your goalie fills the entire goal!"
"Yeah," said a girl. "We should have two goalies to make it even!"
"What!" said a fish monster. "Two of our players are zombies.
You humans should lose two players if we're going to keep things even!"
"No way!" said another girl. "You guys have a two-headed monster!
She should count as two players!"
Mr. Gwarg blew his whistle. "Let's start the game!"
The gym teacher carried the bag to the center of the field and pulled out the game ball.
Wiggling tentacles covered it, and electrical sparks danced across its surface.
The human players shrieked and ran off the field.
"What is that thing?" cried Mayor Hubbletree.
Mr. Freaky blinked in surprise. "It's a soccer ball, Mayor.
I thought you said you used to play?"
"That's not a soccer ball, Freaky!" the mayor shouted.
"That's a disgusting—Oh, never mind. This whole trip is a disaster."
A moment later a human player ran back from the bus with a new soccer ball.
Ben saw that this one had no tentacles or electrical sparks.
"We're using our ball for the game!" Mayor Hubbletree snapped.
A few monster players started to argue, but Mr. Gwarg shot them a look.
"Fine," the gym teacher told the mayor.
A tall boy quickly got control of the ball.
He passed it to a girl up the field.
"That's Rebecca," said Dave. "She's really good at soccer."
Rebecca dribbled the ball fast.
Leo ran in front of her, but Rebecca got the ball past him and continued down the field.
She rushed past the two zombie defenders and took a shot.
The goalie blob lunged toward the ball, but he was too slow.
The ball went past him, and the humans cheered.
"Score one for the humans!" shouted Mr. Gwarg.
The monsters had the ball now.
The tiny goblin ran toward three large human players.
Keeping perfect control of the ball, the goblin scooted between a player's feet.
"Hey!" the kid yelled.
The goblin reached the humans' goal and shot.
The goalie caught the ball and threw it toward a player nearby.
The boy dribbled the ball past Leo.
The monster flapped his wings and flew after the boy.
Mr. Gwarg blew his whistle. "No flying!"
"Sorry!" said Leo, dropping back to the ground.
The goblin took the ball from the boy and headed back up the field.
A moment later a big human kid charged toward the goblin, knocking him over.
"Ow!" cried the goblin. "No fair!"
"Sure, it's fair!" the kid called over his shoulder.
"You can check in— Oof!"
Francis had popped out of the ground, tripping the kid.
Mr. Gwarg blew his whistle again. "Francis!"
"Sorry!" called the worm.
Now Rebecca had the ball. She headed down the field and took another shot.
The ball knocked over a zombie.
In the bleachers Waldo shook his head.
"How did those zombies ever get on the team?"
Ben shrugged. "Don't ask me."
The ball was still sitting in the grass near the fallen zombie.
As Rebecca ran to it, light flashed—and the ball turned into a gigantic spider!
"Whoa! The soccer ball turned into a giant spider!" cried a human boy.
"It's going to attack us!" cried a girl.
"Run for your lives!" cried another kid.
The human soccer players sprinted off the field and hid.
All around Ben, human kids leaped up.
They pushed and shoved as they rushed down the bleachers' steps.
"This is terrible!" Mr. Freaky wrung his hands.
"Everything is totally out of control!"
The spider charged up the field. Ben noticed that it was growing bigger.
Ben and his friends ran down to the field.
Several teachers chased the spider.
But every time someone got close to the giant creature, it shot sticky webs.
"Aargh!" shouted Mr. Gwarg as a large web stuck to his face.
Miss Bungle hopped onto her broom and flew after the spider.
The spider spun around and flung webs at the broom flying teacher.
She lost control of her broom and slammed into the bleachers.
"This is outrageous!" shouted Mayor Hubbletree.
"Freaky! You said we were going to have a friendly game of soccer!"
Mr. Freaky didn't seem to know how to reply.
He grabbed his handkerchief and blew his noses.
"Students from People Place Middle School!" Mayor Hubbletree shouted.
"Back on the bus! We're leaving this instant!"
As Ben watched the humans leave, he noticed someone else running.
It was a large troll.
And she was wearing the same hoodie that the mystery girl and the squid had been wearing.
Ben pointed out the troll to Waldo.
"I think that troll made the ball turn into a spider."
"What?" Waldo squinted at the troll. "Why do you think that?"
"The troll is wearing the same hoodie that the mystery girl and the squid monster wore," Ben replied.
"She must be in their gang! We have to stop them!"
Ben shot after the troll, and Waldo hurried after him.
The troll ran around an equipment shed.
"I'll float through the shed and surprise the troll on the other side," thought Ben.
He floated toward the shed, passing through one wall, then through all of the equipment, and then . . .
"Oh no!" cried Ben. "I'm stuck!"
Ben was stuck halfway through the wall of the shed.
He pushed and pulled and struggled to get out, but nothing worked.
He watched helplessly as the troll ducked around a corner of the school building.
Waldo hurried over. "Don't worry, Ben. I'll help you."
But then the wizard slapped his forehead, causing his glasses to fall off.
"Ugh. I don't have my spell book with me.
I can't get you out of there without looking up the right spell."
"Waldo, just try," Ben pleaded. "The troll is going to get away!"
Waldo stooped down for his glasses. He put them back on.
"I don't know . . . I'm not very good at—"
"You can do it!" said Ben.
"Besides, what's the worst that can happen? I'm already stuck in a wall."
Waldo took a deep breath. "Okay, I'll give it a try."
The wizard thought for a moment.
Then he muttered some words under his breath.
Suddenly—pop! Ben flew out of the wall.
Waldo blinked in astonishment. "It worked!" he cried.
"I can't believe it—I did a spell without my spell book!"
He jumped up and down, causing his glasses to fall off again.
"Awesome!" said Ben. "Now let's catch that troll!"
They ran around the corner of the building and found a pink monster.
Ben gasped when he realized what she was wearing.
"The hoodie!" Ben cried.
"She must be in the gang," said Waldo. "But where's the troll?"
Ben glanced around. The troll was nowhere in sight.
"I don't understand," he said.
"Why would this monster stick around if the troll ran away?
If they were in the same gang, they'd probably run away together."
Suddenly Ben thought of something. "Maybe there isn't a gang at all."
Waldo scratched his head. "What are you talking about?
What about the other monsters and the mystery girl?"
"I think this monster is all of them," said Ben.
"I think she can change shape."
The monster gasped.
"Who are you?" Ben asked the monster.
The monster didn't answer.
Ben glanced at Waldo. "Do you know any spells that can help us?"
"Yes," said Waldo without taking his eyes off the monster.
"I know a spell that makes creatures reveal their true forms." He paused.
"But I've never tried it."
"You can do it, Waldo," said Ben. "You freed me from that wall."
Waldo nodded. "You're right. I don't need my spell book.
I am a very talented wizard!"
He muttered some words under his breath and—poof!
"Oh no!" cried Ben.
"Moo!" said a cow.
Ben stared at Waldo, who was now a cow.
Meanwhile, the pink monster ran back toward the soccer field.
The teachers were still trying to catch the spider.
"Whoa!" shouted Mr. Freaky as the pink monster accidentally knocked him over.
Mr. Freaky climbed back to his feet.
Then—shloomp! Ben floated straight through the principal.
"Ouch!" cried Mr. Freaky. "What's going on here?"
"That pink monster is the one who's trying to ruin today's field trip!"
Ben shouted over his shoulder.
"Oh no!" cried the principal. "We have to catch her!"
Mr. Freaky ran after the monster, and other teachers joined in the chase.
Mr. Gwarg ran fast and tried to grab the monster.
Suddenly—poof! There was a puff of smoke, and Mr. Gwarg was blown backward.
The monster turned blue and got away.
Miss Bungle had nearly grabbed the monster's hood when bright light flashed and the monster disappeared.
When the monster reappeared farther down the field, she was a green ogre.
"This is a disaster!" cried Mr. Freaky.
Just then Ben heard the sound of rushing wind.
He looked up and saw Winnie on her broom, ripping through the sky like a rocket.
The witch weaved in and out of the crowd and toward the spider.
The spider shot webs at Winnie, but she caught them with one hand.
She flew in a circle around the spider, letting one strand of web wrap around the creature's legs.
The spider fell over, unable to move.
Next Winnie shot across the field, toward the green ogre.
The ogre tried to run away, but Winnie flew like lightning.
She flung the web and the ogre was caught.
"Excellent flying, Winnie!" said Miss Bungle.
Winnie beamed.
Everybody ran over to the ogre.
Ben noticed that she was starting to change shape again. She grew thinner.
Long black hair grew from her head.
Everybody gasped.
"Deb!" cried Mog.
"Deb?" Mr. Freaky stared at her.
"I don't understand. Why were you trying to ruin the people's visit?"
Deb hung her head. "I wasn't trying to ruin it.
But when the humans arrived, I started feeling weird.
Then strange magic kept happening.
I tried to talk to Waldo in the lab, but he didn't even recognize me.
When I saw my reflection, I knew why."
"That human was you?" said Waldo.
Deb nodded. "I turned back into myself for a while.
But then I turned into a bunch of other monsters."
She looked at Mrs. Germ. "Why is this happening to me?"
Mrs. Germ held out a hand. "Come to my office, dear.
We'll get this all sorted out."
The next day Ben was sitting with his friends at lunch.
Mog and Deb were there.
Gaby and Waldo were there too. Waldo wasn't a cow anymore.
"Luckily the spell didn't last long," said the wizard.
"I was back to normal by dinner."
Winnie came over to the table and sat down.
"When are you retaking your test?" Ben asked her.
Winnie shook her head. "I'm not retaking the test."
"What?" Ben was alarmed. "Why aren't you retaking it?"
Winnie grinned. "Miss Bungle said that my flying yesterday was the best she's ever seen.
I earned my broom flying license!"
"Awesome!" said Ben. Waldo gave her a high five.
"I have some news too."
Deb, who'd been sitting silently with the group, suddenly spoke up.
They all looked at her.
Deb's voice shook a little. "I found out yesterday that I'm not a ghoul.
I'm a doppelganger. I was adopted when I was really young.
Since everyone else in my family is a ghoul, I took on that form at first.
My parents had no idea either."
"Wow," Winnie murmured softly. "That's big."
"You never changed form until yesterday?" asked Waldo.
"Nope," said Deb. "I didn't understand what was happening.
I also have magic powers. They kept going crazy.
I'm so sorry about everything that happened."
"It sounds pretty scary," Ben said.
He was always worried about learning how to float through objects.
But his problem seemed silly compared to what Deb had gone through the day before.
Deb was still explaining things.
"Mrs. Germ thinks that being close to the humans caused my change.
Doppelgangers like to make themselves look like humans.
So when I was near humans for the first time yesterday, everything started happening."
She looked like she might start crying.
"It doesn't matter," Mog said quickly.
"Ghoul, doppelganger . . . Either way, you're perfect, Deb.
You're so smart and . . ."
"Oh boy," Ben whispered to Winnie as Mog went on and on about how great Deb was.
"I know." Winnie grinned at Ben.
"It sounds like somebody is totally in love again!"
"Yeah," Ben thought, gazing into Winnie's pretty green eyes. "I am."
"This is going to be the best field trip ever!" Ben said.
He was sitting next to Winnie on the school bus.
"I guess it will be interesting," Winnie murmured.
"I've never been to People Place before.
My parents say that many people don't like witches.
Or any kind of monsters."
Ben knew Winnie was very nervous.
Other students on the school bus seemed nervous too.
So did Miss Bungle, the broom-flying teacher, and Mr. Freaky.
The principal was running up and down the bus aisle, warning everybody to behave.
"Remember, students, this field trip is very important.
We're going to be camping overnight at the People Place Museum.
And you know what Mayor Hubbletree said.
If monsters create any problems, he's going to consider tearing down Monster Academy again."
"No problem, Mr. Freaky," Mog said, blowing a slime ball at a skeleton.
"You know me—I always behave."
"Don't worry, Winnie," Ben said.
"People are just like monsters. They only look strange."
Winnie laughed. "I guess you're right.
Everything went well when the people came to Monster Academy.
And Jen is dating a person."
"Yep," said Ben. "Jen is still dating Dave."
Mr. Freaky was wringing his hands.
His three noses wiggled like mad.
"Students, Miss Bungle is going to start collecting permission slips.
Please have yours ready—along with your monster manners and best behavior."
"Permission slip, please," Miss Bungle said to a three-eyed monster.
The monster handed her the slip of paper.
Miss Bungle took it and then moved to the monsters in the next seat.
"I hope that you all remembered to pack food in your lunchboxes," Mr. Freaky said.
"We'll be eating dinner at the museum."
"I remembered," said a goblin.
"I brought my own food because people eat weird stuff. Here's my lunchbox."
He held up a big metal pail filled with slime.
"Uh-oh," said an octopus monster.
"I probably didn't bring enough food."
She gazed sadly at the two barrels of fish beside her.
"That's okay," said a ghoul.
"I brought enough dead rats for everyone!"
"Did everyone bring a sleeping bag—or whatever you sleep in?" asked Mr. Freaky.
"I brought my camping coffin," said a vampire.
"I packed my portable pyramid," said a mummy girl named Cleo.
Waldo, who was sitting across from Cleo, grinned at her.
But Ben saw Gaby, sitting on the other side of Waldo, frown.
"Waldo and Cleo have been spending a lot of time together," Ben whispered to Winnie.
"I think Gaby's a little jealous."
"Waldo told me Cleo is helping him learn Egyptian magic," Winnie replied.
"That's cool," Ben said. "I hope we'll see some stuff from Egypt in the museum."
"Mr. Freaky, I have all the permission slips," Miss Bungle announced a few minutes later.
"Then I guess we're ready to go." Mr. Freaky loosened his tie and swallowed hard.
The driver turned the ignition key.
A shriek came from the engine, followed by some coughing sounds and black smoke.
"We're off!" Ben said.
The monsters laughed and talked as the bus drove through the familiar streets of Monsterville.
The kids played games, and the doppelgangers changed shape a bunch of times to amuse everybody.
But the laughter faded as the bus approached the wall that separated Monsterville from People Place.
"Now, don't worry, students!" Mr. Freaky called out.
"Remember, we have permission to visit People Place.
And we are Mayor Hubbletree's special guests!"
All the monsters—even the zombies—held their breath as the bus slowly traveled through the gate in the wall.
"Whoa! It's so bright here!" moaned a ghoul.
"Yeah," said a vampire. "Is it always this sunny?"
"It's a little creepy," said a skeleton.
"Do I look like a person now?" asked Carly.
She had changed her face to try to imitate a person.
But her nose and eyes were in the wrong places.
Everyone laughed uneasily.
Ben saw Winnie sit up straight and clutch her broom. He squeezed her hand.
"Don't worry," he reassured her.
"This trip will be a blast. We'll see cool stuff and have fun."
Winnie nodded. The broomstick was shaking in her hand.
"We're almost at the museum," announced Mr. Freaky a minute later.
The bus drove past a huge building with two large stone lions out front.
"It's the museum!" Gaby said.
"Cool. The building looks pretty old."
"Yeah! Like a beautiful crypt," said a vampire.
Ben waited for the bus to stop.
Instead it pulled around to a lot in the back of the building.
Mr. Freaky sprang out of his seat.
"Here we are!" he called.
"Our field trip in People Place is about to begin!"
Ben looked out the window of the school bus.
A man wearing a gray suit and red tie was hurrying toward them.
"Welcome to People Place," he called in a friendly voice.
"My name is Al—Al Normal."
The monsters slowly climbed off the bus.
"I'm the museum director's assistant," the man continued cheerfully.
"I'm going to show you monsters all around the museum.
I'm sure your overnight stay in our new education wing will be really great!"
Mog looked around in confusion.
"Where are all the cobwebs?" he asked.
A vampire was squinting and searching for her sunglasses.
"It’s too bright here for me."
Mr. Freaky flapped his arms nervously.
"Now, students . . . remember your monster manners, please!
We are guests in People Place."
"Stay calm, Mr. Freaky," Miss Bungle said.
"Everything is totally under control."
"Ugh!" a monster burst out.
"That part of the museum looks so new and shiny!"
Al Normal beamed with pride.
"Yes, we've just had a major renovation. Isn't our building beautiful?
Some sections are still under construction, of course, but the work is nearly finished.
You'll all have to come back for the dedication ceremony in the spring."
"It's a very nice building," Ben said. "The museum looks really cool."
"Thank you." Al Normal nodded at Ben.
"The construction crew is still working on the area between the education wing and the main part of the museum," he explained.
"I'm very sorry about any inconvenience.
But the classrooms where you'll be spending the night are finished.
They are ready for your stay, and I think you'll be very comfortable there."
Mr. Freaky was looking around with a frown.
"I thought that the museum director was supposed to meet us when we arrived," he said.
"Mayor Hubbletree indicated that she'd be here to greet us."
"Um, Dr. Bones had to deal with some last-minute museum issues," Al Normal explained.
"And Mayor Hubbletree will be here very soon.
We'll meet the director right after I show you our new education wing.
I think you monsters will be very impressed with what you see."
"I'm sure the education wing is beautiful," Miss Bungle replied politely.
She turned to the group of Monster Academy students.
"Monsters! Please line up. It's time to start the tour."
Mr. Freaky looked startled. "I-it is?" he stammered.
"Oh . . . yes! It is!
Nothing to be afraid of, students! Everything is totally—"
"Under control!" shouted a few monsters.
The group followed Al Normal into the museum.
Gaby ducked so that she wouldn't hit her head on the door.
A monster wrinkled his nose.
"It's all so . . . er, new!" he said, looking around.
The vampire wearing sunglasses shuddered.
"Wow. The lights are even brighter in here," she moaned.
"We're very proud of this new addition to the museum," Al Normal was saying.
"Everything is quite modern and up-to-date.

"You have solar power!" The vampire gasped in horror.
"Isn't that dangerous? It sounds awful."
"Oh no. It's not dangerous," Al Normal said.
"It's very safe and very clean as well."
"It's good for the environment," Ben chimed in.
"Mr. Creepy said that's helpful for people and monsters."
The vampire nodded slowly, but she still looked uneasy.
A long hallway was cluttered with construction equipment—metal pipes, scaffolding, tools, paint cans, and ladders.
Ben could see that a new wall was being constructed.
"What's going on there?" Mr. Freaky asked, pointing to the mess.
Al Normal frowned. "I'm sorry about that, Mr. Freaky.
