So we'll have to go around to the main entrance to see the exhibits.
But first, we'll view the education wing.
After that we can go upstairs to the director's new office and meet her."
He smiled at the monsters.
"Does anyone have any questions so far?"
"I do! I do!" A monster waved his hand.
"Yes?" said Al Normal pleasantly.
"When's dinner?" the monster blurted out.
"Yeah!" Mog chimed in, rubbing his belly. "I'm really hungry."
"Er . . ." Al Normal quickly checked his watch.
"Let's see. We have a busy schedule, but I think we can eat dinner around—Eek!"
He shrieked in horror as a hairy creature sprang at his face!
Al Normal ducked, and the hairy creature zoomed past his head. "Look out!" he cried.
Startled, some of the monsters ducked too.
"What is that thing?" thought Ben.
It looked familiar, but he couldn't remember where he'd seen it before.
"I'll stop it!" Waldo cried.
He reached into his backpack for a wand as the creature leaped around the lobby.
"Waldo, it's really fast!" Gaby said. "Be careful!"
Waldo frowned and put away his wand as the creature raced toward the construction area.
Al Normal's eyes were wide with alarm.
"It's heading for the main part of the museum!"
"I'll get it!" Mog said.
He dived at the thing but missed. "Oof!"
Mr. Freaky looked panicked.
"Now it's running upstairs!" he wailed.
"Oh, this is a disaster!"
"Uh-oh." Al Normal gulped.
"The museum director's office is up there."
"Students!" commanded Miss Bungle. "Catch it!"
Ben darted after the creature.
"This isn't good," he thought.
If the creature caused trouble, the monsters would get blamed.
Mayor Hubbletree would be furious!
The thing raced toward an office.
Then—zoom!
Something whooshed right over Ben's head. "Winnie!"
Winnie was riding her broom.
She scooped up the hairy creature just before it reached the office door.
"Got it!" she called, bringing it back to the group.
Al Normal shuddered. "What is that thing?"
Jen flushed. "It's mine.
I opened my lunchbox, and my dinner got away!"
Mr. Freaky blew his three noses. "Put it away, Jen, now!"
Al Normal looked sick. "You monsters eat things like that?"
Cleo laughed softly.
"Al Normal looks better green," she whispered to Waldo.
Gaby frowned. "That's rude, Cleo. He's our host."
A woman dressed in a business suit stood in the doorway of the office.
A construction worker stood nearby, holding a screwdriver.
"D-Dr. Bones!" Al Normal stammered.
"I'm sorry about the commotion! It won't happen again."
"Hmpf!" snapped Dr. Bones. She didn't look happy.
Neither did the construction worker standing near Dr. Bones.
Ben saw him scowl. "Monsters," muttered the construction worker.
"You can't trust them."
"That's not true," Ben burst out.
"We're just like people!" Winnie chimed in.
"With a different diet," Jen said.
Al Normal stepped between the monsters and Dr. Bones to make introductions.
Mr. Freaky and Miss Bungle shook hands with Dr. Bones.
"I'm pleased to meet all of you," Dr. Bones said.
She looked very serious.
"We'll have to hurry around to the front entrance for the rest of your official greeting," she said.
"The mayor has probably arrived by now.
I'm sorry we can't walk through the museum, but there's still construction in that hallway."
"If you paid us more, we might be done," the construction worker muttered.
Dr. Bones shot him a stern look.
"We've discussed this already," she said.
"You've been paid the amount in your contract.
Now you need to finish the work."
"This job has been harder than we thought," complained the worker.
"It's taking longer too. If you paid us more, we could hire more workers and finish faster."
Dr. Bones pursed her lips.
"The museum doesn't have any more money for construction right now.
Now please get back to work."
The workman grumbled as he stomped over to the construction area.
Al Normal checked his watch.
"I'll tell the mayor you're coming," he said to Dr. Bones, hurrying off.
Dr. Bones pointed to several nearby rooms.
"You can leave your sleeping bags and other things in those two classrooms," she told the monsters.
"Be sure to lock your lunchboxes," Miss Bungle added, giving Jen a look.
The monsters put down their things and then followed Dr. Bones toward the rear entrance.
"I could probably float through all that stuff," Ben thought.
"But Mr. Freaky would get mad if I didn't stay with the group."
Near the main entrance, Dr. Bones scratched her head.
"Where are the TV cameras? I invited a crew from People Place News."
Ben looked up. The only person waiting to greet them was Mayor Hubbletree.
He hurried up to Dr. Bones.
"I sent the news crew home," the mayor explained.
"After all, some people are unhappy about this field trip.
They don't like the idea of monsters staying overnight in People Place."
"Ridiculous," Dr. Bones muttered.
Mr. Freaky pulled out his handkerchief and blew his noses a few times.
"Monsters!" he said to the students.
"What do we say to Mayor Hubbletree?"
"Good afternoon, Mayor," the monsters chanted.
"Thank you for inviting us to People Place."
Mayor Hubbletree flashed a quick smile.
"Welcome to the People Place Museum," he said.
"We're all . . . um, delighted to have you here."
Then he leaned close to Mr. Freaky's ear.
"This field trip better not cause any problems, Freaky, or I'll knock down Monster Academy with my own bare hands!"
"Mayor Hubbletree didn't sound very welcoming in his 'welcome' speech," Ben whispered to Winnie.
"Monsters make him nervous," Winnie whispered back.
Mr. Freaky's noses were wiggling wildly as he tried to reassure Mayor Hubbletree.
"Don't worry, Mayor. Miss Bungle and I will make sure that things are under control."
"You'd better, Freaky!" Mayor Hubbletree snapped.
"I went to a lot of trouble to arrange this field trip.
A lot of people are very suspicious of monsters, you know."
Dr. Bones looked impatient. "Don't worry, Mayor.
Everything will be fine.
I'll make sure that all the monsters are snug in their beds."
"I have a coffin, not a bed," said a vampire.
"I have a pyramid," Cleo said.
Winnie giggled. "Do you think we should tell Dr. Bones that zombies never sleep?"
"Wonderful, Dr. Bones!" the mayor was saying.
"I look forward to receiving a wonderful report tomorrow.
Now please excuse me. I have some very important work to do at City Hall."
As the mayor left, the Doppel Gang made funny faces behind his back.
"Stop that at once!" Mr. Freaky ordered.
Dr. Bones turned to Al Normal. "You're in charge," she said.
"I'll be in my office."
Al Normal looked nervously at the group.
"Okay, people, er, monsters! Let's go inside."
Ben followed the other monsters into the museum.
"I'm sure that you'll find many interesting things here," Al Normal began.
"We have all kinds of fascinating exhibits—dinosaurs, rocks, plants.
We also have a wonderful Old West exhibit and an Egyptian collection with valuable jewels."
"Ooh! Dinosaurs!" said a lizard monster.
Gaby pointed to a fountain. "What a pretty fountain."
"It represents the oceans of the world," Mr. Normal said.
"There's a map of the museum right here."
He pointed to a big map on display.
Beside it was a stand with printed maps.
Al Normal looked at Miss Bungle and Mr. Freaky.
"Should I show the students around the museum?" he asked.
"I think they can explore the exhibits on their own," Miss Bungle said.
"I don't want anyone to get lost," Al Normal murmured.
"No problem. We can use the maps," Ben said.
Al Normal still looked uneasy.
"I'll be walking around the exhibits, watching to see if anyone needs me."
"Too bad he doesn't have more eyes," whispered a three-eyed monster.
"I wonder where the Egyptian exhibit is," Cleo said.
"I bet we can find it," Waldo replied, looking at his map.
"Let's check out the Early Humans exhibit first," Gaby suggested.
"I read that people used to live in caves."
"Wow!" Mog said. "Maybe they're more like monsters than I thought."
Ben and Winnie started exploring the museum.
They looked at the cave people and then headed to the dinosaur exhibit.
A few monsters were standing at a glass case.
"Ugh!" cried a fish monster.
"I thought they'd have real dinosaurs here.
These are just dumb skeletons!"
A tall skeleton glowered at the fish monster. "Are you calling skeletons dumb?"
Waldo read aloud from a museum pamphlet.
"It says here that ancient people thought that huge fossil bones belonged to giants."
"Maybe they did belong to giants," Gaby said.
"But now people know those bones really belonged to dinosaurs, which are long extinct," Waldo continued.
"How do they know dinosaurs are extinct?" asked the fish monster.
"Dinosaurs could still be roaming the earth."
While the others argued about the bones, Ben walked around.
He spotted a pair of zombies standing near the museum entrance.
"They must be new students," Ben thought.
"I didn't notice them on the bus."
He decided to walk over and introduce himself.
But he lost the zombies in the crowd before he could reach them.
"Huh. Where did they go?" he said, looking around.
Nearby, some people in hard hats came out of the construction area.
"Excuse me, did you see two zombies go by?" Ben asked them.
"Nope," said the first worker, whom Ben had seen at the director's office earlier.
"Hey," said the other worker with a frown.
"Shouldn't you be with the other monsters?
Dr. Bones doesn't like students wandering around the museum on their own."
"Dr. Bones doesn't like anybody," the first worker muttered under his breath.
Just then Ben heard a shriek.
"That sounds like Cleo!" he thought.
He thanked the workers and whirled around to see what was happening.
He found his friends at the Egyptian exhibit.
They were all staring into a tall glass display case, just past the Egyptian jewels.
Cleo had her hands clapped over her mouth.
"Cleo, what's wrong?" Ben asked.
Cleo pointed at the case.
"See that mummy? He's my uncle Tut!"
"What?" Ben gasped.
"That mummy is your uncle?"
Cleo nodded. "My uncle Tut has been missing for a thousand years.
I never thought I'd find him here.
The people must have kidnapped him!"
"People are horrible!" said a vampire.
"Yeah!" agreed the fish monster.
"I think we're supposed to be giving people a chance," Ben reminded everyone.
"Well, people aren't giving monsters a chance," said Mog.
"They're putting mummies on display. This isn't a museum—it's a prison!"
"We're all trapped!" added a goblin.
Ben didn't feel trapped. He could float through the walls and leave at any time.
"Cleo," he said calmly.
"I bet there's a good explanation for why your uncle Tut is here."
Cleo wasn't listening. Instead she was pounding on the display case.
"Uncle Tut!" she cried. "Uncle Tut, can you hear me?"
"Are you sure it's your uncle, Cleo?" Waldo asked.
"You said he's been missing for a thousand years.
How could you even recognize him?"
"A lot of mummies look alike," Gaby chimed in.
"I'm positive!" Cleo insisted.
"My family has a statue of Uncle Tut from when he was king.
And some paintings. That's definitely my uncle!"
Just then Al Normal ran into the room.
He looked frantic. "I heard a scream. Are you monsters okay?"
"No." Mog shook his head.
"Someone is killing monsters and putting them on display. It's not fair!"
"What?" Al Normal shook his head in confusion.
"No, that's not true."
"It's not just monsters," said the fish monster.
"I saw lots of stuffed people in the Early Humans exhibit."
Al Normal sighed. "Monsters, please relax.
Those aren't real people.
They're dummies—life-size models made to look like cave people."
"Oh," Mog said. "Well, they look pretty real."
"Mr. Normal, are you saying that's not a real mummy?" Waldo asked, pointing at the display.
"Of course it's a genuine mummy," Al Normal said.
"All of our Egyptian displays come from ancient Egypt.
That's the genuine mummy of Tutmosis the Thirteenth."
"Uncle Tut!" Cleo wailed.
"I told you it was my uncle Tut! What have you done to him?"
"Young lady, how can he be your uncle?" Al Normal was growing impatient.
"He's a mummy!" He blinked as he realized something.
"Oh. You're a mummy too."
Cleo burst into tears. "Wait until I tell my parents!"
Al Normal patted Cleo awkwardly. "There's no reason to cry.
I promise, we didn't do anything to your uncle.
Tutmosis was that way when he came here—way before I was born."
"Maybe he's just asleep," Ben said. "I think I see him breathing."
"You're right!" Cleo started pounding on the case again.
"Uncle Tut! Uncle Tut, wake up!"
Other monsters started banging on the case too. "Uncle Tut! Wake up!"
"Monsters!" Miss Bungle called.
"Please settle down. You're behaving like people!"
Just then Mr. Freaky came running into the exhibit room.
Dr. Bones was right behind him.
"Monsters, please!" Mr. Freaky cried.
He took out his handkerchief and blew his noses.
"What is going on in here?"
Dr. Bones rushed toward Cleo. "Stop that at once!" she ordered.
She tried to pull Cleo and the other monsters away from the case.
But everyone kept shouting and banging.
"Ben's right," Waldo said.
"Uncle Tut is definitely breathing.
If he wakes up, Cleo, he can go home with you."
Cleo looked at him. "That would be so great.
But how can we wake him up?"
"I could throw the case in the fountain," Gaby suggested.
"The cold water might wake him up."
"Uh . . ." Ben glanced uneasily at Dr. Bones.
"I don't think the people would like that," he said.
"Maybe I could float through the case and shake him awake."
"Good idea," Winnie said.
"My spell book is upstairs with my stuff," Waldo said, reaching into his pockets.
"But I have a wand with me. I can try a magic spell."
"Oh no," Ben thought, trying not to groan.
By now Dr. Bones was shouting.
"Monster children! Step away from the displays right now!"
"It's not a display!" Cleo wailed. "It's my uncle!"
Waldo pointed his wand. "Wake up!" he cried.
Ka-zap! Bing! The spell bounced off the glass case.
Monsters covered their heads and dived out of the way.
The spell zapped over their heads and shot into the next room.
Cleo peeled her hand away from her eyes.
"Did the spell work?" she asked in a hushed voice.
Ben turned to look at the display case.
Unfortunately Uncle Tut was still inside.
Then he heard Winnie gasp.
"It worked on something!" she said, pointing to the next room.
"The museum's dinosaur skeletons have come to life!"
Ben gasped as dinosaur skeletons stomped through the museum, their bones rattling.
"N-n-nobody panic!" Mr. Freaky yelled. "Everything is totally under control!"
"No, it's not!" Dr. Bones cried.
A stegosaurus lumbered toward her. "What have you monsters done?"
Ben saw a big dinosaur stomp into the Early Humans exhibit and roar at a stuffed mammoth.
The stegosaurus was now drinking from the fountain in the lobby.
A tall beast was munching on the plastic palm trees at the entrance to the Egyptian exhibit.
"Help!" screamed Al Normal as the stegosaurus charged toward him.
"Stop!" Ben commanded, floating in front of the dinosaur.
But the stegosaurus ran right through Ben.
Winnie jumped on her broom.
She zoomed toward Al Normal and yanked him out of the way.
"Waldo! Fix this!"
"My spell book is upstairs!" Waldo moaned. "All I have is a wand."
"Yay!" whooped a skeleton who was hanging onto the tail of the big dinosaur.
Mr. Freaky and Dr. Bones ducked as the dinosaur ran by them.
"Do something, Mr. Freaky!" the museum director commanded.
Mr. Freaky blew his noses. "Students!" he bellowed. "Do something!"
"No!" Cleo yelled at the stegosaurus as it charged toward the mummy display case.
"Stay away from my uncle."
She grabbed Waldo's wand and cried, "Spell, begone!"
Magic sparks flew from the wand—and the dinosaur froze in its tracks.
"Why didn't I think of that?" muttered Waldo.
Winnie was still on her broom.
She took the wand from Cleo and flew around the museum, waving it.
Zap! Zap! Zap! Soon all the dinosaurs were lifeless bones again.
Mr. Freaky dusted off his suit.
"You see?" he said to Dr. Bones. "Everything is totally under control."
"I think this is enough excitement for one day," Miss Bungle announced.
She checked her watch. "It's nearly dinnertime.
Why don't we return to the education wing and eat?
Then we can settle down for the night.
I'm sure by tomorrow everyone will feel much better."
"But what about Uncle Tut?" Cleo protested.
"They're keeping him prisoner!"
"He's not a prisoner," Dr. Bones snapped, "and he's not your uncle.
He's an exhibit. He's been with us for decades."
Cleo folded her arms. "Well, he's been my uncle for centuries!"
"We're not going to solve this tonight," Miss Bungle said.
"Cleo, let's talk about this again in the morning."
"That's a fine idea." Dr. Bones scowled.
"I must get back to work.
Now I have to check on the dinosaur exhibits as well."
"I'm sorry." Waldo hung his head.
"It was an accident," he murmured.
Back in the education wing, the monsters ate dinner quietly.
After dinner Al Normal led them to the movie theater.
"Students, this is an absolutely thrilling documentary."
"Goody!" yelled a goblin.
"What's the film about?" Mog asked.
"The history of glaciers."
"Ugh!" All the monsters groaned.
"That sounds so boring," Mog complained.
"Now, students!" Mr. Freaky leaped to his feet.
"We are guests here. Show your monster manners, please."
The lights went out and the movie started.
Al Normal hurried off to help Dr. Bones lock up the building for the night.
Ben stared at the massive chunks of ice on the screen.
They were actually kind of interesting.
He turned toward Mog. "I never knew that—"
Zzzz. Zzzz. Mog was already snoring.
With a sigh, Ben turned back to the screen.
After the movie the monsters had a snack.
Then the kids started telling spooky people stories.
A goblin finally burst into tears. "I'm scared! I want my mommy!"
"Bedtime, everyone!" Mr. Freaky said, clapping his hands.
Soon all the monsters were settled into their beds for the night.
The girls were in one classroom with Miss Bungle.
The boys were in another with Mr. Freaky.
"Ha-ha!" Mog was laughing as he poked Ben.
"Check out Mr. Freaky's pajamas!"
Waldo climbed into his sleeping bag.
"Mr. Freaky, what about Cleo's uncle?" he asked.
"We can't just leave him here."
"We'll talk about it in the morning," Mr. Freaky said.
"I'm sure the people will be reasonable."
"They haven't been reasonable so far." Waldo sighed. "Poor Cleo."
Ben was sleeping near a desert display.
It had friendly-looking birds and snakes.
Mr. Freaky's snores echoed through the quiet room.
Most of the other monsters fell asleep fast too.
But Ben kept tossing and turning.
"So far this field trip has been a disaster," he thought.
"No wonder people are afraid of monsters."
Even worse, Dr. Bones was going to tell Mayor Hubbletree about the dinosaur incident.
Soon Monster Academy would be nothing but a pile of rubble.
Just then Ben heard something moving on the other side of the room.
A shadowy figure was creeping toward the classroom door.
The door opened, and the figure slipped out.
Ben got out of his sleeping bag and floated through the classroom door.
Ahead of him the shadowy figure was creeping down the corridor.
Ben floated after him.
"Who is that?" he thought.
The figure was holding some sort of book.
"Hey!" Ben called out, and the figure whirled around in surprise.
"Waldo!" Ben exclaimed. "What are you doing?"
"Phew! Thank goodness it's you!" Waldo looked relieved to see Ben.
"I couldn't sleep," the wizard explained.
"I kept thinking about Uncle Tut. I promised Cleo that I'd help her wake him up.
I've brought my spell book this time. I'm sure I can wake him up."
Ben didn't want to hurt Waldo's feelings.
But the wizard's spells rarely worked, and so many things had already gone wrong on this field trip.
"Um, Waldo, do you think a spell is safe?" Ben asked carefully.
"I mean, what if you make a mistake? Dr. Bones is already furious at us, and Miss Bungle said—"
"It'll be fine," Waldo said. "It can't hurt to try, right?"
"Um . . ." Ben didn't know what to say, so he just nodded slowly.
"Okay, well, I'll come with you, just in case something happens.
How are we going to get to Uncle Tut?
Al Normal said he locked the main entrance at eight o'clock."
"I bet we can go through the construction site, if we're careful," Waldo said.
"I saw some construction workers entering the museum from the education wing."
"Okay," Ben said with a shrug. "I guess we can try."
He and Waldo slipped downstairs to the first-floor construction area.
As they got closer, they noticed someone else had gotten there first.
"Cleo!" Ben whispered.
"What are you doing here?"
"I can't wait until morning," Cleo whispered back.
"I need to rescue my uncle now!"
Waldo held up his spell book. "Don't worry. We'll figure this out."
Ben looked around uneasily.
"Let's go," he whispered. "Before we get caught."
The three monsters examined the construction area.
It was still filled with scaffolding, tools, buckets, partially finished walls, and other obstacles.
Ben knew he'd have no trouble getting through, but his friends might.
"I'll go first," Ben said.
"I'll try to warn you guys about obstacles in our way."
Cleo and Waldo nodded, and Ben floated into the construction area.
"These workers are really sloppy," he whispered to Waldo and Cleo, who were following close behind.
"They've left buckets and tools everywhere. Watch your step."
"We will," Waldo replied.
"Ouch!" said Cleo.
Ben whirled around. "What's wrong?"
"My wrapping got caught on that nail."
She laughed nervously. "It would be really embarrassing if I unraveled."
They started forward again.
"Whoops!" said Waldo as something crashed loudly to the floor.
"What's wrong now?" Ben turned and saw Waldo lying on the ground, holding his ankle.
"I tripped on something," Waldo said.
"I twisted my ankle." He rubbed it. "Ouch."
"Can you stand?" Ben asked.
"Sure. I—Yow!" Waldo yelped as he stood, and his leg buckled under him.
Cleo looked worried. "I think you sprained your ankle, Waldo," she said.
"Or worse. We'll have to go back."
"No!" Waldo protested. "We can't give up on Uncle Tut."
"Look at you, Waldo," Cleo whispered.
"You can't walk. And if we get caught . . ."
"I can keep going," Ben said.
"I can move much more quickly than you guys. I can wake Uncle Tut on my own."
Cleo looked torn. "Are you sure, Ben?" she asked.
Ben shrugged. "I'll try my best."
"Thanks," Cleo said. She flashed him a grateful smile.
"I'll take Waldo back upstairs. I have some extra wrapping.
I bet I can wrap his ankle without Miss Bungle or Mr. Freaky finding out."
"Good luck!" Waldo whispered as Ben continued floating through the construction site.
Without the other two monsters slowing him down, Ben quickly made his way into the main part of the museum.
He floated toward the Egyptian display.
But before he could enter, he saw two figures sneaking into the exhibit.
"That's interesting," Ben thought. "Some other students are sneaking around the museum."
Ben floated toward a papyrus display.
Now he could see two zombies prowling around, whispering furiously to each other.
As Ben drew closer, he spotted something glinting in their pale hands.
"Huh," Ben thought. "What is that?
It looks like gold—" He gasped out loud. It was jewelry.
"Yikes!" he thought. "Those zombies haven't come to help Uncle Tut.
They're stealing the jewels from the Egyptian exhibit!"
"Stop!" Ben called to the zombies.
The two monsters jumped at the sound of his voice.
Then they dashed across the lobby, racing toward the construction area.
They dodged into the construction with Ben following behind.
"Come back here!" Ben shouted.
It was dark, and the zombies were a good distance away from him.
But these zombies were taller than the zombies at Monster Academy, and—Brrpp! Brrpp!
Suddenly an alarm blared and lights flashed on. Brrpp! Brrpp!
"Don't move!" yelled a stern voice.
Ben froze in terror as two museum guards ran toward him.
"We caught a thief!" said one guard. His nametag read Bob.
"It's a ghost!" said the other one. Her name was Hazel.
"B-b-but . . . It wasn't me!"
Ben tried to explain everything, but the guards just stared at him.
"Don't try to escape, ghost!" Bob snapped.
"The director will be here in a minute."
The two guards each grabbed one of Ben's arms.
Ben moaned. He knew he could float away from them, but what good would it do?
He'd just wait for Mr. Freaky and Miss Bungle to arrive and explain everything.
Soon Dr. Bones stomped through the construction and into the lobby.
"What's going on here?" she demanded.
"This ghost was stealing Egyptian jewelry," Hazel said.
"But don't worry, Dr. Bones." She smiled proudly. "We caught him."
"I didn't steal anything!" Ben protested.
"Empty your pockets," Bob ordered.
Ben did, but all he had was a gum wrapper and a few coins.
"Where'd you put the jewels?" Bob demanded.
"I didn't steal the jewels," Ben repeated.
"But I saw who did. Like I said—it was two zombies!"
"Where's Mr. Freaky?" Dr. Bones demanded.
"I told Mayor Hubbletree that this monster visit would lead to trouble."
She sneered at Ben.
"But I didn't expect you monsters to steal museum treasures."
Ben shook his head, trying to explain to the museum director now.
"I saw some zombies. But they're not from Monster Academy!"
Dr. Bones stared at Ben.
"You're the only monsters here today. No monsters ever come to People Place."
"Except for Uncle Tut," Ben muttered under his breath.
But Dr. Bones had a good point. Where had the zombies come from?
"We'll get to the bottom of this situation."
Dr. Bones looked at the guards. "Bring this ghost to my office."
"Yes, Dr. Bones," Bob said. "Should we call the police?"
"No," Dr. Bones said quickly.
"The museum doesn't need bad publicity.
It's lucky I was working late.
Bring the rest of the monsters too."
The guards led Ben outside, taking the long way to Dr. Bones' office.
The museum director unlocked doors with her keys as they went, relocking everything behind them.
Soon Ben was sitting in a chair in Dr. Bones' office.
Mr. Freaky paced up and down the director's office nervously.
"Dr. Bones," the principal said.
"Ben insists that some strangers stole the jewels.
I'm sure he's telling the truth."
Dr. Bones glared at Ben.
"Where are these two zombies?" she demanded.
She pointed to the hallway, where the rest of the monsters were lined up, looking sleepy and scared.
"Do you see them out there?"
Ben peered through the glass and then shook his head.
"They're not there. At first I thought maybe the zombies were new students.
But they are definitely not from Monster Academy."
"There are exactly three zombies on this trip," Mr. Freaky said.
"And they are all standing in the line outside!"
The guards scowled. "That ghost is lying!" Hazel said.
"Dr. Bones, we need to search everyone!"
One by one, the guards made all the monsters come in and empty their sleeping bags, their backpacks, their lunchboxes, and their pockets.
The monsters' belongings piled up.
The guards found spell books, Mog's collection of comic books, Scary People Stories, and snacks—dried bat wings and crunchy spiders.
But there were no Egyptian jewels.
"Where did you stash the loot, ghost?" Bob demanded. "Confess!"
"I didn't steal anything!" Ben insisted.
"How many times do I have to tell you?"
Mr. Freaky's noses were wiggling like mad.
"Where's Mayor Hubbletree?
This situation is totally out of control!"
By now it was very late.
Dr. Bones turned to the guards.
She looked exhausted.
"It's time to bring the suspect to the police station," she murmured.
"I'll meet you there soon."
"Okay, Dr. Bones," the guards said.
Dr. Bones got her coat from a nearby rack.
As she put it on, something fell out of her pocket and clattered to the floor.
Everyone stared at the object—it was a glittering piece of golden jewelry!
Ben blinked in surprise as he looked from the gold jewelry to Dr. Bones.
The guards rushed toward her.
"Where's the rest of the loot?" Hazel demanded. "Confess!"
Dr. Bones scowled. "This is ridiculous.
Why would I steal from my own museum?"
"Maybe the museum isn't paying you enough," Bob suggested.
"Maybe she's trying to make monsters look bad!" Mr. Freaky snapped.
"This is absurd!" Dr. Bones said, sighing.
"I'm going to call the police. They'll find the real culprit."
"Stay right there!" ordered Bob.
He pushed Dr. Bones into a chair.
Ben watched the two guards huddle, listening as they whispered back and forth.
"It's too soon to call the police."
"If we can find the rest of the loot, the mayor will probably give us a reward!"
Mr. Freaky's face was turning redder and redder.
"Call the police right now!" he demanded.
"If you don't, I'm going to take all the students back to Monsterville!"
"You're not going anywhere, buddy!" Hazel snarled.
"We have a plan," the other guard said.
"We'll call the police if we don't find the jewels by morning."
"You can't hold us here all night!" Dr. Bones complained.
"Yes, we can." Bob grinned.
"We'll lock you in the Old West jail exhibit."
"What about those zombies?" Ben said.
Hazel shrugged. "The only zombies I see are the ones in your group."
"Grr!" Ben growled with frustration.
"This is an outrage!" Mr. Freaky stamped a foot.
"Wait till Mayor Hubbletree hears how we've been treated.
He said people would be friendly and kind.
But instead we've been treated like—"
"Monsters!" Bob snapped.
The guards left Ben and Dr. Bones in the director's office.
They locked the rest of the monsters in the classrooms and then grabbed Ben and Dr. Bones.

The voices seemed to be coming from inside a newly built wall.

Ben floated toward the new wall.
Cautiously, he poked his head through.
On the other side, he saw two construction workers and a bag—filled with the stolen Egyptian jewels!
"Boo!" Ben shouted.
The startled thieves jumped. "The ghost!" one cried.
Both sprang to their feet and rushed out of a hidden door in the wall.

He floated after the workers as fast as he could.
Crash! Just then Gaby burst through the construction area.

They ran toward the Egyptian exhibit.
Winnie swooped after them on her broom. "I'll get them!"

The two thieves dove to the floor.
Winnie steered downward, zooming faster than Ben had ever seen her fly.
Crash! Her broom smashed into Uncle Tut's display case.

This time a spell zapped Uncle Tut, still sleeping inside the case. Sha-zam!

Then he dipped the spoon into the stew and tasted it.

Then he looked at Ben.
"You used rotten nectarines, didn't you? And do I taste worms?"

After Mr. Icky had picked Ben to be on the TV show, everyone was excited.

Other monsters patted him on the back and gave him the claws-up sign.

He made himself think about possible birthday presents for Winnie.
"What do witches like?" he asked himself.
He thought about Winnie's favorite things.
She loved to fly. Maybe she'd like a new broom?
Ben pulled out his phone.
He found a website that sold flying brooms.
One broom was shaped like a lightning bolt.
Ben watched a demonstration video.
The broom was so fast, it left a streak of fire across the sky.
"Wow!" Ben said. "Winnie would love this broom. How much does it cost?"
He scrolled down the page and found the price.
"Six thousand dollars?" Ben gulped.
There was no way he could afford that.
He looked at some other flying broom websites.
The cheapest broom Ben saw was still too expensive.
It was five hundred dollars, and it looked like a piece of junk.
Ben's shoulders slumped, and he put his phone away.
As Ben brooded, the hedge that ran down the side of his yard shook slightly.
Something was rustling on the ground.
Ben peered over.
"Who's there?" he said. There was no answer.
For a moment the hedge was still.
Then it moved again.
"Something is in there," Ben thought.
He floated over for a closer look.
He moved some of the leaves out of the way and looked in at the branches.
A pair of glowing eyes stared back at him.
A chill ran down Ben's spine. "It's a . . . a kitten!"
Meow! The tiny black kitten leaped out of the hedge and straight toward Ben.
Ben jumped to the side.
The kitten landed on the grass.
It looked up at Ben and hissed.

Ben ran toward his back door with the kitten chasing him all the way.

He shot across his backyard.
The kitten sprinted behind him, hissing and pouncing at his feet.
Ben floated through his fence and into a neighbor's backyard.
He stopped to catch his breath.
"Whew! I think I lost—"
Hiss! Meow! The kitten was on top of the fence.
It leaped down and fell right through Ben.
"Ahh!" Ben dashed through the neighbor's yard and onto the street.
The kitten was still right behind him.
Ben darted upward, flying over the trees.
Looking down, he saw the kitten.
It was still hissing at him, but at least it couldn't fly.
With a sigh of relief, Ben flew home.
On Wednesday morning Ben was one of the first students to arrive in the cooking classroom.

After school Ben hurried into Ghoulie's Jewelry Shop.

Mrs. Ghoulie pointed at a small rack at the end of the counter.

Ben went over to the rack.
He saw a necklace for fifteen dollars.

On Friday morning Sid agreed to take care of the kitten until after school.
"I just have to get through this cooking show," Ben said.
"Then I'll find a home for the kitten."

At Monster Academy everyone was outside, waiting eagerly for Kids' Kitchen Showdown to start.
"The master chef has arrived!" a mummy shouted.
Ben grinned as monsters patted him on the back.
Mr. Freaky's noses were wiggling madly.
Sweat dripped down Mayor Hubbletree's forehead.

Gaby pointed toward three human kids.

Rebecca Gold said nothing.

Mayor Hubbletree hurried over.

"Are you sure this place is safe?"

Mayor Hubbletree wiped more sweat from his forehead as everyone headed inside.
The cooking classroom still smelled like hot sauce.
Ben and Waldo glanced at each other.
"It smells weird in here," Viv Stryder said.

Crew members got to work setting up lights and cameras.

Ben leaned closer to Waldo.
"We obviously didn't clean up all of the hot sauce.

Bright light flooded the room.
Cameras rolled.
Ben was so nervous, he barely heard Viv Stryder introduce all the contestants.
The host was still speaking to one of the cameras.
"The first dish for today will be mac and cheese. Time starts . . . now!"
Ben hurried into the pantry for ingredients.
"Eww!" one human kid said. "They have canned slugs here!"

Ben returned to his workspace.
He put bat claws, leeches, and mud into a food processor.
Then he shredded some moldy cheese.
Once his macaroni was boiled, Ben put everything into a pan.

He noticed the wall was shaking even more now.

"Is there something alive in there?"

"Ben will present his dish to the judges first."
Ben took a deep breath.
Then he picked up his mac and cheese and floated up to the judges' table.

Ben grinned.
"Right then," Bolton Ramsey said.

"I'm not eating any of this monster's food!"

Rebecca Gold spoke up.
"I'd like to try your mac and cheese."

"I believe it's important to try new things."

"You two have no sense of adventure."
Rumble! Rumble! The wall shook violently.
Ben tried to ignore it as he spooned out some of his mac and cheese for Rebecca Gold.
"It smells wonderful, Ben." The judge took some on her fork and lifted it toward her mouth.
Rumble! Rumble!

Crew members tripped over one another, all trying to reach the door.

Mayor Hubbletree held up his hands.
"Everyone, please remain calm! Everything is totally under control!"

"Yikes!" Mayor Hubbletree cried as the sauce oozed toward him.
The mayor scrambled onto a chair.
"Where's Freaky? This is his fault!"
Ben looked around.
The principal was huddled in a corner with his face in his hands.
Bolton Ramsey stood up.
"I'm leaving!" He stormed out of the room, with Margaret Oh following him.
Rebecca Gold was still sitting at the table.

"Mmm. Delicious!"

Rebecca Gold looked around at the chaos.
A lightbulb exploded.
A cameraman held a half-melted camera in his hands. Wires sizzled.

Viv Stryder hopped down from the table and made her way to the door.

Mayor Hubbletree wiped his brow.
"Why do things like this constantly happen around here, Freaky?

Mr. Freaky blew his noses.
"I don't know, Mayor. I really don't know."

Meow! The kitten swatted at Ben's feet.
"You have a lot of energy today," he said to the kitten.

The kitten leaped up, nearly knocking the gift out of Ben's hand.
When Ben turned to leave, the kitten followed.

He shut the door and floated down the street.
The kitten followed, jumping up and swatting at his feet.
"Stop it," Ben said.
As he turned to scold the kitten, he floated into a tree.
"Ugh!" Ben cried.

"This is unbelievable! I haven't gotten stuck like this in a long time.

"No!" Ben cried as the gift slid into the drain.

Mr. Freaky tripped on a bucket as he walked back toward the microphone.

"We have study hall after lunch," Gaby said to Mog.
"Let's go to the library now and get started.
We can read about Monsterville history—that's the best place to start."
"Okay," Mog said.
The two of them returned their trays to the kitchen and hurried off to the library.
Winnie stood up. "Come on, Waldo.
We have to get started too.
Let's go to the lab and figure out a spell.
See you later, Ben."
Ben sighed as the two of them left.
"This situation stinks," he thought.
Somebody was bound to get mad at him.
Finally he decided he wasn't hungry anymore, so he picked up his tray.
As he headed toward the garbage can, a blob waved to him.
"Hey, Ben, are you going to eat those toad toes? I'm really hungry today."
"Nope. You can have them," Ben said.
"Just return my tray to the kitchen when you're done, okay?"
"Don't worry about that," the blob said. "I'll eat the tray too!"
"Great," Ben said. But he didn't feel great.
If only Gaby and Waldo hadn't made this stupid bet!
A few minutes later, Ben floated through the door of the science lab.
"How's it going in here?" he said.
Winnie looked up and smiled.
She was stirring a potion in a big cauldron as Waldo handed her some ingredients.
The liquid inside the pot glowed green as Winnie mixed it.
"We're brewing a location spell," she said.
"Can I help?" Ben asked.
"Sure." Winnie gestured toward some supplies on a high shelf.
"Can you hand Waldo that big sack of lizard scales?"
"The green ones or the gold ones?" Ben asked.
"Gold," Waldo said. "As in gold treasure."
"Got it." Ben had to use both hands to get the heavy sack off the shelf.
He lowered it and then handed the sack to Waldo.
"Ah-choo!" Waldo sneezed.
Ben and Winnie immediately braced themselves, but this time nothing happened.
Waldo grinned. "I think my cold is finally getting better!"
He tipped the sack and started to pour the lizard scales into the cauldron.
Suddenly Winnie yelped.
"Wait! Waldo! Ben gave you the green scales!"
She groaned. "Oh no. Now we'll have to start all over again."
"But . . ." Ben shook his head in confusion as he stared at the sack.
He was sure he'd given Waldo the right ingredient.
"I know I grabbed the gold—"
Winnie cut him off with a smile.
"On second thought, we're good," she said.
"We don't really need any help.
Like my mom says, too many witches spoil the potion.
Why don't you go see how Gaby and Mog are doing?"
Ben blinked at her.
He couldn't tell if she was trying to get rid of him or trying to be fair.
"Okay," he said with a shrug.
"See you later. Call if you need me."
As he left, he noticed that the bag of green scales was still on the shelf.
"I did get the right bag!" Ben thought.
"Waldo's sneeze must have changed the gold scales to green."
Ben felt annoyed. He'd tried to help Winnie, but Waldo had messed it up.
When Ben got to the school library, Gaby and Mog were already rushing out.
They were both grinning.
"You two look happy," Ben said.
"Did you find the treasure already?"
"Nope," Mog said. "But Gaby thought of a really good clue."
"I remembered that Pedro mentioned a painting," Gaby told Ben.
"He said an artist painted him before he buried the treasure."
"Right." Ben nodded.
"So that painting could hold a clue to finding the treasure!" Gaby said.
"We looked up information about pirate art," said Mog.
"And we found out where that painting is."
"Where?" Ben asked.
"At the Monsterville Historical Society," Gaby said.
"They've got some pirate artifacts there."
"We're going there after school," Mog added.
"You can come with us if you want."
"Okay . . . maybe," Ben said.
"If I'm not busy helping Winnie and Waldo."
After school Ben couldn't find Winnie.
So he went with Gaby and Mog to the Monsterville Historical Society.
The historical society was located in an old haunted house on the edge of town.
"Whoa, look at all this stuff," Mog burst out.
"Yikes," Ben added.
The ground floor of the building was packed with objects.
There were old toys and dusty books and racks crammed with robes, capes, and vests.
Huge mummies and wax monster figures stood along the walls of one room.
File cabinets overflowing with papers and old photographs filled another room.
Gaby scratched her head, looking overwhelmed.
"I hope we can find that painting of Pedro in here.
The building closes at six, and this could take longer than I thought."
"Maybe we can find a guide to help us," Ben said.
They looked around until they finally spotted a mummy wearing a guide badge.
Ben floated over to him.
"Excuse me, sir. We're looking for a specific painting of Monsterville," he said.
"It's an old painting showing Pedro the Pirate burying his treasure.
Do you know where it is?"
"Second floor. Outlaws section," the guide said.
"You can't miss it."
"Thanks," Gaby said. The three of them hurried toward the staircase.
"Hey, Waldo and Winnie just walked in!" Mog said.
"Why are they here?" Ben wondered aloud.
"Who cares?" Gaby said. "Come on. Let's find that painting!"
"You two can probably find it on your own," Ben said.
"I'll go say hello to Winnie and Waldo. Maybe they need some help now."
"Okay," Gaby said.
"But don't tell them about the painting. That's our clue."
"I will. I mean, I won't. Don't worry, Gaby.
I won't say a word about the painting."
Gaby and Mog tore upstairs.
Waldo and Winnie were still standing near the front entrance.
Ben floated up to them as they finished talking to a guide.
"Hi, Ben," Winnie said.
"How'd you know we were coming to the historical society?"
"I came with Gaby and Mog," Ben said.
"Oh. They're here too?" Waldo asked.
He sounded funny because he was pinching his nose to stop himself from sneezing.
"Did they find a clue that led here?"
"I can't talk about that, remember?" Ben replied.
"I'm helping both teams. What are you guys doing here?"
"We created a Magic Mirror spell," Waldo said.
"Huh?" Ben asked.
"It's a mirror for finding stuff. But the mirror works only one time," Winnie explained.
"We asked it to show us Pirate Pedro's gold."
"But it showed us an image of a golden compass from Pedro's pirate ship," Waldo said.
"The guide said the compass is definitely here—somewhere."
"When we find it," Winnie added, "we're going to cast another spell.
It'll take us to the burial site."
"Want me to help you look for the compass?" Ben asked.
"Okay," Winnie said. "The guide said it's in one of the back rooms."
"We're going to need to get permission to take the compass with us," Waldo said.
"Maybe you can talk with somebody about that?
We got Mr. Freaky to write a note."
Waldo handed Ben a sheet of paper.
"We told him we're working on a project about pirate ships."
"We didn't want to tell him about the treasure until we found it," Winnie said.
"No problem," Ben said.
"I'll go to the visitors' office. I think it's on the second floor."
Inside the visitors' office, Ben explained the situation to a bored-looking skeleton.
The skeleton barely looked at Mr. Freaky's note before stamping it, "Approved."
"Thanks," Ben said.
On his way back downstairs, Ben saw Gaby and Mog staring at a painting in a gold frame.
It showed Pedro as a young pirate skeleton.
He was standing on top of a chest inside a deep hole, looking proud as the sun sank behind him.
Nearby a few other pirates stood with shovels under a small oak tree.
Mog was quickly sketching the painting as Gaby wrote in a small notepad.
"Hey, Ben!" Gaby waved excitedly.
"We found the painting!" Mog said.
"We're not allowed to take a picture of it so I'm trying to draw it."
"We see a bunch of clues," Gaby said.
"Hmm." Ben looked carefully at the painting.
"All I see is the treasure chest, some pirates and Pedro, and a tree."
"Those are all clues," Gaby replied.
"The leaves on the tree show that it was early fall.
The position of the sun and the shadows tell us it was late in the day."
Mog's eyes gleamed.
"And the size of that treasure chest tells us something else—that treasure is huge!"
After studying the painting, Gaby and Mog went to look at some old maps of Monsterville.
Ben went back downstairs with the permission form.
He floated around, looking for Winnie and Waldo.
"Being on two different teams is exhausting," he thought.
"I hope somebody finds this treasure soon."
"Ben!" Winnie called to him from the front entrance.
"Did you get the approval? We found Pedro's compass!"
"Cool," Ben said. "And yes, you have permission to take it."
"Great!" Winnie said. "Let's go!"
The three of them dashed outside—and the sky instantly flashed with weird green light.
"Yikes!" Ben stopped in his tracks. "What's going on?"
"I think it's our spell," Waldo replied.
"We cast a magnet spell—it makes the compass attracted to Pedro's treasure."
Winnie held the compass in front of her as they hurried along Buzzard Place.
The compass needle seemed to be pointing at the Monsterville clock tower.
"Why didn't the first spell lead you right to the treasure?" Ben asked.
Waldo shrugged. "We don't know," he admitted.
"Although we did make a few mistakes with the potion, and I still have this dumb cold."
"Plus, I'm pretty new to spell casting," Winnie said.
They turned left at the clock tower, and the needle pointed them toward Swampside Lane.
By now the sky had grown dark.
A full moon hung over the bubbling green swamp as they raced along.
"Ah-choo!" Waldo sneezed a few times and had to slow down to catch his breath.
Ben was panting too.
"Why are you guys trying so hard to win?" he asked.
"It's only a friendly bet.
I mean, you're going to use the treasure to help fix the school, no matter who wins. Right?"
Waldo nodded. "Yeah . . ."
"So don't you think it's kind of dumb to try to prove that magic is better than detective work?" Ben went on.
"I mean, what's the point of arguing about it?"
Winnie burst out laughing. "It is kind of dumb," she admitted.
"But it sounded fun to me—like a scavenger hunt, as Mog said."
"Yeah," Waldo added with a grin.
"Besides, a wizard has to defend his magical powers.
Ah-ah-ah-choo!" He sneezed loudly, and the three of them turned green.
Winnie moaned. "Not again."
"Hey!" Waldo said. "I know! I'll cast a spell to fix my cold."
"No!" Winnie said sharply.
"No more spells for now. Let's just keep searching for the treasure."
Soon the compass was pulling the three of them up Cemetery Hill.
At the top they paused so that Winnie could reverse Waldo's green spell.
"Phew, that's better," Winnie said. "I didn't like being green."
Ben was staring down at all the lights below.
To the left he could see lights twinkling in People Place.
To the right Monsterville was lit up too.
"It's a nice view from up here."
"My parents hike up the hill sometimes," Waldo said.
"Enough small talk, guys." Winnie was staring at the compass.
"We're almost at the burial site." She pointed below.
"The compass is pointing down the hill, past that huge tree, and right at . . ."
Ben's eyes went wide as he realized where, exactly, the compass was pointing. "Monster Academy!"
Waldo gasped. "The treasure must be buried under our school!"
"Yep." Winnie took another look at the compass.
Sure enough, its needle pointed right at the school.
"Could it be wrong?" Ben asked.
"I don't think so," Waldo replied.
"I guess we'll find out," Winnie said.
Her voice shook. "I wonder what we'll find—piles of gold?"
Ben remembered the huge chest he'd seen in the painting of Pedro, but he didn't say anything.
That clue belonged to Gaby and Mog.
"Yes!" Waldo said.
"We're going to find tons of gold.
Maybe some other valuable stuff too, like pearls and jewelry.
Pirates stole all kinds of loot."
"Let's go," Ben said eagerly.
The three of them rushed down the hill and wound through the streets toward Monster Academy.
Even though school had ended hours ago, a few lights were on inside the school building.
"Someone's working late," Ben said.
"Maybe Mr. Bog is still mopping up all those puddles."
"Or trying to fix the heat again," Winnie said.
Just then Ben spotted some figures near the big tree close to the front of the building.
One of the figures was very tall.
"It's Gaby and Mog!" he said.
"Looks like they tracked the treasure here too!"
"Hi, guys!" Winnie called to Gaby and Mog.
They looked up in surprise.
"Hey!" Gaby said. "Did you guys track the treasure here too?"
Waldo smiled at her. "Yep."
"We followed some clues in an old painting at the Monsterville Historical Society," Gaby said.
Then she gestured at the old tree.
"There was a tree in the painting. We think it might be this one."
"It's grown a lot since Pedro buried the treasure," Mog said.
Winnie held up the gold compass.
"We found Pedro's old compass and put a spell on it.
I guess it worked just as well as detective work."
"Which means everybody is a winner!" Ben said brightly.
"So you guys don't have to compete anymore. We're all on the same team now."
"That was so much fun," Mog said.
"We still need to find the treasure," Winnie reminded everyone.
"All we know is that it's buried near this tree," Gaby said.
She glanced at the school building.
"Maybe it's even buried under the school building."
"That's what we were thinking too," Waldo said.
"We can try using the compass to track the exact spot."
"First we'd better find a shovel," Mog said.
"Let's see if there are any shovels in the equipment shed."
The kids found one shovel in a shed near the soccer field.
When they headed back to the front of the school building, the main doors suddenly flew open.
Mr. Freaky, Mayor Hubbletree, and Pirate Pedro came out.
As the grown-ups talked to one another, none of them noticed the students standing near the tree.
"I think they're talking about Monster Academy," Winnie whispered.
Ben stepped closer so he could eavesdrop.
"Thank you for meeting with us tonight, Pedro," Mayor Hubbletree was saying.
"Obviously this is an emergency situation involving Freaky's poor school."
"You're welcome, mate," the pirate said. "I'm glad to help, if I can."
"Thank you, Pedro. I'm sure your fundraising will save Monster Academy," Mr. Freaky said.
"Your Career Day talk was so inspiring.
Lots of citizens of Monsterville—"
"And People Place!" The mayor cut in.
"Both monsters and humans will enjoy hearing your pirate tales," Mr. Freaky went on.
"Pirating is such an exciting job—it's almost as thrilling as being the principal of Monster Academy."
Just then a breeze blew, and boards flew off some windows on the second floor of the school.
"Indeed!" Mayor Hubbletree declared.
"Pedro, your fundraising talks will be an enormous success. Hundreds of people—"
"And monsters!" Mr. Freaky said.
"Will happily attend," the mayor went on.
"And most importantly they'll pay good money to hear your tales.
The funds you raise might even be enough to repair Freaky's school."
He shook his head as the flagpole snapped in two.
"I don't know how you monsters put up with this place.
Everything is falling apart, Freaky."
Mr. Freaky took out his handkerchief and blew his noses.
"With this budget crisis, we've gotten a bit behind on repairs.
But everything is totally under control at Monster Academy."
"Hmpf," the mayor grunted. "I'm not so sure about that."
"Well, I'm happy to help," Pedro repeated.
"Talking to the students was great fun. It reminded me of the good old days with my band of pirates." He sighed.
"We'd all sail the seas together for months.
Why, this one time, when we met Awful Ollie the Orange . . ."
Pedro launched into another pirating tale.
After a few minutes, Mr. Freaky and the mayor looked a little bored.
But Ben saw that Mog's eyes were glowing.
"Pedro is so lucky," Mog whispered. "Being a pirate sounds awesome."
"Ollie and his men had no idea what we were plotting," Pedro went on.
"They were just passing the time on the deck of their ship, singing and playing their instruments.
That's when we jumped aboard with our swords and cried—"
"Shiver me timbers!" Mog blurted out loudly.
"What was that?" Mr. Freaky gasped, and spun toward Ben and the others.
"What are you students doing here?"
Mayor Hubbletree squinted at them through the darkness.
"It's very late, Freaky. Shouldn't those monsters be home in bed?"
"We're . . . uh, searching for Pedro's treasure," Waldo said.
The adults chuckled.
"How nice," Mayor Hubbletree said.
The mayor came over and patted Mog's head.
"Treasure hunting! That sounds like a fun activity, kids . . . er, I mean, monsters."
Winnie looked annoyed.
"We're not playing treasure hunting," she said.
"This is for real."
"Yeah," Mog said, rubbing his head.
"We've actually found Pedro's lost treasure.
And guess where it's buried."
"Where?" said Mr. Freaky, Mayor Hubbletree, and Pedro all at once.
Mog grinned. "Here at Monster Academy!"
"What?" Mayor Hubbletree and Pirate Pedro looked stunned.
Mr. Freaky blew his noses.
"You found Pedro's treasure? Are you sure it's buried at Monster Academy?"
Ben nodded. He and the others quickly explained how they'd tracked down the treasure.
Pedro looked excited. "You aren't just trying to fool an old pirate, are you?"
"No, sir," Mog said. "We found your treasure, but . . ." He looked down.
"We wondered . . . well . . . we wondered . . ."
"If you'd donate it to our school!" Winnie finished for him.
"Of course, I'll donate the treasure to the school," Pedro replied.
"I'm an old skeleton now. And I'd be proud to help Monster Academy."
Mr. Freaky's noses twitched with delight.
"Wonderful!" he cried. "With this treasure we'll be able to make the repairs!"
"Great work, young monsters," Mayor Hubbletree declared.
"Now take us to the treasure!"
"Er . . ." Winnie checked the magic compass.
"We don't know exactly where it is, but we know we're close."
Gaby glanced at the tree and then back at the school building.
"It's got to be inside the school."
"You mean under the school," Ben said.
"It might not be easy to dig up the school building."
"Now wait a minute, students.
Nobody is going to dig up Monster Academy!" Mr. Freaky said.
"Hmm." Mayor Hubbletree rubbed his chin.
"Actually, Freaky, I have a wonderful idea.
We can just knock down your school and dig until we find the treasure."
Mr. Freaky turned pale. "Knock down the school?"
"It's the easiest and fastest way.
Besides," the mayor added with a laugh, "your school is already falling apart."
"You can't destroy our school," Mog said.
"Of course I can," Mayor Hubbletree said.
"People Place owns this land, in case you monsters have all forgotten.
That makes the treasure mine.
But because I'm such a nice guy, I'll share it with you.
After we flatten Monster Academy, I'll use some of the treasure to build you a nice, new school."
"But we like this school!" Gaby blurted out.
"And it'll take years to build a new Monster Academy."
"Nonsense," the mayor said.
"You'll like your new school much better than this dump.
We'll get rid of that nasty cafeteria and the library full of cobwebs." He shivered.
"Not to mention the leaky roof, peeling paint, and broken windows."
He pulled out his phone and began tapping.
"There! It's all arranged. I've contacted People Place Wrecking.
The bulldozers will be here at sunrise."
All the monsters gasped. "Sunrise?"
"Oh no!" Mr. Freaky wailed. "This is terrible!"
But Mayor Hubbletree was beaming.
"I'd better get some sleep.
I want to be here at the crack of dawn when the bulldozers start rolling. Good night, everyone."
With that, a limousine pulled up in front of the building and whisked the mayor away.
The monsters stood on the steps in stunned silence for a moment.
"I wish the office ogre were here right now," Mr. Freaky moaned.
"Or Miss Bungle. She always knows what to do."
He glanced quickly at the students.
"I'll be in my office, thinking, if you need me."
He headed for the building entrance.
"I'll call your parents to let them know you're staying at Monster Academy tonight for a special project."
"This is awful," Mog said. "What are we going to do?"
Suddenly Pedro brightened.
"I know! I'll gather my old pirate band!"
He drew his sword and waved it.
"We'll battle those bulldozers as if they were enemy ships.
Don't worry, students! I'll be back at dawn with my crew to save the day!"
Pedro hurried off into the darkness.
"Whew!" Mog said. "That's a relief. The pirates are going to save Monster Academy."
Winnie bit her lip.
"I don't know, Mog. Pedro doesn't know anything about our school.
Or the humans in People Place."
"Yeah," Gaby added.
"And what if Mayor Hubbletree keeps the treasure for himself?"
"I don't think he'd do that," Ben said.
"But we can't count on the grown-ups to save our school.
There's only one thing to do—find the treasure ourselves, before sunrise!"
"Yes!" the others cried. They all ran into the school.
"Based on the shadows in the painting, I think the treasure is buried on the east side of the building," Gaby said.
"That's what the golden compass says too!" Winnie said. "Let's go!"
The compass led them down a dark hallway.
"This way," Winnie said, pointing to the right. "We take this turn and—"
Boom! She slammed hard into a wall.
"Ugh!" Ben groaned as he bumped into the wall, right behind Winnie.
"I think there's a boiler room on the other side of this wall."
"Maybe we can cut through the gym," Gaby said. "Come on!"
The five friends dodged through the gym equipment and reached the far door.
In the hallway, they started following the compass again.
At last they came to a glass door.
"The greenhouse!" Gaby said.
"I hope the treasure is buried here," Waldo said.
"The floor of the greenhouse is dirt—it should be easy to dig."
They went inside and Winnie ran along, following the compass.
"It's buried right here!" she cried, tracing a big X on the ground.
"X marks the spot!" Mog grinned and started digging.
They found some more shovels in the greenhouse, and soon everyone was digging—and sweating.
They dug for hours.
Finally Gaby stopped to rest. "It's hot in here," she said.
"And we're making such slow progress. We don't have much time left."
"I need a snack," Mog complained. "And some sleep."
"Hey!" Waldo snapped his fingers.
"I'll use magic to make the shovels dig on their own!"
He started to cast a spell. "Shovels strong and shovels true—"
"Waldo—" Winnie warned.
"Do the digging for me and—ah-ah-ah . . . !"
"Uh-oh," Mog murmured.
"Choo!" Waldo sneezed, and all the shovels turned into worms.
The worms wriggled away before Winnie could try to turn them back into shovels.
"Ack!" Mog cried. "Now what are we going to do?"
The kids slumped to the ground, dirty and exhausted.
Nobody said anything until Ben got to his feet.
"I'll look around," he said. "Maybe there are some other tools we can use for digging."
Rumble! Just then Ben heard something outside. "Oh no!" he cried.
"The wrecking crew!" Soon bulldozers, wrecking balls, and steam shovels would be destroying their school!
"Steam shovels!" Ben blurted out. "Winnie, can you make a magical steam shovel to dig faster?"
"I don't know anything about steam shovels!" Winnie cried.
"I'm still learning magic, and I don't have a spell book."
Waldo jumped to his feet. "I can try—"
"No!" everyone shouted.
"I wasn't going to try magic." Waldo looked offended.
"I just wanted to explain how steam shovels work."
"Tell me!" Winnie cried.
Waldo quickly described how steam shovels work, sketching diagrams in the dirt.
Then Winnie closed her eyes.
"Shovel, shovel, soil and rubble . . . Help us dig out of this trouble!"
Zap! A steam shovel appeared and went instantly to work.
Dirt flew all over the greenhouse.
Clunk! At last the steam shovel hit something.
"The treasure chest!" Mog cried.
Ben glanced out the window.
Bulldozers had nearly reached the school's driveway.
"Quick! Let's lift it out of the ground!"
The steam shovel lifted the chest out of the ground.
"Open the doors," Winnie said. "Let's get the chest outside!"
Waldo threw open the greenhouse doors, and they hauled the heavy chest out onto the lawn.
Mayor Hubbletree and Mr. Freaky were standing near the school's main entrance.
And Ben spotted someone else. Pedro!
He was racing toward the bulldozer with two other pirates.
The old skeletons waved their swords.
"Stop!" Pedro yelled.
"You'll have to go through us to knock down Monster Academy!"
The three pirates leaped in front of the bulldozers.
"Pedro, get out of the way," Mayor Hubbletree commanded.
Pedro stood fiercely with his crew.
"Wait!" Mog waved his arms madly.
"Pedro! Mr. Freaky! We found the treasure!"
"You don't have to knock down the school!" Ben yelled.
Pedro looked over and saw the chest. "Whew!" he said.
"To tell you the truth, I wasn't sure we could stop these bulldozers."
The mayor rushed over.
"Open that chest!"
Pedro broke the rusty old lock with his sword.
He threw open the lid.
The mayor bent forward. "What's this?" he bellowed.
Ben floated closer. Inside the chest lay not gold but . . . "Huh? Musical instruments?"
Pedro grinned. "We were the best pirate band on the seas!"
He reached for a xylophone with his bony fingers.
Mr. Freaky collapsed onto the ground.
"Monster Academy is doomed! Music won't save the school."
"Of course it will!" Pedro said.
"I could find only our drummer and banjo player, but we can still put on a concert."
"Pedro and the Pirates will fill Monster Stadium!" Waldo said.
"They'll definitely raise enough money to repair our school."
Mr. Freaky slowly climbed to his feet.
"I told you students not to worry.
Everything at Monster Academy is totally under control!"
Ben turned to Mog, who was holding a banjo.
"Still want to be a pirate when you grow up?"
"Nah." Mog shook his head and strummed the banjo.
"Maybe I'll join a band instead!"
"Art Week is finally here!" Gaby exclaimed. "I'm so excited!"
It was Monday morning, and Ben was walking to school with Gaby.
"I'm not into art," he said.
"But I am excited. I've got my first assignment for the Monster Academy Times.
I'm supposed to write an article about Art Week.
If the article is good, I might get some more assignments."
"Well, you'll definitely need photos to go with your article," Gaby replied.
"So much great artwork will be on display."
"Yep." Ben nodded.
"Do you know that ghost named Pixel?"
Gaby shook her head.
"He's in sixth grade.
He's really good at photography.
He's taking a bunch of photos for my article."
"Cool." Gaby giggled.
"I heard Mr. Freaky is working on something special for Art Week.
I wonder what it is."
When Ben and Gaby reached their school, they walked up the steps and entered.
It was early, but the halls of Monster Academy were already bustling with activity.
Near the main entrance, students were hanging up art as the art teacher, Ms. Van Ghoul, called out instructions.
"Zombies, don't drool on the eighth-graders' portraits!
And, mummies, don't trip on your wrapping—you'll drop that beautiful pottery!"
Several witches were hanging up a huge Art Week banner.
Art Week posters covered the walls.
Many of the posters included photos of teachers, which Pixel had taken.
"Hey, Gaby, have you ever heard of the artist Leonardo da Creepy?" Ben asked.
"Of course! He's coming to Monster Academy on Friday night for the final event, right?"
Ben lowered his voice.
"It's supposed to be a secret, but he's planning to donate a painting to our school."
"Whoa!" Gaby squealed.
"Da Creepy painted Moaning Lisa.
That's one of the most famous paintings in the world!"
"I know. That's why this is a really big deal."
"Ben! Gaby!" They looked up to see Winnie hurrying toward them.
She was carrying her witch's broom and her art supplies.
Mog was trailing after her, wearing a big frown.
"What's wrong, Mog?" Ben asked. "You look grumpy."
Mog waved a claw at the artwork in the halls.
"I don't know what all the fuss is about," he grumbled.
Ms. Van Ghoul overheard him and came over.
"Why, Mog, the fuss is about art!
And art is for everyone.
Anybody can create something beautiful."
"I can't," Mog said.
"I stink at everything—painting, sculpting, drawing.
I can't even draw a flower.
That's why I don't have anything on display."
"Nonsense, Mog," Ms. Van Ghoul said.
"And there's still time. I'll be hanging up art all week long."
"Maybe you just need to find some inspiration, Mog," Winnie said.
"Yeah, look around at all the cool stuff," Ben said.
"That will give you some ideas."
The Doppel Gang was standing nearby.
The one named Larry snickered.
"We'll help you find some inspiration, Mog."
"Yeah!" Carly said, laughing.
"We know lots about art. We even know how to improve it!"
"Huh?" Mog said. "What are you talking about?"
Moe, the third doppelganger, waved him over.
"Come on. Let's walk around and look at the stuff in the hallways.
We'll show you what we mean."
"Uh . . . Okay."
Mog went off with the doppelgangers.
Winnie headed off to the gym, and Ben wandered through the hallways too, taking notes for his article.
Someone shouted his name.
Ben turned and saw Pixel.
"Ben! Ben!" the younger ghost cried.
He floated toward Ben, holding up his fancy camera.
"Watch out!" Ben called. But it was too late.
Crash! Pixel flew into a piece of pottery, which sailed off its pedestal. "Oops!"
The pot bounced off a blob, who quickly caught it.
"Watch where you're going, ghost!" the blob snarled.
"It took me a long time to make this thing!"
"Sorry!" Pixel said.
"That's a nice pot, by the way."
He snapped some photos of it.
"You have to get photos of the witches' flying painting," Ben said.
"They're making it in the gym.
When the painting is finished, it will hover in the air."
"That sounds amazing!" Pixel said.
"I'm planning to take pictures of everything in the show.
I'm hoping to get some cool angles too."
He floated upside down and snapped a photo of Ben.
As he flipped upright, he banged his head on a display table.
"Ouch! Well, the bell's about to ring. I'll see you later."
"Bye, Pixel." As Ben started toward his locker, loud laughter rang out.
At the other end of the hallway, he saw a big group of monsters looking at something on the wall.
"It must be a cool piece of art." Ben hurried over and gasped.
The monsters were looking at an Art Week poster.
The poster featured a photo of Mr. Freaky.
But someone had drawn a big black mustache under the principal's three noses!
Brring! The first bell rang, but nobody moved.
Everyone around Ben was laughing hysterically at the poster.
Ben couldn't help laughing too.
Mr. Freaky looked ridiculous with big bushy whiskers under his noses.
The Doppel Gang stood near the poster with Mog.
Larry held a thick black marker.
Ben had little doubt about who had drawn the mustache.
Pixel snapped a few photos of the poster.
Then he took some shots of the laughing students.
"Fun scenes from Art Week," he said, floating toward Ben.
"We can put these photos on the school website."
"Um . . . I'm not sure Mr. Freaky will like that," Ben said.
"But we'll find out in a second because here he comes!"
"Students!" Mr. Freaky was racing toward the group, his arms flapping like mad.
"Students! What is going on? The bell rang!
Why aren't you in your classrooms?" His noses wiggled wildly.
"What is Mr. Freaky wearing?" somebody said.
Ben had been wondering the same thing.
The school principal wore a suit, as usual, but over it was a strange-looking apron.
And atop his head was a stranger-looking mask.
"Is that a welder's mask?" Ben thought.
The principal screeched to a halt as his eyes landed on the poster.
A few monsters began tiptoeing away.
For a second the hallway was completely silent.
Then Mr. Freaky spoke in a low tone. "Who . . . did . . . this?"
Ms. Van Ghoul pushed through the crowd.
"What's going on, Mr. Freaky?"
The principal pointed. Ms. Van Ghoul stepped closer to the poster.
Mr. Freaky took out a handkerchief and blew his noses.
For a second, Ben thought Ms. Van Ghoul might start laughing.
Instead she tilted her head to view the poster from another angle.
"Why, Mr. Freaky.
You look very handsome with a mustache.
Have you ever considered growing one?"
"Did you just say . . . "
A smile crept across his face. " I look handsome?"
"Yes! That's exactly what I said.
A mustache would show off those three beautiful noses!
And don't worry about this prank.
I think it's a good sign.
It shows that our artistic juices are flowing for Art Week."
"So . . ." Mr. Freaky was still smiling.
"Does that mean . . . Are you saying that everything is under control?"
"Yes." The art teacher nodded. "Everything is just fine."
"Phew!" Mr. Freaky blew out a breath and put away his handkerchief.
"Good! I can return to the industrial arts classroom then." He laughed shyly.
"I'm actually in the middle of creating an art project myself."
"Really?" Ms. Van Ghoul sounded surprised.
"I used to sculpt while I was in college.
I think you'll find my latest work very, very special.
I plan to unveil it on Wednesday."
Abruptly he spun around.
"Okay, that's enough.
Everyone, get to class.
And no more drawing on posters!"
Monsters began heading off to class.
Ben hurried over to Mog.
"Hey, Mog, did the Doppel Gang draw that mustache?"
Mog nodded. "I thought it was funny," he said.
"And artistic. It even gave me an idea for an art project."
"The prank was funny, but I wouldn't call it artistic," Ben said.
"And maybe you'd better keep away from the Doppel Gang for a while.
I have a feeling they're going to be very, er, creative this week."
The next afternoon, after classes were over for the day, Ben met Waldo along with Winnie and some other witches near the gym.
The witches were all carrying supplies for their flying painting—brooms, paintbrushes, and drop cloths.
Waldo had promised to help with the painting.
Ben was planning to take more notes for his newspaper story.
"We sketched the painting last weekend.
Now we're ready to start adding color," Winnie explained.
"If everybody works really hard today, I think we can finish up by tomorrow or Thursday at the latest.
Then it will be ready by Friday night, when Mr. da Creepy comes."
"Cool, but . . ." Ben looked at the witches' supplies.
"Don't you need paints?"
"We need magic paints," Winnie said.
"Remember? It's a magic painting."
"I mixed the paints yesterday and left them in the gym this morning," Waldo said with a grin.
"Everything should be ready to go."
"Thank you so much, Waldo."
Winnie beamed at the wizard and pushed open the gym doors.
"That sounds . . . Oh no!" She let out a gasp.
Ben and the others gasped too.
Inside the gym it looked like a colorful tornado had struck.
Cans of paint were spilled all over the floor.
Blobs of paint were splattered on the walls and floating through the air.
A tiny witch named Greta burst into tears. "What a mess!"
Poor Greta was still sobbing.
Ben thought Winnie might start to cry too as she gazed around the gym in dismay.
"Who did this?" Winnie murmured.
"Why would somebody spill our paint?"
Greta sniffed. "I bet it was the same monster who drew the mustache on Mr. Freaky's poster.
That was funny, but this is mean!"
"It is mean," Ben thought.
He remembered that Mog had been with the Doppel Gang when they decorated Mr. Freaky's poster with a mustache.
Ben hoped Mog wasn't involved in this prank.
"You know what?" Winnie took a deep breath.
"It doesn't matter who did it.
We have to get the mess cleaned up so we can start painting."
"Right," a witch named Samantha chimed in.
"Let's get to work."
Nodding, Greta wiped her nose.
"I'll see if Mr. Bog can help us."
She hurried off to get the school janitor.
Winnie turned to Waldo.
"Our painting has to be ready for Leonardo da Creepy's visit on Friday night.
Do you think you can make more paints for us tonight?"
"Sure." Waldo was wiping some paint drops from his glasses.
"It should be okay. I mean, as long as my magic spell works again."
"Uh-oh," Ben thought.
Waldo's spells rarely worked the way they were supposed to.
A few minutes later, Mr. Bog arrived with his cart, and everyone began cleaning.
As Ben mopped the floor, he looked around for clues.
On the far side of the gym, he spotted something.
Tiny droplets of paint were tracked across the floor.
Ben put down the mop and followed the trail.
It led out a rear door of the gym and into the boys' locker room.
Near the row of sinks, the paint trail stopped.
"Huh," Ben murmured.
"Maybe the vandal stopped here to clean paint off himself."
Ben floated around the locker room, looking for more clues. Nothing.
Back in the hallway, he floated around, searching for signs of anything unusual.
As he passed the cafeteria, he halted.
There was something unusual—the three doppelgangers were inside with buckets and sponges.
They were wiping down the tables.
"What are you guys doing?" Ben called.
Larry moaned. "We got detention!"
The office ogre stood nearby, her arms folded.
"They drew a mustache on Mr. Freaky's poster," she snapped.
"I don't care what Ms. Van Ghoul says—that is not art.
It is vandalism, pure and simple!"
"How much longer do we have to clean?" Carly complained.
"You'll clean until I tell you it's time to stop.
Poor Mr. Bog had to help with some emergency cleanup in the gym.
I may send you down there to help him after you've finished this!"
Ben noticed that none of the doppelgangers reacted to the office ogre's mention of the gym emergency.
"Hmm," he thought. "Maybe they didn't spill the paint. Now, where's Mog?"
A few minutes later, Ben found his friend in the art room.
Several photos were spread out in front of Mog—they were pictures of Monster Academy teachers.
Ben told Mog about the spilled paint, watching his face carefully.
"Wow." Mog looked upset. "That's terrible. Can I help?"
"I think Winnie and her friends can handle the mess," Ben replied carefully.
"But do you have any idea who might have done it?"
"Nope." Mog shook his head.
"I've been in here since classes ended, working on an art project."
He held up a photo of the gym teacher.
He'd drawn a mustache and beard on the teacher's face.
"I call it Gwarg With Goatee," Mog said proudly.
He showed Ben several other pictures with mustaches and beards drawn on them.
"What do you think?"
Ben shook his head. "Sorry, Mog, but I don't call that art."
"What do you mean?" Mog said.
"Winnie said I needed inspiration.
I got inspired—by the Doppel Gang's art."
"It's not really art," Ben repeated.
"The Doppel Gang was just making trouble when they drew that mustache on Mr. Freaky."
"Ms. Van Ghoul said it was art!" Mog said indignantly.
"I think she just wanted to calm down Mr. Freaky, so he wouldn't ruin Art Week before it began."
"Well, I like these photos," Mog insisted.
"I'm going to give them to Ms. Van Ghoul to display for Art Week.
If she doesn't like them, she doesn't have to use them."
Ben sighed and then floated out of the classroom and back to the gym.
He still had no idea who'd tampered with the magic paints.
But he was a reporter.
So he knew how to keep his eyes and ears open for clues.
On Wednesday afternoon Monster Academy students and teachers gathered in the lobby near the school's main entrance.
A white sheet covered a huge object that sat in the middle of the floor.
"We'll finally get to see Mr. Freaky's sculpture," Winnie said to Ben.
"Yep." Ben held up his notebook.
"I'll be writing about it for my newspaper article."
He looked around for Pixel, who was weaving in and out of the crowd with his camera.
"And Pixel will take some great photos of it."
"Lots of them!" the ghost chimed in.
Ms. Van Ghoul stood close to the sculpture with Mr. Freaky.
She clapped her hands to get everyone's attention. "Listen up, students!"
"And please remain calm, everyone!" Mr. Freaky called out.
"I know it's hard on such an exciting day!"
Zzz. Zzz. At the back of the crowd, some zombies were snoring.
"Well, I won't keep you waiting for one more minute."
Mr. Freaky reached for the sheet covering his sculpture.
With a quick yank, he pulled it away.
Ben's eyes went wide, and his jaw dropped.
"What a piece of junk!" Mog burst out.
Ben blinked.
Mog was right—the whole thing was made from junk and metal scraps.
Car bumpers and hoods, along with fan blades, antennas, tools, and other metal objects had been welded together to form one gigantic junk sculpture.
The artwork rested on six mismatched wheels.
A blob moved closer for a better look. "Um, Mr. Freaky . . . What is that thing?"
Mr. Freaky puffed out his chest as Pixel started taking photos.
"I call it Moving Inspiration!"
"Moving?" somebody said.
"It's just sitting there. It looks like a junkyard to me."
"Oh!" Mr. Freaky slapped his forehead.
"I forgot to plug it in!"
He plugged a long cord into the wall.
With a cough and a sputter, the massive sculpture began to whirl in place.
Ben snickered. "Now it looks like a junkyard on wheels," he whispered to Winnie.
Ms. Van Ghoul was beaming.
"Remember, students—art is in the eye of the beholder.
That's the magic of art and Art Week.
We learn to appreciate new forms of beauty!"
"I wouldn't exactly call that thing beautiful."
Ben scratched his head.
"How on earth will I describe it in my story?"
"That's going to be a challenge," Winnie said.
"I'm sure Mr. Freaky is expecting very positive reviews of Moving Junkyard.
I mean, Moving Inspiration." They both laughed.
Then Winnie glanced at a clock on the wall.
"I've got to get back to the gym. We started painting today."
"How's it going?" Ben asked.
"Are you guys making progress?"
"Slow progress," Winnie said.
"We still have a lot to do before Friday, but I think it'll be okay."
"It'll be more than okay," Ben said.
"Your flying painting will be the big hit of Art Week—bigger even than da Creepy's new painting."
"I don't know about that," Winnie said.
"But thanks for the vote of confidence."
With that, she hurried off, and Ben went over to interview a skeleton.
"Do you have a minute?
I'd like to get your opinion about Mr. Freaky's sculpture."
The skeleton spoke in a low voice. "Is this on the record?"
"Actually, it is," Ben replied.
"It's for my article for the school paper."
"Sorry! I'm super busy right now!"
The skeleton clattered off down the hallway.
With a sigh, Ben spun around and scanned the monsters who were still hanging around the lobby.
Who would say something positive about—
"Mog!" Ben hurried over to his friend.
"What do you think of Moving Inspiration?"
Mog glanced at the sculpture and rubbed his chin.
"It's okay, I guess. I mean, at first I didn't get it.
I didn't know you could make art out of junk."
Ben jotted down some notes.
"So it sounds like you find Moving Inspiration . . . inspiring?"
Mog nodded. "Yeah, I think I do."
"Psst! Mog!" a voice said.
Ben and Mog looked over.
The Doppel Gang stood nearby, waving for Mog to join them.
"Want to walk around school and check out some more art?" Carly said.
"Sure," Mog said.
Ms. Van Ghoul smiled.
"Why don't you monsters go to the art room?" she said.
"The mummies are building pyramids out of straws.
I'm sure they could use some help."
"That sounds fun," Larry said, winking at Mog. "Come on!"
"Be careful, Mog," Ben said under his breath as he watched them go.
Ben looked down at his notes.
"I have enough quotes about Mr. Freaky's sculpture," he thought.
"I should probably interview the witches next."
His article was due on Friday morning.
Screech! A loud noise filled the hallway.
"Watch out!"
Ben looked up.
He was pretty sure that was Pixel's voice.
Crash! Boom! The zombies were now wide awake.
"Wh-what is that thing?" a fish monster yelled.
"It's Mr. Freaky's sculpture!" a blob said. "And it's alive!"
Ben spun around.
Sure enough, the massive sculpture had stopped spinning in place.
Now it was rolling forward—right toward the crowd!
"Run for your lives!" a werewolf howled.
Students dived out of the way as the metal monster sputtered and screeched.
Its parts spun and twisted.
