Ben shot backward as the sculpture rolled toward him.
It rumbled closer and closer and then moved right through him!
Crash! The sculpture smashed into the bank of lockers behind Ben.
Everybody ducked as metal parts flew through the air.
"Phew!" Ben gasped. "That was a close call!"
Mr. Freaky ran down the hall and dropped to his knees.
"My precious sculpture—it's ruined!"
Ms. Van Ghoul hurried forward.
"I'm sure you can piece it back together, Mr. Freaky."
"But . . ." Mr. Freaky shook his head.
"Isn't Leonardo da Creepy coming tomorrow?"
"Yes," Ms. Van Ghoul said.
"He wants to make sure that our art is up to his artistic standards.
It's just a quick inspection.
He'll be back on Friday night for the big event."
Mr. Freaky gave a heavy sigh.
"I wanted him to see Moving Inspiration while he was here.
But I guess it can wait."
He picked up a twisted metal pipe and stared at it gloomily.
"My sculpture was working fine this morning," he muttered.
"I think somebody sabotaged it!"
Mr. Freaky started gathering up the broken pieces of Moving Inspiration.
Meanwhile Ms. Van Ghoul waved some students over to a quiet spot.
Until now, the art teacher hadn't seemed bothered by the vandalism.
This time, however, Ben thought she looked worried.
"Leonardo da Creepy is a famous artist," Ms. Van Ghoul began, "and he's very, very picky.
We cannot let any other problems happen this week.
Otherwise, Mr. da Creepy might not participate."
A goblin gasped. "But he's supposed to give us a new painting!"
"Yeah. It could be another Moaning Lisa," a blob added.
"A painting like that could make Monster Academy famous!"
"I know." Ms. Van Ghoul nodded in agreement.
"I've spent a lot of time convincing him to come here to celebrate Art Week with us.
It would be awful if he canceled.
So if you know anything about who is causing all the trouble, please tell me immediately."
Ben looked down, wondering if he should say something about the trail of paint drops in the gym.
It was a clue—maybe even a big clue.
But a part of him was still worried that Mog was involved.
Ben didn't want his friend to get in trouble.
"I won't say anything yet," Ben thought.
If he kept interviewing monsters and teachers for his story, he might learn more about what was going on.
Suddenly he had an idea.
Pixel had been taking a ton of photos all week long.
Maybe his camera held some clues.
Ben darted off, looking for Pixel.
As he flew past the art room, he saw Mog and the Doppel Gang in there, helping the mummies make the pyramids.
Ben felt a wave of relief. "That's good," he thought.
"It looks like Mog has been too busy to mess with Mr. Freaky's sculpture."
"Has anyone seen Pixel?" Ben called into the classroom.
They all shook their heads. "No."
"Thanks."
Ben's next stop was the newspaper office.
"There you are!" Ben said.
Pixel sat at a desk, staring at his camera with a worried expression.
"Are you okay?"
"No." Pixel shook his head.
"Something happened to my camera.
It went dead as soon as Mr. Freaky's sculpture stopped moving."
He bit his lip.
"It seems to be working again now.
But most of the photos I took are gone."
"What?" Ben's heart sank.
He needed those photos for his article—not to mention his investigation.
"Don't worry," Pixel said quickly.
"As long as my camera is working, I can take some more photos today and tomorrow.
I'll have plenty for the story and the school website."
"Okay." Ben nodded, hoping Pixel was right.
"Sounds good. Thanks.
In the meantime Mr. Freaky wants me to find out what happened with his sculpture.
Did you happen to notice anything suspicious while you were taking photos?"
"Nope," Pixel said. "Sorry, but I didn't see a thing."
On Thursday morning Ben and Gaby walked to school.
"That's weird," Gaby burst out as they got close to the school building.
"What's weird?" Ben asked.
She pointed. Kids and teachers stood outside the main doors.
"It's almost time for the first bell.
How come Mr. Freaky hasn't unlocked the doors yet?"
Before Ben could reply, the school doors flew open.
Mr. Freaky came racing out, followed by Ms. Van Ghoul.
The principal was wringing his hands.
"Students, this is a disaster!" he cried.
"Art Week is completely out of control!"
Teachers and kids stepped cautiously into the building.
"Oh no," Ben murmured.
The vandal had struck again.
Sculptures had been knocked over.
Pottery, baskets, and spider web weavings lay everywhere.
Paintings and drawings hung crookedly from the walls, and the big Art Week banner dangled from one side.
"This is awful!" Mr. Freaky wrung his hands again.
"What are we going to do, Ms. Van Ghoul?
Leonardo da Creepy will be here at ten o'clock!"
"Who could have done this?" Gaby said.
Several heads spun toward the Doppel Gang.
"No way! It wasn't us!" Moe said.
Larry and Carly shook their heads furiously.
Ms. Van Ghoul's eyes looked glazed.
"It's not so bad," she said in a tight voice.
Then she fluttered around, picking up a pot and putting it back on its stand.
"We just need to do a little cleanup."
"A little cleanup?" Ben thought.
"This place is a disaster zone!"
Mr. Freaky took out his handkerchief and mopped his head.
"Hey!" A fish monster pointed to a painting.
"My piranha family portrait was hanging there yesterday.
Someone else made this painting to look like it!"
A blob gasped. "I see a bad copy of my painting too!"
"That's not my artwork either," a goblin said.
"Whoever painted that thing must have been half asleep!"
"Everyone, calm down." Ms. Van Ghoul sighed.
"Mr. Freaky will investigate while the rest of us clean up."
"Me? Investigate?" Mr. Freaky spun around.
"Where's Ben?" he demanded.
"He's writing a story about Art Week for the paper.
And that's what reporters do—they investigate!"
"I'm working on it, Mr. Freaky," Ben mumbled.
"Okay, monsters, all claws on deck!" Ms. Van Ghoul said.
The monsters worked all morning to clean up the wrecked exhibits.
Just as Ben and another ghost finished rehanging the Art Week banner, Leonardo da Creepy arrived.
"He's here!" Mr. Freaky cried. "Get ready!"
A tall ghoul with a long beard and a red beret strode into the building.
Ms. Van Ghoul hurried over to greet him.
"Mr. da Creepy! We're so glad you're able to participate in Art Week!"
Mr. da Creepy frowned. "I'm not participating yet.
I've come to inspect the artwork.
Things must be up to my standards, you know."
"Oh yes. I'm aware of that," Ms. Van Ghoul said.
"If you'll follow me, I'll show you the fabulous artwork on display.
The students have been working very hard to make Art Week great!"
Leonardo da Creepy grunted.
Ben followed the adults through the school, taking notes for his article.
As they strolled along, Ben noticed that Leonardo da Creepy did not look impressed with the students' work.
The artist's lip seemed to curl with distaste.
"I must say, Ms. Van Ghoul," Mr. da Creepy said, "many of these artists do not take art very seriously."
The smile slipped from Ms. Van Ghoul's face.
"Oh, we're very serious about art here at Monster Academy!
If you need more proof of that, I can show you an amazing work in progress.
It's a flying painting—have you ever seen one?"
Leonardo da Creepy raised his eyebrows.
"Did you say, a flying painting?"
"Yes, we have a flying painting.
The witches are still working on it," Ms. Van Ghoul said proudly.
"And when it's finished, it's going to be breathtaking."
"Oh." Mr. da Creepy's tone had changed. "May I see it?"
"Certainly."
Ben heard Leonardo da Creepy gasp as they all entered the gym.
"Now, this is what I call art!" he gushed.
"Why, I'd be delighted to participate in the festivities tomorrow night."
"Phew!" Mr. Freaky let out his breath.
"Does that mean you'll still donate your painting?"
"Of course," Mr. da Creepy replied.
"In fact, I just finished painting it this morning.
I think the Monster Academy community will love it."
Ms. Van Ghoul's face lit up. "Wonderful!" she said.
"The ceremony will start tomorrow evening at seven."
"Wait till I tell Winnie," Ben thought happily.
The witches' flying painting wasn't finished yet, but it had already saved the day.
Leonardo da Creepy was coming back to Monster Academy—with a magnificent painting of his own!
The rest of Thursday—and Friday—were busy.
Ben helped the witches work on their flying painting, and then he spent some time working on his article about Art Week.
"Almost done," he thought happily as he floated to the newspaper office on Friday afternoon.
All he needed now was the ending.
In a few hours, the school would host a ceremony with Leonardo da Creepy.
Once Ben reported on that, he'd have everything he needed to finish his article.
The only thing left to do until then was gather up Pixel's photos for the newspaper story.
As Ben hurried through the hallways, he couldn't help thinking that the school looked awesome.
Artwork hung from all the walls, and colorful displays filled the building.
The mummies' straw pyramids had been moved to the cafeteria, and once again, Mr. Freaky's junk sculpture sat in the lobby.
To his own surprise, Ben felt proud.
"It was a tough week," he thought.
But Art Week was nearly over, and maybe, just maybe, it would be a success.
"Hey, Ben!"
Inside the newspaper office, Mog and Pixel were looking at something.
"There you are!" Mog said.
"I've been looking for you.
I finally have something good enough to display for Art Week."
Ben looked around. "Where is it?"
"It's not here, silly," Mog said. "Pixel has a photo."
Pixel held out his camera so Ben could see.
"Huh. It's a sculpture."
Ben peered into the camera again.
"It sort of looks like a dog."
"That's right!" Mog beamed.
"It is a dog!
I figured if Mr. Freaky could make a sculpture out of junk, I could too."
Ben gave him a high-five.
"I like it, Mog. Did you make it with playing cards?"
"Right again," Mog said.
"I call the sculpture Cards Playing Dog."
"Very funny." Ben smiled.
"I'm glad you gave up on those dumb photos with the mustaches.
This is real art."
"Thanks," Mog said.
"Now I have to find Ms. Van Ghoul.
She's looking for the perfect spot for it. See you later!"
Ben and Pixel waved good-bye.
Then Ben looked at Pixel.
"Speaking of photos, how are the Art Week photos going?
Are they all ready?"
Pixel nodded. "Yep. All I have to do now is take a photo of the witches' flying painting.
It's finally finished."
"Woo-hoo!" Ben cheered. "What a relief."
"I'll go now and be back in a few minutes."
Pixel floated out through the door, and Ben sat down to reread his story.
A moment later the door flew open, and Mr. Freaky burst in.
His eyes swept the room.
"Are you looking for me, Mr. Freaky?" Ben asked.
"Er, not exactly. I mean, I did want to get an update on your investigation.
But right now I'm working on something else.
Apparently"—Mr. Freaky rolled his eyes—"Leonardo da Creepy doesn't exactly like kids or schools.
So he needs a"—the principal made air quotes with his fingers—"'quiet place' to relax during tonight's ceremony.
I suggested the cafeteria, but he said he couldn't relax there because it's too noisy.
Plus, it smells like barbecued bat wings.
So I thought maybe he could come here."
"The newspaper office is pretty quiet," Ben said.
"Except when we have tight deadlines. I'm sure it'll be fine."
"It'll do," Mr. Freaky said. "But it's messy.
And Mr. Bog is really busy right now, helping Ms. Van Ghoul with some of the artwork."
He took out a handkerchief and started dusting the desks and shelves around Ben.
Then he headed for the supply closet.
"Is there a broom in here?"
There was a sound as he opened the door, and then Ben saw something tumble out and hit Mr. Freaky.
"Oof!"
"Are you okay?" Ben asked.
Mr. Freaky didn't reply.
Instead he just stared at the object at his feet—it was a large portrait of a piranha family in a broken frame.
Ben gulped as Mr. Freaky slowly spun toward him.
"It's one of the missing paintings!" Mr. Freaky burst out.
"Ben, did you steal this?"
"Of course not!" Ben replied.
"I had no idea it was in there."
"Ben?"
Just then loud, panicked voices came from the hallway.
Ben recognized one of them—it belonged to Winnie.
"Our flying painting!" she screamed.
"Somebody wrecked our flying painting!"
"Oh no, not again!" Mr. Freaky moaned.
He blew his noses with the dusty handkerchief.
Ben took off for the gym, with Mr. Freaky flapping his arms after him.
The witches' flying painting hovered in the air along one wall of the gym.
It showed a famous race, with witches zooming through a moonlit sky on sleek brooms.
Some areas of the painting still looked beautiful, but Ben saw several long, messy smears across one section.
In another spot, colors ran together, and little blobs of paint floated in the air all around the flying painting.
A few witches stood looking at it in horror.
Greta was chewing nervously on her hat.
"After all that work!" she sobbed.
"Our painting is ruined!"
Ben stood helplessly beside Winnie.
"It's not that bad," he mumbled.
"I mean, I know it's not perfect anymore, but—" Winnie shot him a look, and he stopped talking.
Waldo burst into the room, his glasses flying off his face.
"This is terrible!" He stooped to pick up his glasses.
"Who ruined the painting?"
Mr. Freaky spun toward Ben.
"I think I know who the culprit is!"
Several monsters gasped.
Ben held up his hands.
"I'm not the vandal, Mr. Freaky," he said.
"As I was trying to tell you earlier, I had nothing to do with that missing painting.
I had nothing to do with this mischief either."
Mr. Freaky stared at Ben for a second before nodding.
Then he slumped over, looking defeated.
"Leonardo da Creepy will be here at seven," he moaned.
"Art Week is totally out of control!
What are we going to do?"
"I know what we're going to do," Winnie said suddenly.
"We're going to fix it. We have to anyway.
Greta, round up as many sixth-grade witches as you can find," she commanded.
"Samantha, see if you can locate the witches from the broom-flying squad."
"Okay!" The two witches raced off on their brooms.
"We need some new paints," Waldo said.
"I'll start mixing them."
"I can help you," another witch said.
"I'm in Advanced Magic class this year."
The two of them went into a corner of the gym to cast spells.
While the other monsters worked, Ben looked for clues.
Soon he spotted the gym teacher talking to Mr. Freaky.
"Mr. Gwarg, did you see anything suspicious?" Ben asked.
Mr. Gwarg shrugged.
"I did hear a commotion a little while ago.
But when I got inside the gym, the painting had already been damaged.
The gym was deserted."
Ben sighed. "It looks like the vandal got away again."
"That means he or she could try to ruin some of our artwork again," Mr. Freaky said.
"I'd better go check on my sculpture."
"And I'll patrol the halls," Mr. Gwarg said.
"Ben, let me know if you discover any clues in here."
Ben nodded and went to the painting to see if he could do anything to help.
Several witches were arguing about the best way to fix the painting.
"We should start at the bottom and work our way to the top."
"No! We should start at the top and work our way down."
"I want to add a better finish line," Greta said.
"No way!" Winnie called out.
"We're not making any changes, you guys.
As soon as the paint is ready, we'll just patch up what we can."
"I think I'll focus on the investigation for now," Ben thought.
He drifted away from the witches again.
"Let's see," he murmured.
"The vandal probably slipped out the gym's rear door."
As Ben floated toward the back of the room, an object under the bleachers caught his eye.
Ben stooped down.
"It's Pixel's camera."
Ben looked around the gym, but he didn't see the younger ghost anywhere.
"That's odd," Ben thought.
Pixel had come to the gym to take photos of the flying painting.
So why wasn't he here?
And why did he abandon his camera?
Ben turned on the camera and started looking at the photos.
The most recent ones showed the witches' painting—looking absolutely perfect.
"So Pixel was here before the vandal struck," Ben thought.
"I wonder if the vandal was chasing him and that's how Pixel dropped his camera."
Ben suddenly felt very worried.
He didn't know Pixel well, but he did know that the ghost loved his camera.
There was no way Pixel would abandon his camera unless something terrible had happened.
Ben froze, the camera still in his hands.
Where would Pixel go if he needed to hide or get away from someone?
"The old photography classroom!" Ben thought.
It was a tiny room upstairs, which nobody ever used anymore.
Ben needed to get there right away!
Ben flew up to the photography classroom and tried to turn the doorknob.
But the door was locked.
He knocked. "Pixel? Are you in there? It's me, Ben."
There was no reply, so Ben floated through the door.
In the back of the classroom, he could see the small darkroom, once used for developing photographs.
Sure enough, Pixel was huddled in a corner.
He was hunched over something, sobbing.
"Pixel! Are you okay?"
Pixel jumped.
Floating toward the younger ghost, Ben saw tears streaming down his face.
"What happened?" Ben asked.
"Did you see the vandal? Are you hurt?"
Pixel stared at Ben, unable to speak for a moment.
"I'm okay," he finally said in a shaky voice. "I'm not hurt."
"Then what's wrong?" Ben asked again.
"Look. I found your camera.
Do you know who the vandal is?"
"Yes, it's . . ." Pixel swallowed hard. "Me!"
"What?" Ben blinked in surprise.
"You? You're the vandal? But . . ."
He looked around and spotted the other two missing paintings.
Their frames were broken too.
"Oh wow." Ben ran a hand through his hair.
"This is bad." He dropped into a chair.
"I messed the paintings up," Pixel said.
"I didn't steal them.
And now I'm trying to fix them.
Please believe me, Ben.
I didn't mean for any of this to happen!"
Ben shook his head. "Sorry, Pixel, but I don't understand."
Pixel took a deep breath, and then the whole story tumbled out.
"I wanted to get great photos for your article.
So I tried to float in cool ways to get interesting angles.
But I am not good at advanced floating techniques.
I kept smashing into things—like Mr. Freaky's sculpture.
I bashed into the motor and made the whole thing go haywire!"
"Okay," Ben said slowly. "What else did you do?"
"I knocked over all the artwork too!
But I didn't want anyone to know, so I grabbed the three broken paintings and brought them to the newspaper office.
I tried to fix them, but I couldn't.
That's when I made those dumb copies.
I was hoping nobody would notice." Pixel made a face.
"Pretty dumb, huh?"
"Nope." Ben frowned. "Very dumb!"
Pixel winced.
"That explains the painting in the newspaper office closet.
By the way, Mr. Freaky found it and blamed me!"
"Sorry." The younger ghost winced again.
"I was working on it in there, and somebody came in, so I shoved it into the closet.
Every time I tried to go back for it, somebody was in the office."
"What about the flying painting?" Ben asked.
"That got vandalized twice."
"I knocked over the paints earlier in the week.
And then today I smeared the paint while I was trying to take photos.
I didn't realize the flying painting was still wet!"
"Go on."
"While I was trying to sneak out of the gym without being noticed, I dropped my camera.
I couldn't go back for it because Mr. Gwarg was in there." Pixel shrugged.
"I'm just so awful at floating!
I know I should practice more often, but I like photography better.
I'd much rather take pictures than practice boring floating techniques."
"Wow. Pixel." Ben sat there for a minute with his chin in his hands.
He couldn't believe how much damage Pixel had caused—all by mistake.
"Why didn't he ask me or a teacher for help?" Ben thought.
But of course Ben knew the answer to that question perfectly well.
"I used to have trouble with floating too," Ben blurted out.
"For the longest time, I couldn't float through doors and walls.
I was too embarrassed to tell anyone."
Pixel blinked at him. "Really? Same as me?"
"Yep. But I practiced and I got better. You can do that too."
"I'll try, I promise. But . . ." Tears filled Pixel's eyes again.
"In the meantime I ruined Art Week!" He shook his head.
"Worst of all, I wrecked the witches' beautiful painting."
"Art Week isn't over yet," Ben said.
"And the witches are very good artists.
They're fixing the flying painting right now."
He glanced at the artwork on the floor near Pixel.
"It looks like you've finished repairing those paintings, so we can hang them back up in the hallway."
Pixel nodded as he wiped away his tears.
Then he glanced up at a clock on the darkroom wall.
"I guess we'd better hurry, Ben.
Leonardo da Creepy will be here any minute!"
"Yeah," Ben said with a grin.
"And we need to get your photos ready for my newspaper article!"
Ben tucked the two paintings under his arm.
"Follow me!" he said, grabbing Pixel's arm.
Together the ghosts floated smoothly through a wall of the darkroom and out into the classroom.
Then they glided through another door into the hallway.
"Whoa! This is what I call floating," Pixel exclaimed.
"We haven't bumped into anything or knocked stuff over!"
"You'll get better soon," Ben promised him. "I'll help you."
The two ghosts zipped downstairs and quickly hung up the two missing paintings.
Then they got the third one from the newspaper office and hung it up too.
After they'd picked out some good photos for the newspaper article, they flew to the gym.
The witches were still flying around, frantically putting the finishing touches on the flying painting.
When Ben went up close, he could see the fresh paint in several places.
But the paint would dry, and from a distance, nobody would notice a thing.
"It looks great, Winnie," Ben said.
"Thanks!" Her green eyes glowed with relief. "I think so too."
Only Mr. Freaky still looked worried as he wrung his hands and blew his noses.
"Hurry up, witches! Leonardo da Creepy will be here in fifteen minutes!"
At seven o'clock Ben went into the main lobby, where Mr. Freaky and Ms. Van Ghoul were waiting nervously.
A few minutes later, a sleek black car pulled up in front of the school.
The famous artist emerged, carrying a large painting wrapped in brown paper.
Ms. Van Ghoul and Mr. Freaky hurried to greet him.
"Welcome back, and please come with us," Ms. Van Ghoul said.
"We're holding the ceremony in the gym.
Everyone is very excited to see your new painting."
"It's one of my best," Mr. da Creepy boasted.
"It might be even better than Moaning Lisa."
"Wow," Ben thought. "It must be a spectacular painting."
"And don't worry about all the commotion," Mr. Freaky went on.
"If you need quiet time, you can use the newspaper office.
It's very quiet in there."
They entered the gym, which was crowded now with students and a news crew.
A camerawoman was shooting the flying painting as a reporter stood in front of it with a microphone.
Ben pointed them out to Winnie.
"Look! Your flying painting is going to be on TV!"
"Thanks, but I bet they're just killing time until Mr. da Creepy unveils his new painting."
Ben shook his head.
"Nope. Everybody loves that painting.
It's the best work of art in the whole school."
Winnie grinned slyly. "Better than Moving Inspiration?"
"Hmm." Ben pretended to think for a minute.
"Yep! Much, much, much better!"
At last the lights dimmed, and the Boneyard Brass Band played a couple of songs.
Then Mr. Freaky and Ms. Van Ghoul each gave a long speech about Art Week and how great everything had turned out.
At last it was Leonardo da Creepy's turn.
Everyone clapped as the artist stepped up to the microphone.
His painting stood on a big easel next to the podium, still wrapped in brown paper.
Winnie gripped Ben's hand. "This is so exciting!"
Ben nodded, jotting down a few notes for his newspaper story. "It sure is."
Leonardo da Creepy cleared his throat.
"Good evening, students and members of the Monster Academy community.
I'm very proud to be here to present a gift to this wonderful, artistic school—it's my latest masterpiece."
Several monsters cheered.
"Let's see it!" cried a skeleton.
"It sounds like you're all very eager to get to it," Mr. da Creepy said with a smile.
"So, with no further ado . . . "
He leaned closer to the painting.
"I'll present my latest work of art."
Ms. Van Ghoul hurried forward, and together they removed the brown paper wrapping.
A gasp rippled through the audience as the covering fell away.
Ben looked at Winnie, and Winnie looked back at Ben.
They both burst out laughing at the same time.
"It's a portrait of Mr. Freaky!" Ben said.
"I'm sorry, but—" Winnie covered her mouth as she laughed even harder.
"That's the ugliest thing I've ever seen!"
"I know!" Ben said. "His noses look huge!"
But onstage Leonardo da Creepy was beaming.
And so was Mr. Freaky.
In fact, Ben had never seen the principal look prouder.
"Mr. Freaky loves it!" Mog said.
"And you know what?" Mog cocked his head and stared at the painting.
"I like it too. I think it captures his personality."
"I guess Ms. Van Ghoul was right," Ben whispered to Winnie.
"Beauty is in the eye of the beholder!"
Ben floated through the halls of Monster Academy on Thursday afternoon.
Near the auditorium cheerleaders were selling orange T-shirts and black T-shirts.
"Get your Team Orange shirts!" one shouted.
"Team Black shirts here!" another called.
Ben grinned. Tomorrow was Field Day, and everyone seemed super excited.
He'd heard from Winnie and Mog that the day was tons of fun.
Two teams competed against each other in games like tug-of-war and sack races while the rest of the school cheered them on.
Only 12 monsters competed, and Ben was hoping he'd get to be one of them.
"I really want to be on Team Orange," a worm monster said.
"Sorry, Francis, but you don't stand a chance," a werewolf replied. "You have to be fast."
"Oh." Francis hung his head. "Is there a digging event?"
A loudspeaker crackled loudly.
"All students to the auditorium for the pep rally!" Mr. Freaky, the school principal, announced.
Pixel floated up to Ben. "Hey, Ben. Can I sit with you for the pep rally?"
"Sure," Ben replied. "Have you seen Winnie?"
Pixel shook his head. "Nope."
"Huh." Ben had been hoping to sit with Winnie at the pep rally, but he didn't see her anywhere.
The students settled into their seats.
Some were already wearing orange or black T-shirts, even though the Field Day teams hadn't been chosen yet.
For a few minutes, Miss Bungle and the cheerleaders led some cheers.
Then Mr. Freaky hurried onto the stage, his noses wiggling.
"Good afternoon, students.
I know you're excited to hear about the teams for Field Day.
So Mr. Gwarg will choose the captains and explain a few rules."
The gym teacher stepped up to the microphone.
"Okay, monsters," Mr. Gwarg began.
"There will be two teams this year, orange and black."
"We had orange and black last year!" a fish monster yelled.
An orange monster with black spots stood up.
"What's wrong with orange and black?"
Everyone laughed. The fish monster grinned sheepishly.
Mr. Gwarg ignored the laughter.
"I've chosen two captains based on their performance in gym class.
The captain of Team Orange is . . . Zork."
"Yes!" A lizard monster leaped to his feet and pumped a fist.
Other monsters started hooting and cheering.
"Good choice!" Pixel said to Ben.
"Zork is a fantastic athlete. He'll be a great captain."
"I guess," Ben muttered.
"I mean, if you don't mind your captain showing off all the time."
Lots of monsters liked Zork, but Ben wasn't one of them.
He'd been a little jealous of Zork ever since the Monster Mash dance, when Zork had danced with Winnie all night long.
Mr. Gwarg cleared his throat.
"The captain of Team Black is . . . Mog."
"Woo-hoo!" Mog got up and did a little celebration dance.
Ben cheered for his friend.
"This is so great!" he thought.
Mog would definitely pick Ben for his team.
Mog would definitely ask Winnie too.
"As you know, each team captain may now pick five students for his team," Mr. Gwarg said.
"Remember, there's no magic during Field Day activities.
And don't forget to bring your best school spirit!"
A few minutes later, the pep rally ended, and everyone began filing out of the auditorium.
Mog rushed over to Ben and Pixel.
"Hey, you guys. Want to be on Team Black?"
"You bet!" Pixel said.
"Sounds awesome!" Ben said, giving Mog a high five.
"Who else is on the team?"
"Deb and Waldo," he replied.
"Waldo?" Ben blurted out. Then he felt bad.
Waldo was a good friend, but he wasn't very athletic.
Mog shrugged. "I know he's not very fast, but he's good at catching.
We might need that in the slime ball toss.
I have to find one more monster for the team though."
"What about Winnie?" Ben said quickly.
"I already asked her, but she said no," Mog said.
"Really?" Ben was shocked.
Mog shrugged.
"I don't get it either. She was acting kind of weird."
"Where is she?" Ben asked, looking around.
"Maybe I can convince her to change her mind."
"She's out there." Mog waved toward the hallway.
"Give it a try, Ben. It would be great to have her on our team.
I'm going to hold the first Team Black practice in the gym in a little while."
"Okay. I'll let you know what she says."
Ben zipped outside, scanning the crowded hallway for Winnie.
He knew he could get her to join the team.
Finally he spotted her at the opposite end of the hallway.
But as Ben got closer, his heart sank.
Winnie was talking and laughing . . . with the captain of Team Orange—Zork!
"Ugh." Ben groaned as he watched Winnie grinning up at Zork.
She was giggling as if Zork had said the funniest thing in the world.
"What if he's asking her to join Team Orange?" Ben thought.
That would be terrible!
He picked up speed, zooming toward Winnie and Zork.
"Ouch!" a goblin shrieked as Ben floated through him.
"Hey, Ben, want to buy a T-shirt for Team Orange?" a cheerleader asked.
"No thanks," Ben said. "I'm on Team Black."
"What about a Team Black T-shirt then?" another cheerleader asked.
"Maybe later," Ben said. "Hey, Winnie!" he called.
"Winnie!" By now, Winnie and Zork had started walking away together down the hallway.
Frustrated, Ben shot up to the ceiling above the crowd. "Winnie!" he yelled once more.
This time she heard him and stopped.
He flew over to drop down directly in front of her.
"Oh, hi, Ben," she said.
"Hey, Ben," Zork added.
Ben gave him a curt nod before turning back to Winnie.
"Do you have a minute?" he asked.
"I wanted to talk to you about something. It's kind of important."
"Sorry." Winnie shook her head.
"I can't talk right now.
I need to find my cousin Serena. She's visiting my family for a few days."
"I didn't know your cousin was coming."
Winnie let out a sigh.
"I wish I could forget it myself," she said.
"She was supposed to meet me outside the auditorium before the pep rally, but she never showed up.
I have no idea where she is."
Zork puffed out his chest.
"I've been helping Winnie look for her.
I'll go and check the gym now.
If I spot her, I'll send you a message."
"Thanks so much, Zork." Winnie flashed a smile at him.
"That's so nice of you."
"He's just walking around school," Ben muttered as Zork hurried off.
"It's not a big deal. I can help you look too."
"Okay, great." Winnie pulled out her phone and began scrolling through her messages.
"Why hasn't Serena texted me?"
Ben was still worried that Zork was going to ask Winnie to be on Team Orange.
"Hey, do you want to be on Team Black with Mog and me?" he blurted out.
"Deb's on the team, and so is Waldo."
Winnie looked annoyed.
"I already told Mog no.
I have a lot of homework this week, and Serena is visiting."
"Zork didn't ask you to be on his team, did he?"
"What?" Winnie blinked in surprise.
"Ben, are you accusing me of lying?"
"Of course not!" Ben said quickly. "I'd never—"
"Good," Winnie snapped.
"Because I'm telling the truth.
Like I said, I'm stuck with my cousin for the next three days.
Come on, let's keep looking for her."
As they walked through the halls, Ben didn't bring up Field Day again.
Winnie seemed to be in a really bad mood.
Ben had never seen her so irritable.
"Your cousin must be awful," he said.
Winnie bit her lip.
"She's not really awful . . . It's just that she's always at the center of attention."
"What do you mean?" Ben asked. "Does she—"
"Ar-roo!" A werewolf's loud howl cut him off.
As Ben and Winnie approached the library, Ben saw a group of male monsters standing in a large circle.
While the werewolf kept howling, a two-headed monster stood on both heads, and a squid monster spun around like a break dancer.
"What is going on in there?" Ben asked.
"I know exactly what's going on!" Winnie said. "Serena is in there!"
Winnie stomped into the library, and Ben floated in after her.
Sure enough, standing in the center of the large circle, was a witch—the most beautiful witch that Ben had ever seen.
"Wow!" Ben thought.
Without realizing it, he let out a gasp.
Winnie was pushing her way through the crowd.
"Excuse me!"
"Hey, cousin!" the beautiful witch said.
"Hello, Serena." Winnie gestured at the lovesick monsters.
"Can you please fix this situation?"
"Sure." Serena looked at the monsters and smiled.
"Okay, guys. I found my cousin, so the rest of you can go now.
Thanks for the welcome to Monster Academy."
A skeleton clattered over to Winnie.
"Is Serena really your cousin?" he asked.
"Yep," Winnie replied.
He put a bony hand on his heart.
"Wow, you're the luckiest witch in the world!"
Serena heard him and threw an arm around Winnie's shoulder.
"Lighten up, Winnie," she said.
"We're going to have so much fun while I'm here!"
Ben heard Winnie mutter a few words in reply.
It didn't sound like she was having fun yet.
Ben was still staring at Winnie's cousin.
"Aren't you going to introduce me?" he said, nudging Winnie gently.
She sighed. "Ben, this is my cousin Serena. Serena, this is my friend Ben."
Ben felt a little hurt. Winnie usually introduced him as her boyfriend.
"It's nice to meet you, Ben," Serena said.
She flashed a dazzling smile at him, and he felt himself blushing from head to toe.
"Thanks! It's amazing to meet . . ." Ben let his words trail off as Winnie glared at him.
"It's nice to meet you too," he mumbled.
"Where were you, Serena?" Winnie asked with a frown.
"You were supposed to sign in at the main office and then meet me outside the auditorium for the pep rally.
I waited and waited for you.
You made me late for the pep rally—I missed most of the cheers."
"Sorry about that," Serena said.
"I headed to the pep rally after I went to the main office.
But all these monsters kept stopping to talk to me."
Winnie let out another big sigh.
"Well, we need to go upstairs now.
I have to get my broom from the broom-flying classroom before it gets locked for the day."
She grabbed Serena's arm and dragged her away.
"Hey, Winnie," Ben began.
"Can we talk about Field Day again? I just wanted—"
"I'm busy, Ben!" Winnie said loudly.
"Didn't you hear me say that before?"
"Yes, but . . ." Ben's words trailed off as the two witches disappeared into the hallway.
He ran a hand through his hair.
"Mog is right," he thought.
"Winnie is acting really weird today."
His thoughts flashed back to Winnie's laughing and smiling with Zork.
She'd seemed fine then.
Suddenly Ben felt a large hand clamp down on his shoulder.
It was Mog's.
"Ready for practice, Ben?" Mog asked.
"Team Black had better practice today, or Zork's team will beat us."
"No, they won't!" Ben burst out.
"Team Black is going to win!"
"That's what I call team spirit," Mog said.
They headed toward the gym.
"Did you have any luck with Winnie?" Mog asked.
"No." Ben shook his head.
"She told me what she told you—she's too busy.
Her cousin is visiting for a few days."
"Too bad," Mog said.
"But it's okay. Jen said she'd love to join Team Black if Winnie can't do it."
Ben felt worried. "Jen's a blob, Mog," he said.
"Blobs can't run very fast.
And there's a sack race and a cross-country race during Field Day."
Mog shrugged. "Blobs are faster than zombies," he said.
"And they don't drool. Besides"—he peered closely at Ben—"Jen's really nice.
She'll be a good team member."
"You're right." Ben nodded.
"I guess I'm just getting carried away because of Zork.
I can't stand the thought of losing to that guy!"
Ten minutes later Team Black was warming up inside the gym.
After only six push-ups, Waldo and Jen looked exhausted.
Deb and Pixel looked only slightly better.
Ben tried not to think about it.
"We'll be fine," he told himself. "We can beat Team Orange."
When warm-ups were over, Mog gathered the team together.
"Great warm-up, everybody.
Now let's start practicing for the slime ball toss," he said.
"I don't have any slime balls, but we can practice with dodo eggs.
I got them from the cafeteria."
"Ooh!" Jen squealed. "I love catching slime! I can't wait till tomorrow."
Mog looked at Waldo. "Just remember—Mr. Gwarg said no magic tomorrow."
"Got it," Waldo murmured.
"Good." Mog quickly went over the rules for the practice game.
"If the egg cracks, you're out.
Now everybody spread out a little bit."
Team Black tossed a dodo egg around, being very careful not to drop it or crack it.
Mog called out a few tips, and Ben had to admit that Mog had been right about Waldo.
The wizard was pretty good at tossing and catching the egg.
Before long, some other monsters wandered into the gym to watch Team Black practice.
"This is actually going pretty well!" Ben thought with relief.
Suddenly the gym doors opened again, and Serena sauntered in.
Winnie hurried in right behind her cousin, trying to keep up.
A few monsters gasped when they spotted the beautiful witch.
As Mog turned to see what was causing the commotion, the dodo egg flew from his hand.
It sailed through the air—heading straight for Waldo's face!
"Waldo!" Ben cried. "Look out!"
"Huh?" Waldo saw the egg coming and managed to duck in the nick of time.
Ben didn't move, expecting the egg to pass right through him.
But—splat!
The dodo egg hit Ben in the chest, and gooey green dodo yolk splattered all over him.
"Ugh." Ben looked down at his shirt.
"What a mess. Why didn't the egg go right through me?"
Loud laughter suddenly rang out.
A few of the monsters from Team Orange had come into the gym.
"Nice catch, ghost boy!" Carly called. Carly was a doppelganger.
A witch named Brunhilda was cackling with delight.
"You've got egg on your face, Ben!"
Winnie hurried over to him.
"Are you all right?" She held a hand over her mouth, as if she was trying hard not to laugh too.
"I'm fine." Ben wiped egg off his shirt.
"Sorry about that, Ben," Waldo said.
"I tried to cast a spell to stop the egg, but—"
Mog frowned. "No magic during Field Day events, Waldo.
So you can't use it during practice, either."
Waldo nodded. "Right!"
Zork and his teammates were still laughing.
"No offense, Team Black," Zork said.
"But if that's the best you can do, Team Orange is headed for an easy victory."
"Maybe you guys should just sit in the stands and . . ." Carly made her eyes pop out.
"Watch the events instead of competing in them."
Deb, who was the only doppelganger on Mog's team, shot back.
"Well, watch out, Team Orange.
Because tomorrow we're going to bury you!"
She changed into a big tombstone that read RIP Team Orange.
The two doppelgangers kept dueling while everyone in the gym watched.
Carly turned into a giant worm.
"You're the ones who will be sleeping with the worms when we're through with you!"
"Even a worm could outrun you slugs."
Deb became a giant slug and slithered around the gym, leaving a trail of slime.
Serena turned to Winnie.
"This is getting boring," she murmured.
"Let's go." Heads turned to watch walk toward the exit.
Winnie rushed after her.
Zork stepped into the middle of the gym.
"Huddle up, Team Orange," he called.
"Let's show these Team Black losers how a real team practices."
Carly and Brunhilda joined him, along with Cleo and a werewolf named Lon.
Ben quickly counted the competitors.
"That's only five monsters," he thought.
"I wonder who the sixth member of their team is."
Mog scowled. "That's enough practice for now, Team Black.
Let's get out of here.
We don't want to give these jokers any tips for winning."
They headed for the exit too.
"Don't drop any more eggs on your way out!" Carly called after them.
"Yeah," Lon said. "You guys already stink!"
Zork laughed. "I'm looking forward to seeing you tomorrow—especially at our first event, the tug-of-war.
That's when you'll get a look at our secret weapon!"
Mog gulped and looked at Ben. "Did he just say secret weapon?"
The next morning Ben found his teammates on the field behind the school.
They were all dressed in black.
"Welcome to Field Day!" Mr. Freaky called.
Like the teachers, he was dressed in orange and black so he could root for both teams.
The cheerleaders waved their pom-poms. "Go, Orange! Go, Black!" they cheered.
Mr. Gwarg blew his whistle.
"Okay, monsters, here's how Field Day works.

"Sid's right. It would be interesting to see the pets—and it could be a fun family outing."
Ben's mother shook her head. "I don't know if that's such a good idea."
"I know you don't like dogs, Mom," Ben said.
"But there will be other pets at the show."
She shuddered. "I can't stand most animals.
Uncle Edgar's bird gives me the creeps.
Aunt Petunia's stinkworm makes her house smell terrible, and the neighbors' tarantula is always digging up our backyard!"
Ben's father put down his fork.
"Maybe Ben, Sid, and I will go to the show," he said.
"You can stay home, honey."
"You're forgetting something," she said. "Sid is allergic to some animals."
"It's okay, Mom," Sid said quickly.
"I just break out in green spots.
Green spots are a little itchy, but they look cool!
I'll put up with hundreds of green spots, if it means we can have a pet."
"Good one, Sid!" Ben thought, glancing hopefully at his mother.
But her lips were tightly pursed.
"We're not getting a pet," she said firmly.
"Right now we are only talking about pets—and the pet show."
"Where we can definitely find a pet that you'll like!" Ben said.
"I'll be at the show all weekend long. It's a great opportunity!"
Sid clapped his hands. "Yeah!"
"Boys, that's not what I said."
Ben's mother closed her eyes and took a deep breath.
Then she opened them again.
"Okay, I'll think about it. But I'm making no promises."
"I can help Ben look at pets at the show," Sid said.
"We'll do a simple test. If I don't get green spots, I'm not allergic."
Their mother tapped a finger on the table. "Hmm . . ."
"We can at least let the boys look around at the show," their father said.
"There's no harm in that."
"Please, Mom," Ben pleaded softly.
"All right," she said at last.
"You two can look." She stared hard at Ben.
"But if Sid starts sneezing or itching a lot, you have to bring him home immediately."
"Bring him home?" Ben repeated.
"Yes," his mother said.
"I'll drop Sid off at Monster Academy tomorrow after school.
You can keep an eye on him."
"Oh, boy!" Sid shouted. "This is going to be great!"
"But I have volunteer stuff to do at the show," Ben moaned.
Besides, he wanted to hang out with his friends.
"Sid can help you with the duties," his mother said.
"I'm sure he won't get in the way."
"But—"
Ben's father cut him off with a stern look.
"A ghost who wants a pet needs to show responsibility, Ben.
So you should certainly be able to take care of your little brother for a few hours without difficulty."
Ben was trapped. "Okay," he said with a heavy sigh.
When Ben arrived at Monster Academy the next day, he grinned at the unusual scene.
As always, monsters were streaming into the school building.
But today some of them had brought their pets with them.
Mr. Freaky stood outside, blowing his noses.
"Now, students. Remember what I said:
This afternoon you'll have an opportunity to work with your pets.
Until then, let's keep everything under control!"
Ben looked around. Gaby had her giant albino shrew.
A vampire had brought a spider.
Jen had her singing slug, and Cleo was towing a pet jackal with a leash.
"Lucky Deb," Ben thought as he gazed at the pets.
She had a funny piranha-keet that she had taught to speak.
"Wrawck!" the bird squawked.
"Everything is totally under control!"
After classes ended, some students gathered on the field with their pets.
"You may practice for the pet show now," Mr. Freaky announced.
"What if we didn't bring a pet to school?" somebody asked.
"You can help your friends," Mr. Freaky said.
Winnie looked busy with a group of witches, so Ben searched for Mog.
He found his friend working with his two-headed dog.
"Watch this, Ben," Mog called. "Rex-Rex, sit!
Roll over!
Fetch!"
Ben was impressed. "He's smart."
Mog nodded. "I entered Rex-Rex in all three competitions at the show—tricks, obedience, and best pet."
"I think he'll win a prize," Ben said.
Mog obviously didn't need help with his pet.
But maybe Waldo did. "Have you seen Waldo around?"
"He took his owl to the science lab."
"Thanks. See you later."
As Ben opened the door, he heard a nervous shout. "Close the door!"
"Okay!" Ben quickly pushed the door closed. "What's going on?"
Waldo wiped sweat from his forehead. "I don't want Oswald to escape."
Ben saw a birdcage, but there was no sign of a bird.
"Uh . . . I hate to tell you this. But it looks like Oswald already escaped."
"No, he didn't," Waldo said. "Oswald is an invisible owl."
"Oh," Ben said. "How do you know he's still here?"
Waldo reached into his pocket and pulled out a cracker.
He whistled sharply. "Oswald, come!" Waldo tossed the cracker into the air.
Ben felt a rush of air and then—chomp! The cracker disappeared.
Waldo grinned. "He loves those crackers.
But he's not very good at obeying my commands."
He held up another cracker, whistling twice this time.
Nothing happened for a few seconds.
Then Ben heard a flutter of wings.
"Gotcha!" Waldo cried.
He snatched the invisible bird and whistled again.
With a puff of smoke, Oswald appeared.
"Awesome!" Ben said.
But Waldo was frowning.
"When I whistle, he's supposed to turn visible immediately.
If I can't get him to follow my commands, we're not going to do well at the show."
"Do you want help training him?" Ben asked.
"Sure," Waldo said. "I want Oswald to come whenever I whistle once—no exceptions.
And he should turn visible when I whistle twice."
"Got it," Ben said.
"Oswald is pretty stubborn," Waldo added.
"Plus, he likes to chase small animals and carry them off."
Ben gulped, thinking about all the pets he'd seen yesterday at the pet show.
Most of them, like Winnie's kitten and Mrs. Hubbletree's gecko, were pretty small animals.
"Let's get started," he said.
Ben and Waldo spent the next hour training the owl.
After that, it was time to go to the gym for the pet show.
"I'll meet you in the gym in a few minutes," Ben said to Waldo near the school's main entrance.
"My mom is dropping off Sid soon. Good luck with Oswald."
"Thanks." Waldo looked nervous. "I'll need it."
Ben reached into his backpack for his volunteer badge.
He slipped it over his head and then checked his schedule to see what he had to do first.
A second later his mother and Sid approached.
Sid was wearing a volunteer badge too.
"Mom just signed me up as a junior volunteer!" Sid said.
"The office ogre said I can help you."
"Great," Ben muttered.
His mom gave them each a quick hug.
"Remember, Ben, if Sid gets itchy or starts sneezing, call me."
Ben nodded. He and Sid waved as their mom hurried outside.
Then Ben spun to look at Sid. "Do you already have green spots on your hand?"
Sid looked sheepish. "Yes. I petted a cute dog in the hallway."
"I guess we're not getting a dog," Ben said.
Sid shrugged. "Mom hates dogs anyway."
"Come on," Ben said.
"We have to feed some reptiles first."
He led Sid to an area where some reptile tanks were set up.
There were lizards and snakes of different sizes and colors.
Ben spotted Mrs. Hubbletree's terrarium.
Her rainbow gecko, Bowie, sat on a small branch inside it.
Sid was staring at some snakes. "Ugh! I hate snakes."
He backed away as a snake hissed.
"I'll feed the snakes," Ben said.
"You can feed the lizards.
If you have any problems with spots or sneezing, let me know."
By the time they were finished with the job, green spots dotted Sid's arms and legs.
"Rats!" Sid said.
"Yeah," Ben said. "You're covered with spots."
"No." Sid shook his head.
"I said 'rats' because I wanted to check out the rodents next.
Maybe I'm not allergic to them."
"Okay." Ben nodded and checked the time.
"We might see some rodents at the pet parade.
It starts on the stage in a few minutes."
As Ben headed with Sid toward the stage, he spotted Winnie.
She was sitting in a quiet corner, practicing tricks with Inky.
The kitten hissed at Ben, but she mewed softly at Sid.
"That's weird," Ben murmured.
Sid looked surprised too as he started petting the black cat.
"Be careful, Sid," Ben said.
"She likes me now," Sid said.
"And I'm not allergic to cats, remember?"
Winnie went off to join the parade, while Ben and Sid sat down.
A line of pets began walking across the stage and around the gym.
There were dogs and cats, along with Cleo's jackal, Deb's piranha-keet, and Waldo's owl.
Sid was grinning at a small dragon sitting on a skeleton's shoulder. "What a cool pet!"
The dragon suddenly leaped into the air.
Everyone oohed and aahed as it shot small puffs of flame.
"It's awesome!" Ben agreed as the creature dipped closer, brushing their heads.
"Maybe we can get a pet dragon, Sid."
But a second later, Sid groaned.
He held up his hands, where more green spots had sprouted.
Ben sighed.
He and Sid were never going to find the right animal.
"It's okay," he said, trying to sound hopeful.
"We can keep trying. Maybe—"
"Watch out!" A mummy pointed to Sid and shouted, "That ghost has monster pox!"
"Monster pox!" Other monsters started screaming and pointing. "Monster pox!"
"It's just an allergy!" Ben tried to explain.
But there was so much screaming that nobody heard him.
Suddenly—schwoop! The skeleton's dragon shot up into the air.
"Look out!" Ben shouted.
The dragon was flying to the wall, breathing angry flames.
A few banners caught fire, and pets were barking and screeching.
Mayor Hubbletree looked upset.
"I knew this was a bad idea!" he said.
Miss Bungle rushed to the microphone on the stage.
"Everyone, please remain calm," she said.
"Mr. Freaky, I'd like to see you immediately."
"I'm right here!" Mr. Freaky called, hurrying toward the stage.
Zoom! Ben ducked as something streaked through the air above his head again.
"Hey! That's Winnie!" Sid shouted.
Ben looked up. Sure enough, Winnie was on her broom, flying after the dragon.
"Great idea, Winnie!" Ben thought.
If she could catch the dragon, everything would calm down.
"Ahh!" Winnie dodged a blast of flame.
A second later she landed, holding the dragon by its neck.
"Whew! Got him!"
By now Mr. Freaky had joined Miss Bungle onstage.
He banged his noses as he bent toward the microphone.
"Everything is totally under control, students!
The dragon has been caught."
"Wrawck!" Deb's piranha-keet squawked loudly.
"Everything is totally under control!"
Ben zipped up to the microphone to make another announcement.
"There is no monster pox!
My brother's green spots are just a harmless allergy!
Please do not panic!"
Mr. Freaky took out his handkerchief and blew his noses.
Mr. Gwarg ran around, using a fire extinguisher to put out the banner fires.
"Whew." Ben floated back to Sid, who was standing with Mrs. Hubbletree.
The mayor's wife nervously clutched her rainbow gecko.
"Ben, are you sure we're safe?" she asked.
Ben nodded. "Yes, Mrs. Hubbletree.
Everything is fine. The dragon is back with its owner."
"Oh, thank goodness!" Mrs. Hubbletree said.
"I was worried about Bowie.
He's very valuable, you know.
He can change to any color.
He can even match patterns!"
Her jaw suddenly dropped open. "Oh my goodness!"
She pointed at Sid's hand, which was covered with spots again.
And now the gecko had them too.
Bowie was mimicking Sid's spots!
Ben groaned.
"It looks like my little brother is allergic to geckos—along with every other pet at this show."
Mrs. Hubbletree stared at her pet in dismay.
"I hope these spots aren't permanent," she murmured.
"I'd better show this to the mayor!"
Ben gulped as Mrs. Hubbletree dashed over to her husband.
"Mayor Hubbletree is going to make a huge deal of this commotion," Ben moaned.
He grabbed Sid's arm. "Come on. Let's sit down and watch the rest of the parade.
Mom is going to pick us up when it's over."
"Can we look at more pets tomorrow?" Sid asked.
"We still didn't find out if I'm allergic to rats."
"Sure," Ben answered.
But inside he was still feeling doubtful.
"Sid had better not get his hopes up," Ben thought.
Finding the right pet for their family felt like an impossible task.
The next morning Ben and Sid arrived at the show bright and early.
"First, we have to clean some cages," Ben said.
He led Sid over to some empty chairs.
"You can wait here. I'll do the cleaning myself, just in case you're allergic to anything.
When I'm done, I'll get you, and we can visit the rats."
"Sounds good." Sid nodded.
"Cleaning cages doesn't sound fun anyway."
"It's not," Ben agreed.
About an hour later, the brothers approached the rodent area.
Almost instantly, green spots appeared on Sid.
He tried holding a hairless mole rat, but even that one caused green spots to appear.
Finally, Sid threw up his hands in frustration.
"We've tested dogs, lizards, dragons, and now rats!"
He looked like he was about to cry.
"Maybe we should try snakes after all, even though I hate them."
"Maybe," Ben said. But he wasn't crazy about a pet snake either.
"Look, there's Waldo. He's got Oswald with him." Ben waved his friend over.
"Hey, guys!" Waldo smiled as he hurried over with his owl.
He held up Oswald's cage.
"I think I've got this guy's problems worked out.
He's been following all my commands today."
"But . . ." Sid stared at the cage and blinked.
"That cage is empty, Waldo."
Ben and Waldo chuckled.
"It's not empty," Waldo said, clapping a hand on Sid's shoulder.
"Oswald is an invisible owl," Ben explained.
"He can make himself disappear."
"Wow, he's invisible? Cool!" Sid pressed his face right up against the bars of the cage.
Then he turned around to flash a grin at Ben.
"Look! No spots! We can get an invisible owl for a pet!"
"Unless your spots are invisible too," Ben said.
Sid scratched his head. "Oh . . . good point."
"Watch this. I'll make Oswald visible," Waldo said.
He let out two sharp whistles.
They waited.
"I still don't see him," Sid said.
Waldo frowned and whistled again.
But again nothing happened.
Ben tried whistling next.
Still there was no sign of the owl.
"Maybe he's asleep." Waldo reached into the cage.
"Hey, Oswald, wake up!" He felt around for a moment before turning back to Ben.
"Uh-oh." He sounded worried. "I think Oswald escaped."
"What?" Ben stared at Waldo in disbelief. "Are you sure?"
"Yes!" Waldo nodded. "He's not in his cage!"
"When was the last time you saw him?" Sid asked.
"Er . . . I mean, you know what I'm trying to ask."
"I was practicing with him in the library," Waldo said.
"He was visible when I put him back in the cage.
Then I went to the cafeteria for a snack.
Maybe he escaped somehow then."
"Did you lock the cage?" Ben asked.
"I thought I did," Waldo said with a shrug.
"But maybe I forgot or the latch was loose or something."
He held his face in his hands. "This is terrible."
Ben took a deep breath, trying to stay calm.
"He's probably still inside the school building. Let's start looking for him."
"How do you look for an invisible owl?" Sid asked.
"I have no idea," Ben said.
"But we're about to figure that out. Come on, Waldo."
The wizard just stood there.
"What if he flew outside?" Waldo moaned.
"If that happened, he'll be lost forever!"
"We haven't even looked yet, Waldo," Ben said.
"And now we're losing precious time."
Waldo nodded, and the three monsters began searching, whistling and calling for the missing owl.
They searched all over the gym and then looked in some classrooms.
Next they checked the library and hallways.
"I told you this was hopeless," Waldo said.
"There's no way to find an animal who's invisible!"
Ben stayed quiet, and so did Sid.
It was hard to argue with Waldo's point.
Then Ben spotted Miss Bungle waving madly at him.
"There you are, Ben! I've been looking for you.
You were supposed to sweep the bunny rabbits' area.
You didn't show up."
"Oh, right. Sorry, Miss Bungle!" Ben replied.
"Waldo's owl . . . um, well, we had a small emergency."
"You should get going," Miss Bungle said, glancing at her watch.
"You don't want to miss the pet tricks show when it starts."
"Go ahead, Ben," Waldo said.
"Sid and I will keep looking for Oswald. You can catch up with us later."
Ben nodded. It probably wouldn't take him long to sweep the bunny rabbits' area.
After that he could rejoin the hunt for the missing owl.
A chill rippled along his spine as he remembered the owl's sharp beak and talons.
He hoped Oswald wasn't busy hunting right now!
Ben worked as fast as he could in the bunny rabbits' area.
Just as he finished sweeping, the gym went quiet.
Miss Bungle was making an announcement.
"Our pet tricks competition will start in five minutes," she said.
"Pets and trainers, please line up now.
Everyone else, please take a seat in the viewing area."
Ben hurried toward the stage.
He had to find Waldo and Sid, but he didn't want to miss Winnie and Inky's performance.
Luckily, Winnie was first in line.
Clutching Inky, she flashed Ben a nervous smile.
Then she headed for the stage, where three judges sat at a long table.
"Tell us about your pet," the first judge said.
"Well . . . " Winnie smiled, petting Inky.
"I've been training her ever since I got her for my birthday.
She's still young, but she's learned a lot of cool tricks."
She put the kitten down.
"Okay, Inky. Let's show everyone what you can do."
Winnie started with a few simple tricks, like having Inky sit and stay.
Then, to Ben's surprise, Winnie showed the judges how Inky could stand and walk on her hind legs.
"Wow!" Ben clapped hard, along with the rest of the crowd.
Winnie blushed and took a bow.
"I've saved her best trick for last," she said.
"Here, Inky." Winnie patted her left shoulder, and Inky instantly leaped up to sit there.
Then Winnie got on her broom and flew all around the gym.
Everyone clapped again.
"Winnie is super talented!" Francis said.
"I've never seen a cat do tricks before."
"Me neither!" a ghoul agreed.
"My cat always does the opposite of what I say."
Winnie landed, took another bow, and then hurried off the stage.
Miss Bungle returned to the microphone.
"Thank you, Winnie," she said.
"That was wonderful!
Our next contestant, Pixel, has a pet pig."
Ben enjoyed watching Priscilla the pig perform.
The pink pig could sit, wave—even fetch objects.
As the audience clapped, Priscilla and Pixel took a bow.
Next it was Mog's turn.
"Everyone, please give a warm welcome to Mog and his dog, Rex-Rex!"
Mog dashed onstage as Winnie sat next to Ben.
"That was awesome!" Ben said.
"I know." Winnie smiled. "Inky was so great!"
"Mog and Rex-Rex are going to do well too," Ben said.
"Mog has been working hard with him."
Onstage, Mog was working with Rex-Rex.
"Now play dead!"
Rex-Rex stood on his hind legs, clutched at his chest, and then fell over backward.
Everyone laughed.
Sid suddenly dropped down beside Ben.
"How's the hunt going?" Ben asked.
"Any luck?"
"Hunt for what?" Winnie asked.
Ben quickly explained about the missing owl.
"Wow, Oswald can make himself invisible?" Winnie said.
"That's an awesome trick!"
"It's more like a bad habit," Ben muttered.
"Waldo's still looking for Oswald," Sid said,
"but I got tired. Plus, I wanted to watch the show."
Inky had been squirming in Winnie's arms.
Spotting Sid, she jumped into his lap.
Sid laughed. "She didn't like me when she was living with us!
Now I'm her best friend."
Winnie smiled. "Cats are mysterious. That's why I like them."
Sid patted Inky's head. "We could get a cat, Ben."
"No, we can't," Ben said as Inky hissed at him.
"Cats usually hate ghosts."
"Oh!" Winnie pointed at Sid's arm.
"It looks like you are allergic to Inky, Sid."
"What?" Sid sat up to look.
And as he did, Inky sprang into the air—and hovered there!
Winnie stared up at the cat and blinked. "Inky?"
"Come down, Inky!" Sid said.
Other audience members noticed the kitten.
"Look!" Mayor Hubbletree cried. "That kitten can fly!"
"Amazing trick!" a fish monster said.
"It's not a trick!" Winnie cried. "Inky can't fly!"
Ben shot upward, trying to grab the kitten.
But Inky zoomed away.
"Inky!" Winnie cried, hopping onto her broom again.
Everyone in the audience oohed and aahed.
"They think this is part of the pet tricks show!" Ben realized.
He noticed Sid staring at his green spots.
"Are you okay, Sid?"
"Yes." Sid nodded.
"The spots are fading, but I can't understand why I got them."
Ben nodded. It did seem weird since Sid had never been allergic to Inky before.
Maybe—"Yikes!" Ben whistled loudly twice.
Poof! Oswald appeared in midair, clutching Winnie's kitten in his talons.
"Ooh!" The audience stared in amazement.
Winnie zoomed after the owl, but she couldn't keep up with his swoops and dives.
She shot back to Ben.
"Ben! Do something! That owl is going to eat Inky!"
Ben sighed with relief as the owl flew over to Waldo.
"Drop!" Waldo said, and Oswald released the kitten.
Winnie ran over to scoop up Inky.
Then she looked up and glared at Waldo.
"Oswald could have eaten her, Waldo!"
Waldo hung his head. "I'm really sorry, Winnie.
Oswald has a mind of his own.
And it's hard to train a pet who's invisible half the time."
"That's for sure!" Ben chimed in.
Winnie cuddled her kitten for a few minutes and then let out a breath.
"Inky seems fine. Thanks for saving the day, Ben.
I had no idea what was going on when she shot up in the air like that."
Ben nodded. "Sid's spots were the clue. I realized Oswald was nearby."
"I guess I'm allergic to owls too," Sid mumbled.
"Have you thought about a pet rock?" Waldo joked.
Ben rolled his eyes. "Not funny," he said.
Once things had calmed down, the pet tricks show continued.
Ben was rooting for Winnie or Mog to win.
But he enjoyed watching other pets do tricks, especially Pixel's pig and two dogs.
A ghoul hound spun a ball on its nose, like a seal.
A skeleton dog impressed everyone by fetching bones.
After all the pets had performed, the judges huddled on the stage.
Finally they signaled to Miss Bungle that they had selected a winner.
She smiled as she stood in front of the microphone.
"And the first-place winner is . . . Priscilla, the pet pig!
Second place goes to Slimy, the singing slug."
"Yes!" Waldo cried. "Jen won a prize!"
"So did Pixel," Ben said.
"Our next event will be the obedience show," Miss Bungle announced.
"It will start in about one hour.
And after that comes our final event of the weekend—the best pet competition.
While you're waiting for the next show, please visit our pet adoption booth.
We have some wonderful pets there who need great homes."
Ben and Sid looked at each other.
"I have more volunteer duties right now," Ben said.
"But we can try to check it out later."
Ben and Sid found a couple of good seats for the obedience contest.
Mrs. Hubbletree hurried onstage first, beaming as she held up her valuable rainbow gecko for everyone to see.
Ben noticed that she had gotten dressed up for the event.
She had on a colorful dress with a matching handbag.
"Rainbow geckos are very rare," the mayor's wife said proudly.
"Especially in People Place.
Bowie can change to any color—sometimes he even changes to patterns."
"Can we see?" a monster shouted from the front row.
"Sure!" Mrs. Hubbletree said proudly.
"I'll demonstrate."
She spread several colorful fabric squares on a table.
Each time Bowie was placed on a fabric square, he matched the color and pattern perfectly.
"That is pretty amazing," Ben said and others nodded.
A judge smiled politely. "Lizard behavior is quite fascinating, Mrs. Hubbletree.
But I'm afraid it's not really a demonstration of a pet's obedience."
"Oh." Mrs. Hubbletree hung her head, looking deflated. "Are you sure?"
The three judges nodded.
She hurried offstage, and one by one, other pets performed.
As he watched, Ben couldn't help thinking that none of them seemed very talented.
A goblin fish just swam around its bowl.
A spider scurried around the stage instead of following a "stay" command.
Right now a skinny cat was supposed to be heeling, but all she did was stare off into space.
The judges looked bored.
"Next," one called, propping up his head in his hand.
The show continued.
At last it was Mog's turn.
"Go, Mog!" Ben watched his friend take the stage with his two-headed dog.
Everyone clapped as Rex-Rex perfectly followed Mog's commands.
The dog sat, heeled, and lay down.
"He's helpful too," Mog said.
He demonstrated how Rex-Rex could open a latch, and find shoes.
"He can retrieve both of my shoes at once!"
The audience applauded as Mog and his dog finished performing.
"Nice job," Ben thought. It had been a strong, solid performance.
Suddenly the skinny cat's owner rushed toward the stage.
"Excuse me!" she called.
"Judges, please look at this! I got my cat to heel!"
She ran onstage, her cat closely following her.
A judge frowned. "Excuse me! You can't—"
Hiss! The cat froze as she spotted Rex-Rex.
Hissing again, she arched her back and stared at him.
A low growl started in each Rex's throat.
Then the two-headed dog barked like mad.
The cat took off, and Rex-Rex chased after her!
